Accountant.question: Tell me about a challenge you faced at work and how did you handle it?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into how the job seeker responds to difficult situations. Look for a response that shows how the applicant handled the situation and what they learned from it.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I was working on a project for a client who was very demanding. I had to work with them on a tight deadline and they kept making changes to the project scope. I had to learn how to say "no" without upsetting them. I learned that it's important to set clear expectations and communicate those expectations clearly.

Accountant.question: What is the price of Google's stock?
Accountant.overview: Accountants need to have a fundamental understanding of the stock market and how to read financial statements. This question tests whether the applicant can answer a basic finance question.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: Google's stock price is $1,000 per share. The company's market cap is $500 billion.

Accountant.question: Walk me through your CV.
Accountant.overview: A CV is a summary of the applicant's work history, education, and other qualifications. The applicant should be able to explain their work history in a clear and concise manner.
expectations: Ability to clearly and concisely summarize work history
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I've worked at three different companies over the past five years. I started out as an accounting assistant and worked my way up to senior accountant. I have a bachelor's degree in accounting from a local university.

Accountant.question: Why are you not looking at other opportunities?
Accountant.overview: This question reveals whether the applicant is truly interested in the position. The applicant should have a compelling reason for wanting to work for your company.
expectations: Understanding of the company's mission and values
Desire to work for the company
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I've been looking for a job in accounting for over a year, and I'm very excited about this opportunity. I've been following your company for a while, and I think you have a great reputation. I'm very impressed with your products and services, and I think you have a bright future ahead.

Accountant.question: What are your career goals?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's career aspirations. Look for answers that show a desire to continue to learn and grow in the accounting field.
expectations: Desire to advance in the accounting field
Desire to work in a specific industry or type of company
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I want to continue to learn more about the accounting industry and advance my career. I want to work for a large company that has a lot of opportunities for growth and advancement.

Accountant.question: Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years?
Accountant.overview: The applicant should have a clear idea of their career goals and how they plan to achieve them. Look for answers that include the applicant's long-term career goals and how they plan to achieve them.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I would like to be a CPA and would like to work my way up to a controller position within the next 5 years. I plan to take the CPA exam in the next year and will continue to learn accounting software and business processes so I can be an asset to any company I work for.

Accountant.question: How would you deal with a difficult employee?
Accountant.overview: Accountants may have to deal with difficult employees or clients. The applicant should show that they can remain professional and solve problems in a diplomatic manner.
expectations: Ability to remain calm and professional
Willingness to take responsibility for mistakes
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the other person's perspective. I would then explain my position and try to find a solution that works for both of us. If we couldn't come to an agreement, I would escalate the issue to my manager.

Accountant.question: What can you tell me about yourself?
Accountant.overview: This is a simple question that allows the applicant to share their background, skills, and interests. Look for a response that shows the applicant's personality and enthusiasm for the job.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I'm a recent graduate with a bachelor's degree in accounting. I'm very interested in tax accounting and have experience with tax preparation software. I'm also an avid runner and enjoy spending time outdoors.

Accountant.question: Tell me about a time when you had to work with a difficult personality.
Accountant.overview: This question reveals how the applicant handles difficult situations with coworkers or clients. The applicant should explain how they handled the situation and what they learned from it.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I had to work with a vendor who was very difficult to get along with. I tried to be as polite and professional as possible, but I also stood my ground when he was being unreasonable. I learned that it's important to be assertive, but not aggressive.

Accountant.question: How would you rate your MS Excel skills, on a scale of 1-10?
Accountant.overview: Accountants use spreadsheets to track and organize data, so it's important to know how proficient the job seeker is with this tool. Look for an answer that indicates the applicant has a strong understanding of Excel's features and functions.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I would rate my skills at a solid 8. I'm comfortable with the basics, but I'm still learning how to use more advanced features. I've learned a lot from watching YouTube videos and reading Excel blogs.

Accountant.question: Tell me about a time when you had to be innovative in your past position?
Accountant.overview: Accountants may need to be creative when they're working on a project or solving a problem. The applicant should describe a time when they had to think outside the box to come up with a solution.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I was working on a project for a client who was having trouble reconciling their bank statements. I noticed that the client had been using the wrong chart of accounts for their business. I was able to correct the error and reconcile the client's bank statements.

Accountant.question: What made you choose your college?
Accountant.overview: The applicant's college choice can reveal a lot about their personality. Look for answers that show the applicant's interests and how they relate to the college's offerings.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I wanted to study business and management, and my high school guidance counselor suggested I look at the University of Michigan. I liked the school's reputation for excellence in business and management, as well as its proximity to my hometown.

Accountant.question: What courses did you take in college?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's educational background and their interests. Look for answers that include technical courses related to accounting, such as business law or finance.
expectations: Business courses that relate to accounting
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I took accounting, business law, and finance courses. I also took a few computer science classes to help me learn how to use the accounting software.

Accountant.question: What do you think you can bring to the team?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's self-awareness and their understanding of their own strengths and weaknesses. Look for answers that show the applicant's ability to communicate effectively and work well with others.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I'm a team player who is willing to go above and beyond to get the job done. I'm also very detail-oriented, which helps me catch errors and inconsistencies in accounting reports.

Accountant.question: What do you do with the retained earnings at month end?
Accountant.overview: This question reveals whether the applicant has a fundamental understanding of accounting concepts. Look for answers that include the following:
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I make sure that the retained earnings account is properly reconciled to the balance sheet. I also make sure that the retained earnings account is properly classified as a balance sheet account.

Accountant.question: What experience do you have that relates to this role?

expectations: Experience that relates to the job
Experience working in a similar environment

Accountant.question: What is your favorite job?
Accountant.overview: This question allows you to gauge the job seeker's attitude toward their previous work. Look for answers that show a positive attitude and enthusiasm for the job.

Accountant.question: Why did you apply to Vivid Seats?

Willingness to learn more about the company

Accountant.question: How long have you been working in accounting?

expectations: Minimum of three years of experience
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I've been working in accounting for five years. I started as an entry-level accountant and have worked my way up to my current position.

Accountant.question: What are your strengths that make you work well within a team?

Accountant.question: How do you deal with change?
Accountant.overview: Accountants are often tasked with implementing new processes or systems to improve their department's efficiency. The applicant should be able to explain how they approach change and how they adapt to new situations.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I'm very open to change and try to see the benefits of it. I'm always looking for ways to improve our accounting processes and systems, so I welcome the opportunity to try something new.

Accountant.question: How do you learn new things?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into how the applicant learns new concepts and processes. Look for answers that show the applicant's willingness to learn new things, as well as their preferred methods for doing so.
expectations: Ability to learn on their own
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I like to read books and articles about accounting. I also like to attend conferences and seminars to learn about new accounting standards and software features. I've found that I learn best when I'm actively engaged in the learning process.

Accountant.question: How does your current employer impact you?
Accountant.overview: This question allows you to gauge the applicant's loyalty to their current employer. Look for answers that show the applicant's appreciation for the company and willingness to help them succeed.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: My current employer is a small business, so I have a lot of opportunities to help them succeed. I've been able to help them grow their business by identifying new opportunities and improving their accounting processes.

Accountant.question: Tell me about a process you have implemented.
Accountant.overview: Accountants are often responsible for implementing new processes or procedures. This question gives you insight into how the job seeker approaches this task and whether they have a strong understanding of business processes.
expectations: Ability to explain complex processes in simple terms
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I used to work at a small business that had a lot of accounting tasks that needed to be completed. I created a spreadsheet that tracked the different tasks and the status of each one. I updated it every day and sent it to the owner so he could see what was happening with his business.

Accountant.question: Why do you think you are suitable for this job?
Accountant.overview: The applicant should be able to explain why they are the best person for the job. They should be able to discuss their relevant experience and skills, as well as their passion for accounting.
expectations: Strong skills in the accounting solution
Accountant.sampleAnswer:
I have a strong background in accounting and financial management. I've worked with multiple accounting platforms and understand the challenges that businesses face when trying to manage their finances. I'm passionate about helping companies improve their financial management processes and make better business decisions.
 - Tell me about a process you have implemented.

Accountant.question: What would you do if there was a call that came in from collections that does not match the records that you see internally?
Accountant.overview: Accountants need to be able to identify when something is amiss in the accounting records. This question gives you insight into how the applicant responds to an unusual or suspicious situation.
expectations: Ability to identify unusual or suspicious patterns
Good judgment for following up on discrepancies
Willingness to ask for help when needed
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I would first try to determine if the discrepancy was a result of an error in our accounting software or if it was an actual discrepancy. If it was a software error, I would contact the vendor and ask them to fix it. If it was a discrepancy, I would look at the customer's payment history and try to determine why the payment didn't match the records. If it was a fraudulent transaction, I would report it to the appropriate authorities.

Accountant.question: What is a situation where you had conflict and how did you handle it?
Accountant.overview: This question reveals how the applicant handles conflicts and disagreements with other people. Look for a response that shows the applicant is willing to work through conflicts and reach a resolution.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I had a disagreement with my manager about how we should handle a client's request. I wanted to give the client what they wanted, but my manager was concerned about the implications for our business. We talked about our different perspectives and came up with a solution that satisfied everyone.

Accountant.question: How do you resolve conflicts?
Accountant.overview: Accountants may have to resolve conflicts between departments or employees. Look for a response that shows the job seeker's ability to remain calm and objective, while still being able to clearly communicate their position.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I try to understand both sides of the issue before I make a decision. I don't let my emotions get in the way of making the right choice for the company.

Accountant.question: Have you ever used an ERP system?
Accountant.overview: ERP systems are used by many businesses to manage their accounting functions. The applicant should have experience with the most prominent ERP systems, such as Microsoft Dynamics, SAP, Oracle, and NetSuite.
expectations: Understanding of how to use basic features
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I used QuickBooks when I worked at a small business and Microsoft Dynamics GP at larger enterprises. I'm most familiar with QuickBooks Online and helped my previous employer track and categorize their expenses and invoices.

Accountant.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's self-awareness and willingness to be honest about their own shortcomings. The applicant should be able to identify a few strengths and weaknesses that are relevant to the job.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I'm very organized and detail-oriented. I'm also very good at multitasking and working under pressure. My weakness is that I can be too detail-oriented and miss the big picture. I've been working on improving my ability to see the big picture and not get bogged down in the details.

Accountant.question: What are your strengths in accounting?
Accountant.overview: Accountants should be able to identify their strengths and weaknesses. This question allows the applicant to show their self-awareness and willingness to improve.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I'm very detail-oriented and organized. I'm also good at working with numbers and analyzing data. I'm not as familiar with accounting software, so I'm working on improving my skills in this area.

Accountant.question: What is the principle of matching?
Accountant.overview: Accountants use the matching principle to ensure that the revenues and expenses in a period are recorded in the same period. This question reveals whether the applicant understands the concept and can apply it to real-world situations.
expectations: Ability to apply accounting concepts to real-world situations
Accountant.sampleAnswer: The matching principle requires that revenues and expenses are recorded in the same period. For example, if you sell a product on December 31, you should record the revenue in that period and the cost of goods sold in the same period.

Accountant.question: What type of accounting issues have you encountered?
Accountant.overview: Accountants encounter many different accounting issues in their daily work. This question allows the applicant to show their experience with common accounting problems and how they resolved them.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I've encountered a lot of issues with reconciling accounts and tracking expenses. I've had to work with my team to resolve these issues and find ways to prevent them from happening again.

Accountant.question: Why did you choose CNA?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's reasons for applying to your company. Look for answers that show a genuine interest in the company and its products or services.
expectations: Understanding of the company's products or services
Desire to work for the company
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with CNA for many years and know that it's a great company. I'm interested in learning more about the accounting department and how I can contribute to its success.

Accountant.question: How would you handle a challenging situation with your last employer?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's ability to work through problems and find a solution. Look for a response that shows the applicant is willing to take responsibility for their actions and learn from their mistakes.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I would review the situation with my manager and try to understand what happened. I would also talk to the employee who was affected by the mistake and apologize for my role in it. I would then make sure that I understood what happened and how to prevent it from happening again.

Accountant.question: How much experience do you have in the field you are applying for?
Accountant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's experience level. Look for answers that include the number of years the job seeker has worked in the field.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I have three years of experience in accounting and two years of experience in auditing. I'm currently working as an auditor for a large corporation.

Accountant.question: How would you describe your experiences with diversity and how you handled it in a work environment?
Accountant.overview: Accountants may encounter a variety of people from different backgrounds and cultures. The applicant should be able to show how they have worked with people from different backgrounds and how they have handled any challenges that may have arisen.
expectations: Ability to work with people from different backgrounds
Willingness to learn about other cultures
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with a diverse group of people in my previous accounting jobs. I've learned to adapt my communication style to each person's personality. I've also learned how to work with people who have different values and beliefs than me.

Accountant.question: How do you handle multiple tasks?
Accountant.overview: Accountants often have to juggle multiple projects at once. This question reveals how the job seeker prioritizes their work and manages their time.
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I prioritize my work based on deadlines and the impact each task will have on the business. I use a combination of time management techniques, such as the Pomodoro technique, to keep me focused on my most important tasks.

Accountant.question: How do you handle feedback?
Accountant.overview: Accountants may need to receive feedback from their managers or clients. The applicant should be able to explain how they respond to criticism and suggestions for improvement.
expectations: Understanding of how to receive feedback
Accountant.sampleAnswer: I take feedback very seriously and use it to improve my work. I make sure that I understand the criticism before I respond, and I try to find a solution that works for everyone involved.

Accountant.question: What is your experience with Microsoft Excel?
Accountant.overview: Excel is a common tool for accountants to use to create spreadsheets and perform calculations. The applicant should be able to demonstrate their familiarity with the software and how they use it to complete tasks.
expectations: Understanding of how to use Excel in accounting processes

I also know how to use pivot tables and charts to present information in an easy-to-understand format.

Accountant.question: What are you looking for in your next job?

Accountant.question: Tell me about a time when you had different opinions on something than someone else.

Accountant.question: What is your goal?

Desire to work in a specific industry

I want to become an accounting manager at a large corporation. I want to be able to oversee multiple departments and ensure that they're all working together effectively.

Financial Advisor.question: Tell me about a time you failed.

It is a common misconception that failure is a sign of weakness, but it is actually a sign of strength. Someone who has never failed at anything has never pushed themselves to their limits and therefore has never truly experienced success.
expectations: Honest and detailed response about a failure
Explanation of what was learned from the failure
Explanation of how the failure was overcome,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I failed to meet a deadline for my previous employer. I learned that I needed to be more diligent in my work and better manage my time. I took on more tasks than I could handle and was unable to complete them all, which led to the missed deadline. I have since learned how to better manage my workload and have not had a similar issue since.

Financial Advisor.question: What are some of the markets that you can tap into to find prospects?
Financial Advisor.overview: A financial advisor must be able to find new clients and expand his network. The employer wants to know if the applicant has a plan for doing so. The response will provide insight into the applicant's knowledge of the industry and their personal drive to succeed.
expectations: Familiarity with the financial services industry
Personal connections that can be used to expand network,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
I have a wide network of friends and family that I can tap into. I also have experience in networking through my previous employment, which I hope to apply here.
 - Tell me about a time you failed.

Financial Advisor.question: How would you find a target market to start doing business with?
Financial Advisor.overview: The financial advisor position requires the candidate to develop a client base. This is a difficult task that requires a lot of time and effort. The employer wants to know how the candidate will go about finding clients and what their strategy will be.
expectations: Knowledge of current trends in the financial services industry
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I would start by reaching out to my personal connections and those of my family. I would also look to my previous employers for referrals. I would also research local businesses and organizations that might be interested in my services.

Financial Advisor.question: What makes you think you will be successful here?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a final test of the applicant's confidence in his own abilities. A successful financial advisor must be able to sell himself to clients and employers alike. The response will provide insight into how well the applicant can project his own strengths and convince others that he is capable of handling the position.
expectations: Confidence in ability to handle the position
Experience in a similar position or with similar responsibilities
Personal success stories that demonstrate ability to succeed,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have been successful in every position I have held that involves financial planning. I am confident that I will be able to continue that trend here.

Financial Advisor.question: If offered, how do you see your first 3 months working for us?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a way for the employer to gauge the applicant's interest in the position. Someone who is enthusiastic about the job will be more likely to perform well and stay with the company for a long time.
expectations: Detailed description of how they would spend their first 3 months on the job
Specific examples of how they would contribute to the company's goals
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: My first 3 months would be spent getting to know my new colleagues and clients. I would also be learning about the company's goals and objectives so that I can align my efforts with them. I would also be looking for ways to improve my own performance and expand my knowledge of the industry.

Financial Advisor.question: What are you prepared to do in the next 12-24 months?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is designed to gauge the applicant's interest in the position. A financial advisor must be willing to go above and beyond the call of duty to succeed. The employer wants to know that the applicant is willing to do whatever it takes to achieve success in the position, and this question is a good way to find out.
expectations: Commitment to furthering education in finance or related fields
Plans to build a network of clients and expand his business
Desire to take on more responsibilities in the future,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
I am prepared to do whatever it takes to succeed in this position. I will continue my education in finance and economics, build a network of clients, and take on more responsibilities as I grow into the role.
 - If offered, how do you see your first 3 months working for us?

Financial Advisor.question: What is your interest in finance?
Financial Advisor.overview: The financial services industry is a competitive one, and the employer is trying to gauge the applicant's interest in it. Someone who is not interested in finance will not be able to dedicate themselves to the position and will be less likely to succeed.
expectations: Previous experience in a finance-related position,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
Finance has always been a passion of mine. I have taken several courses in the subject and have been able to apply what I learned to my personal finances.
 - What are you prepared to do in the next 12-24 months?

Financial Advisor.question: Tell me about a time you used your creativity/resourcefulness to overcome an obstacle.
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is an attempt to gauge the applicant's ability to think outside the box. The financial advisor position is one that requires a great deal of creativity and resourcefulness. The employee must be able to find solutions to problems that may not have been encountered before, and they must be able to do so without having to rely on other people for assistance.
expectations: Experience in a job position that required creativity
Ability to explain how creativity was used in a relevant situation
Knowledge of relevant resources that can be drawn upon in a time of need,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have always been able to think outside the box when it comes to problem-solving. As a customer service representative, I had to find ways to resolve issues that were not directly covered by our policies. I would reach out to other departments or even customers themselves for help in resolving the issue.

Financial Advisor.question: What are your plans for the future?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is intended to gauge the applicant's interest in the position and their commitment to it. A candidate who is not interested in the position will not be as dedicated to the job as one who is. Someone who has plans for the future will be more likely to stay with the company for a long time, whereas someone who does not have plans will be more likely to leave.
expectations: Plans for the future that involve working in a similar position
Plans for the future that involve working in a different position
Plans for the future that involve starting a business,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
I plan to continue working in a financial advisory position for as long as I can. I am very interested in the work and have no intention of leaving it any time soon.
 - Tell me about a time you used your creativity/resourcefulness to overcome an obstacle.

Financial Advisor.question: What are your plans to grow your business?
Financial Advisor.overview: A financial advisor must be able to attract new clients to grow his business. This is a vital part of the job, and the employer will want to know how the applicant plans to accomplish it. The response will also give insight into how the applicant sees his role in the company.
expectations: Plans to expand the business through referrals
Plans to expand the business through networking
Plans to expand the business through social media
Plans to expand the business through other methods,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I plan to build my clientele by networking with other professionals in my field. I will also use social media to reach out to potential clients and build my brand.

Financial Advisor.question: What licenses do you currently hold?
Financial Advisor.overview: A financial advisor must be licensed to operate in the field. The employer is looking for someone who has already taken the initiative to obtain the required license. It is a sign of dedication to the profession and a sign that the applicant is willing to go above and beyond to succeed in the position.
expectations: Licenses obtained from relevant state or federal agencies
Specifics about how the license will be useful on the job
Details about how the license was obtained,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I am currently licensed as a financial advisor in the state of California. I have been working toward obtaining my Series 7 and Series 63 licenses, which I hope to have completed by the time I begin employment.

Financial Advisor.question: What are you most proud of?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a good way to gauge the applicant's personality. A financial advisor is responsible for handling sensitive information, so it is essential that they be trustworthy and reliable. The response will provide insight into how the applicant feels about his own character and whether he has the ability to be honest and forthright with clients.
expectations: Experience in a position that requires trustworthiness
Personal success stories that reflect integrity,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I am most proud of my ability to maintain trust with my clients. I have never had a client complaint or issue with my integrity, and I hope to continue that trend here.

Financial Advisor.question: How would you build a client book?
Financial Advisor.overview: The financial advisor position is a sales position, and the applicant must be able to demonstrate an ability to sell. The employer wants to know how they will be able to attract new clients and build a network of returning clients.
expectations: Experience in sales or customer service
Knowledge of marketing strategies or other methods of attracting new clients
Ability to describe how they will build a client book,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I would begin by building a network of contacts through my personal network and the professional connections I have made in the past. I would then use those contacts to establish a strong presence in the community.

Financial Advisor.question: Where do you want to open your business?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a test of the applicant's business acumen. Financial advisors are responsible for managing their own businesses, and the employer wants to know if the applicant has a good sense of where to begin. The response will indicate whether they have a realistic understanding of the business world and how they plan to use it to their advantage.
expectations: Knowledge of local business laws and regulations
Personal connections with potential business partners or clients,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have been looking into opening my own financial advisory firm in the city. I have already spoken with several potential clients and partners, and I am confident that I can make a name for myself in this area.

Financial Advisor.question: Have you ever had a conflict with your boss and how did you resolve the issue?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work with others and resolve conflicts. As a financial advisor, the employee will be working with clients and coworkers on a regular basis. The ability to resolve conflicts in a productive manner is vital to the job.
expectations: Experience in resolving conflicts with coworkers
Ability to explain how the conflict was resolved and what was learned from it
Previous success in resolving conflicts with superiors,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have had a few conflicts with my boss in the past, but I was able to resolve them by approaching them with a positive attitude and open mind. I learned that I could not always expect my boss to see things from my perspective, but that it was important to present my case in a way that would allow him to understand.

Financial Advisor.question: How will you find new clients if you worked here?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a test of the applicant's marketing skills. A financial advisor is responsible for bringing in new clients, and the employer wants to know how they will go about doing so. The response will provide insight into the applicant's ability to think outside the box and come up with creative ways to expand his network.
expectations: Experience in a job position that required marketing skills
Smooth-flowing response that reflects effective soft skills
Genuine excitement about heavy communication on the job,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I would use my experience as a financial advisor to build a strong network of returning and trusting clients. I would also use my expertise in investment strategies to help clients reach their financial goals.

Financial Advisor.question: How do you handle pressure?
Financial Advisor.overview: The financial services industry is a high-pressure field. The job of a financial advisor is to be an expert in a field that is constantly changing and evolving. This requires a high level of adaptability and the ability to work under pressure.
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have been able to handle pressure in the past by remaining calm and collected. I have also been able to work well under pressure by remaining focused on the task at hand.

Financial Advisor.question: How would you generate a book of business?
Financial Advisor.overview: A financial advisor is responsible for attracting new clients to his business. This is a crucial part of the job, and it is important to know how the candidate plans to go about it. The response will provide insight into the applicant's marketing and sales skills, which are crucial to the position.
expectations: Experience in a position that required generating new business
Proven success in generating new business through marketing or sales
Knowledge of specific marketing strategies that apply to financial advisors,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I would begin by leveraging my network of contacts and my previous experience as a financial advisor. I would then use my knowledge of the industry to identify potential clients and approach them with my services.

Financial Advisor.question: What is a time when you made an unpopular decision?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a test of the applicant's integrity. A financial advisor is responsible for making decisions that will affect the financial future of his clients. The decisions must be made with the utmost honesty and integrity, and a candidate who is willing to admit to unpopular decisions is more likely to be trustworthy than one who is not.
expectations: Experience in a position that required unpopular decisions
Confidence in ability to make unpopular decisions
Ability to explain unpopular decision in a way that does not reflect negatively on the applicant,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I had to make an unpopular decision as a financial advisor with my previous employer. I had to tell a client that his investment strategy was not working out and that he would have to consider other options. I was able to do so in a way that did not reflect badly on me or the company.

Financial Advisor.question: Do you think you can go door to door and sell?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a test of the applicant's interest in sales and their ability to sell themselves. It is a common misconception that financial advisors are not required to sell their services. In reality, financial advisors are expected to bring in new clients and expand their network. The applicant must be able to demonstrate that he is capable of doing so.
expectations: Experience in sales or customer service
Personal interest in sales or marketing,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have always been interested in sales and marketing. I have been successful in those areas in the past, and I am confident that I can replicate that success here.

Financial Advisor.question: What do you think will be the most challenging part of this job?
Financial Advisor.overview: The most challenging part of the job will be the ability to work with a wide range of people. A financial advisor must be able to work with a variety of clients, each with their own unique financial goals and needs. The candidate must be able to adapt to the needs of each client, which will require a certain degree of flexibility.
expectations: Ability to handle a variety of people
Experience in customer service or human resources
Personal interest in learning about different types of people,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I believe that the most challenging part of the job will be the ability to work with a wide range of people. I have experience in customer service and human resources, so I am well-versed in adapting to the needs of different types of people.

Financial Advisor.question: Why do you want to be in sales?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is designed to get to the heart of the applicant's interest in the position. Someone who is genuinely excited about the prospect of selling will be more likely to succeed in the position than someone who is not.
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have always been interested in sales and marketing. I have had the opportunity to work in both fields and have enjoyed my time in them. I feel that I have a natural talent for sales and would like to put that talent to use here.

Financial Advisor.question: How do you feel about selling insurance?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a test of the applicant's interest in the position. Selling insurance is a vital part of the job, and the employer wants to know if they are enthusiastic about it. The applicant's response will also give the employer insight into their personality and how they will interact with clients.
expectations: Confidence in ability to sell insurance
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I am very excited about selling insurance. I have always been a natural salesman, and I believe that I can use my skills to help clients find the best coverage for their needs.

Financial Advisor.question: What kind of environment do you enjoy working in?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a way for the employer to gauge the applicant's personality. Someone who is comfortable in a fast-paced environment will be more likely to succeed in a job that requires constant interaction with clients. Someone who prefers a more relaxed environment will be more at ease in a position that involves less frequent client contact.
expectations: A job position that requires constant interaction with clients
A job position that requires less frequent client contact
A job position that requires working alone,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I enjoy working in a fast-paced environment where I am constantly interacting with clients. I find it rewarding to help people achieve their financial goals and watch them grow as individuals.

Financial Advisor.question: What makes you think that you can succeed in this role?
Financial Advisor.overview: The employer wants to know if the applicant has the confidence and drive to succeed in the position. They want to know that they are not hiring someone who will be complacent with their success and not try to improve.
expectations: Personal experience in a similar position
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have been successful in my previous role as a financial advisor. I am confident that I can replicate that success here.

Financial Advisor.question: Why do you want to be a software engineer?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is meant to gauge the applicant's interest in the job. The employer is looking for someone who is passionate about the position and will be able to perform well. Someone who has a genuine interest in the field will be more likely to succeed than someone who is only applying because of the money or the title.
expectations: Knowledge of relevant software engineering principles
Interest in the field that goes beyond monetary gain,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have always been interested in computer science and have been working on my own programming projects for years. I am eager to apply my knowledge of software engineering in a professional setting and hope to make a positive contribution to the company.

Financial Advisor.question: What is an example of a goal you didn't achieve and what did you learn from it?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is an opportunity for the applicant to demonstrate their ability to learn from mistakes and grow from them. It is important for a financial advisor to be able to take a step back and assess his own performance, and this question gives the applicant a chance to prove that he can.
expectations: Explanation of how the experience has helped the applicant grow
Ability to reflect on mistakes without dwelling on them
Ability to admit fault without making excuses,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I didn't achieve my goal of becoming a financial advisor with my previous employer. I learned that I needed to work on my communication skills in order to be more effective in my role.

Financial Advisor.question: What is a 12b-1 fee on mutual fund?
Financial Advisor.overview: A 12b-1 fee is a charge on mutual funds that goes to the fund company, not the investor. The fee is charged for distribution and marketing of the fund.
expectations: Knowledge of how the fee is charged
Knowledge of how the fee is used,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
A 12b-1 fee is a charge on mutual funds that goes to the fund company, not the investor. The fee is charged for distribution and marketing of the fund.
 - What is an example of a goal you didn't achieve and what did you learn from it?

Financial Advisor.question: What kind of environment do you thrive best in?
Financial Advisor.overview: A financial advisor is responsible for maintaining a positive relationship with clients. The best way to do that is to create a comfortable environment for them. A candidate who is able to thrive in a variety of environments will be able to adapt to the needs of clients and make them feel at ease.
expectations: Experience in a variety of work environments
Ability to explain how they can adapt to different work environments
Personal interest in the work environment,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
I have had experience in a variety of work environments, from retail to investment banking. I am comfortable in all of them and can easily adjust my style to fit the needs of clients.
 - What is a 12b-1 fee on mutual fund?

Financial Advisor.question: What made you choose Equitable?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is intended to gauge the applicant's interest in the company. Someone who is genuinely interested in working for Equitable will be able to explain why they are interested and how their personal goals align with the company's mission.
expectations: Familiarity with the company's history and reputation
Personal connection to the company's mission,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have been a customer of Equitable for years, and I have always been impressed by your commitment to customer service. I am excited to be able to contribute to that commitment as a financial advisor.

Financial Advisor.question: Do you have a base to start making sales?
Financial Advisor.overview: A financial advisor is a salesperson in the sense that he must be able to attract clients and convince them to trust him with their finances. A candidate who has a network of contacts that he can leverage to gain new clients will be more successful than one who does not.
expectations: Personal connections that can be used as a starting point for sales
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have a network of contacts that I can leverage to gain new clients. I have already begun to build my network by reaching out to friends and family members, and I hope to expand it further as I begin my career here.

Financial Advisor.question: How do you deal with rejection?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a test of the applicant's ability to handle rejection. It is a common occurrence for a financial advisor to have to turn down a client or prospective client. The applicant must be able to explain how he deals with rejection and how he will be able to handle it professionally in the workplace.
expectations: Experience with rejection in previous jobs
Ability to accept rejection as part of the job
Confidence in ability to handle rejection,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have had to deal with rejection in my previous jobs as a financial advisor. I learned that it is important to maintain a professional attitude and not let it affect my work. I am confident that I can handle any rejection that comes my way in this position.

Financial Advisor.question: How do you measure your own success?
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a good indicator of the applicant's work ethic. A financial advisor is responsible for the success of his clients, and that responsibility will not be fulfilled without a great deal of hard work. The response will show how the applicant defines success and how he measures it in his own life.
expectations: Ability to set and achieve goals
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I measure my success by the satisfaction of my clients. I want to see them grow financially and reach their goals, and I take pride in knowing that I played a part in that process.

Financial Advisor.question: Tell me how you establish yourself as an expert in your field.
Financial Advisor.overview: Financial advisors are in a position to build their own reputations and brands. They can do so by offering useful advice and services to clients, but they must also be able to promote themselves effectively. This question examines the applicant's ability to market themselves and their services, which is a vital skill for any financial advisor.
expectations: Personal experience with successful marketing strategies
Previous success in building a brand or reputation,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer: I have always been a strong believer in the importance of branding myself as an expert in my field. I have built my own website and social media presence to help me reach out to clients and establish myself as a trustworthy source of information.

Financial Advisor.question: Tell me about a time you had to overcome a challenge in order to reach a goal.
Financial Advisor.overview: This question is a classic interview question that gets to the heart of the applicant's character. It is a test of their resilience and determination. The response will indicate how well they are able to overcome obstacles and maintain a positive attitude in the face of adversity.
expectations: Experience overcoming a challenge in the past
Ability to explain how they overcame it
Evidence of a positive attitude and perseverance,
Financial Advisor.sampleAnswer:
I had to overcome a challenge in my previous job as a financial advisor. I was tasked with building a new client base, but I found myself struggling to attract new clients. I overcame this challenge by taking initiative and reaching out to people I knew personally.
 - Tell me how you establish yourself as an expert in your field.

Head Cashier.question: What have you done to provide great customer service?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to have a high level of customer service skills and be able to provide excellent customer service to all customers. They need to be able to address any concerns or complaints that customers may have and resolve them in a timely manner.
expectations: Knowledge of how to provide great customer service
Confidence in their own problem-solving abilities,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I provided great customer service by greeting customers as they entered the store and asking them if they needed any assistance. I was friendly and helpful, and I answered any questions they had about the products in the store. I also used my interpersonal skills to resolve any issues that customers had with the products they purchased.

Head Cashier.question: Tell me about a time when you had to pay attention to detail.
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to be able to pay attention to detail and be able to follow the store's procedures for completing tasks. They need to be able to identify errors and correct them before they lead to larger problems.
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I paid attention to detail when I was a cashier and when I was a head cashier. I had to ensure that all cashiers were following the procedures for completing tasks. I had to identify errors and correct them before they led to larger problems. I also had to ensure that all cashiers were following the procedures for completing tasks.

Head Cashier.question: How have you gone above and beyond to show great customer service?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier is responsible for ensuring that all customers are satisfied with their shopping experience. They need to be able to identify the needs of each customer and offer them assistance. They should be able to resolve any customer issues and ensure that the customer leaves the store satisfied.
expectations: High level of customer service skills
Knowledge of how to offer assistance to customers,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I went above and beyond to show great customer service by greeting customers as they entered the store and asking if they needed assistance. I offered suggestions for products that would meet their needs and helped them find the products they were looking for. I resolved any customer issues by listening carefully to their concerns and offering solutions. I ensured that each customer left the store satisfied with their shopping experience.

Head Cashier.question: Tell me about a time when you had to handle a difficult situation between a customer/co-worker.
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier is responsible for handling difficult situations between customers and co-workers. They need to be able to resolve conflicts and keep the peace in the store.
expectations: Confidence in their own problem-solving abilities
High level of customer service skills,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I had to handle a difficult situation between a customer and a cashier. The customer was upset because the cashier had made a mistake with their transaction. I stepped in and explained that the cashier had made an honest mistake and that the customer needed to be more understanding. I helped the customer understand that mistakes happen and that they should be more patient with the cashier.

Head Cashier.question: What was the most difficult situation you had to face in your work and how did you handle it?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to have experience with handling difficult situations and be able to resolve them quickly. They need to be able to handle customer complaints and address their concerns in a professional manner.
expectations: Confidence in taking the lead when necessary
Willingness to take the initiative and resolve problems,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I had a customer return a product that was past its expiration date. I explained the store policy on returns and issued a refund for the product. The customer became irate and started yelling at me. I remained calm and explained the store policy again. I asked the customer to leave the store if they were unhappy with the store's policies.

Head Cashier.question: What are your career goals?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to have a clear idea of where they want to go in their career and how they plan to get there. They should be able to articulate their goals and explain how they will achieve them.
expectations: Willingness to take on new challenges
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: My goal is to become a store manager. I plan to achieve this by working hard and taking on new challenges. I will work my way up the ladder by gaining experience in the retail industry and learning from my superiors. I will continue to learn new skills and take advantage of opportunities for growth.

Head Cashier.question: What would you do if you had a cashier who needed change, an angry customer and a register that broke down all at the same time?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to be able to handle any situation that arises and be able to resolve it quickly and efficiently. They need to be able to prioritize the issues at hand and solve them in the most efficient manner possible.
expectations: Confidence in their own problem-solving abilities,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I would address the customer's concerns first and apologize for the inconvenience. I would then ask the cashier for change and assist them with completing the transaction. I would then address the register issue and call for maintenance. I would complete the end-of-shift paperwork and reconcile the register till to a total of $75 for the next shift.

Head Cashier.question: How do you handle angry people?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier is responsible for handling angry customers and ensuring that they are satisfied with their shopping experience. They need to be able to resolve issues quickly and effectively and maintain a high level of customer service.
expectations: Confidence in their own problem-solving abilities
High level of customer service skills,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I took the time to listen to the customer's concerns and offered solutions that would satisfy them. I was able to resolve the issue quickly and efficiently and make the customer happy.

Head Cashier.question: What is your availability?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to be available to work all shifts and be able to work overtime when necessary. They need to be able to work weekends and holidays and be willing to travel with the store manager if necessary.
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I am available to work any shift that is assigned. I am willing to work overtime when necessary and am available to travel with the store manager on business trips.

Head Cashier.question: What do you understand by customer service?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to have a good understanding of the importance of customer service and how it can affect the success of the retail store. They need to be able to provide excellent customer service and be able to handle any customer complaints or concerns.
expectations: Understanding of the importance of customer service
Confidence in their ability to provide excellent customer service
Ability to handle customer complaints and concerns,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: Customer service is the most important aspect of a retail store because it determines whether or not customers return to the store. I provided excellent customer service by greeting customers as they entered the store and asking them if they needed assistance. I helped customers find items on the shelves and answered any questions they had about products. I also assisted customers with checking out and completed all necessary paperwork for refunds.

Head Cashier.question: What would you do above and beyond for a customer?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier should always go above and beyond for customers. They need to be able to offer the best customer service and ensure that the customer is satisfied with their experience at the store.
expectations: Ability to provide excellent customer service
Willingness to go above and beyond for customers
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I always went above and beyond for customers. I greeted them with a smile and asked how they were doing. I offered them assistance with their shopping needs and made sure they were satisfied with their experience at the store. I made sure they had a pleasant shopping experience by offering them assistance with their shopping needs and making sure they were satisfied with their experience at the store.

Head Cashier.question: How would you handle a situation where the customer is looking for a product that we do not have in stock?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier should be able to handle customer inquiries and complaints. They need to be able to handle these situations with a high level of professionalism and tact.
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I would apologize to the customer for the inconvenience and offer them a substitute product. If the customer was not satisfied with the substitute, I would offer them a refund or a rain check for the product.

Head Cashier.question: What is a time when you needed to be both accurate and fast?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to be able to perform all duties quickly and accurately. They need to be able to complete all tasks in a timely manner, while still maintaining high levels of accuracy.
expectations: Ability to work accurately under pressure,
Head Cashier.sampleAnswer: I needed to be both accurate and fast when I was a head cashier. I had to process transactions quickly and accurately to ensure that the store didn't lose any sales. I was responsible for completing the end-of-shift paperwork and balancing the till to $75 for the next shift. I also needed to complete daily expense reports and reconcile sales totals for the day.

Head Cashier.question: How will you handle an angry customer?
Head Cashier.overview: A head cashier needs to be able to handle angry customers and resolve their issues. They need to be able to listen to the customer's concerns and address them in a professional manner.
expectations: Ability to listen to customer concerns
High level of customer service skills

Administrator.overview: An administrator must be a lifelong learner, so you want to know his or her ideal learning environment. Is it a classroom, a conference, a book or a mentor? What is the best way for this person to learn?
expectations: A desire to learn and grow
Willingness to seek out new information and experiences
A willingness to take on new challenges
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I like to learn by doing. I've found that the best way for me to learn is by taking on new responsibilities and projects.

Administrator.question: Tell me about your greatest failure.

A good administrator will be able to take a negative experience and turn it into a positive lesson. He or she will also be able to reflect on the failure and explain how he or she would handle it differently today.
expectations: Willingness to self-assess and address inefficiencies
Commitment to self-improvement and professional excellence
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I once made a mistake in a report that cost my company thousands of dollars. I was able to identify the problem and correct it before the client noticed, but I learned from the experience and now double-check all my work.

Administrator.question: When are you available?
Administrator.overview: An administrator's time is valuable, and you want to know how they spend it. You want to know if they're available to you when you need them and if they're willing to work long hours when necessary.
expectations: Commitment to work overtime when necessary

Administrator.question: What do you think makes you suitable for this position?
Administrator.overview: The best administrators are self-aware and honest about their strengths and weaknesses. They know what they're good at and what they need to work on. They also know how their skills and experience can benefit a company.
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I think my experience as a manager and my ability to work well with others makes me a good fit for this position.

Administrator.question: What experience do you have with organizing meetings and events?
Administrator.overview: An administrator must be able to not only organize but also facilitate meetings and events. This includes not only setting up the logistics but also managing the flow of information and ideas, keeping the meeting on track and on time, and ensuring that everyone is heard and that decisions are made.
expectations: Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I've organized a variety of meetings, including weekly staff meetings, quarterly departmental meetings and annual conferences. I've been able to keep these events on schedule while ensuring that all attendees have been heard.

Administrator.question: Why did you choose to attend Cy-Fair?
Administrator.overview: You want to know that your administrator is a Cy-Fair alumnus because it shows that he or she has a strong sense of loyalty and pride in the institution. Moreover, it demonstrates that he or she has a strong sense of community and is willing to give back to the community in which he or she was raised.
expectations: A sense of loyalty and pride in the institution
A sense of community and a willingness to give back to the community
A desire to be an example for other students
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I chose Cy-Fair because I wanted to be a part of a great school with a strong reputation. I also wanted to be able to stay close to home.

Administrator.question: What is a time you disagreed with your manager or co-worker?
Administrator.overview: An administrator must be able to stand up for his or her own ideas and opinions. You want to know your administrator is able to express his or her thoughts and ideas in a professional manner.
expectations: Ability to express thoughts and ideas clearly and confidently
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I once disagreed with a co-worker about how to handle a customer complaint. I was able to explain my point of view in a professional manner and we were able to come to a mutual agreement.

Administrator.question: What are your goals for this position?
Administrator.overview: An administrator's goals are always tied to the company's goals. You want to know your administrator is committed to the company's success and will work toward that end.
expectations: Willingness to work toward that end
Administrator.sampleAnswer: I want to help this company succeed by ensuring all administrative duties are carried out effectively and efficiently.

Clerk.question: How do you handle stress?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are responsible for completing a variety of tasks in a fast-paced environment. The right candidate will remain calm and collected when the workday becomes stressful. They will not let stress affect their work performance and will complete tasks in a timely manner.
expectations: Ability to remain calm and focused in stressful situations
Completion of tasks in a timely manner
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I handle stress by remaining calm and focused on the task at hand. I don't let stress affect my work performance. I complete tasks in a timely manner.

Clerk.question: Do you have a car?
Clerk.overview: A car is a necessity for most office clerks. They must travel to and from work and may need to visit clients, vendors and other business partners. A candidate that doesn't have a car may not be able to travel to these locations.
expectations: Ability to travel to and from work
Ability to travel to client, vendor and other business partner locations
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I own a car and have no problem driving to work or visiting clients, vendors or other business partners.

Clerk.question: What would you do if a family of four is waiting to be attended and you have a phone call on hold, an incoming call and the nurse needs your assistance?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are the first point of contact for customers and clients. They are responsible for greeting customers, answering questions and providing assistance. The candidate's answer will indicate their level of customer service, how they prioritize tasks and how they handle stressful situations.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I would take the call on hold and then attend to the family of four. I would apologize to the caller and let them know that I would be with them shortly. I would then attend to the family of four and help them with their questions.

Clerk.question: What makes you stand out from the other candidates?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are a dime a dozen. You want to hire someone that stands out from the crowd. The candidate should possess the skills and attributes that make them unique and better than other candidates. They should be able to explain why they are the best candidate for the job.
expectations: Skills and attributes that make them stand out
Knowledge of why they are the best candidate
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I have experience in multiple industries as a clerk, which gives me a broader understanding of information systems, standards and data processing. I have experience with IT protocol and standard practices. I have also worked with multiple software programs, such as Microsoft Office and Google Docs.

Clerk.question: What is your work experience?
Clerk.overview: Clerks work in a variety of industries and have a variety of job duties. The candidate's work experience will help you determine if they possess the skills and knowledge to perform the job duties you require. The candidate's work experience will also help you determine if they are a good fit for your company's culture.
expectations: Work experience in a variety of clerical positions
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I have worked in the medical, legal and marketing industries as a clerk. I have performed data entry, word processing and document creation.

Clerk.question: Why do you want to work for us?
Clerk.overview: A candidate that wants to work for you is more likely to be a good fit for your company. They are motivated and have a desire to work for your company. They are interested in the job and want to work for your company. They are excited about the opportunity and want to work for you.
expectations: Desire to work for the company
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I am interested in working for your company because I have heard great things about it. I want to be a part of a successful team.

Clerk.question: What's your favorite song?
Clerk.overview: This question is a fun way to learn about the candidate's personality and interests. It's a great icebreaker question to start off the interview.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: My favorite song is "I'm Yours" by Jason Mraz.

Clerk.question: What was your previous job?
Clerk.overview: The candidate's previous job will give you an idea of their work history and what they did in their previous job. Their previous job will also give you an idea of their experience level.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I was a clerk in a medical office.

Clerk.question: How do you prepare for confrontation?
Clerk.overview: Confrontation is a part of the job for clerks. They must deal with angry customers, business partners and visitors on a daily basis. The candidate's answer will reveal how they handle confrontations. A candidate that is well-prepared for confrontation is more likely to remain calm and handle the situation in a professional manner. They are more likely to have a higher success rate in dealing with confrontations.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I've had to deal with angry customers and business partners in the past. I remain calm and handle the situation professionally.

Clerk.question: Where do you see yourself in the next five years?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are in high demand and are expected to grow in numbers. The job outlook is positive for the next five years. The candidate's answer will indicate their career goals and how they see themselves growing in the field. If they have a plan to advance their career, they will be more motivated to work harder and advance their skills.
expectations: Desire to grow in the field
Clerk.sampleAnswer: In the next five years, I see myself as a manager of a team of clerks.

Clerk.question: What kind of problems do you like to work on?
Clerk.overview: Clerks work on a variety of problems. They are problem solvers and enjoy challenges. The candidate's answer will indicate how they handle problems and what they do to solve them. The results of their problem-solving skills will be defined by their ability to solve problems quickly and efficiently.
expectations: Ability to work on multiple problems at once
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I like to work on problems that require me to think outside the box. I like to solve problems that are unique and have never been solved before.

Clerk.question: What would you do if a customer asked you to do something that is not in your job description?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are the first point of contact for customers and business partners. They are the first to answer questions and provide information. They must be able to handle customer requests and provide solutions to problems that arise. The candidate's answer will indicate how they handle situations outside of their job description. They will also show how they handle pressure and stress in a professional manner.
expectations: Ability to think on the spot and provide solutions
Clerk.sampleAnswer: If a customer asked me to do something outside of my job description, I would ask my office manager for clarification. I would then explain the request to the customer and offer a solution.

Clerk.question: What is your experience in customer service?
Clerk.overview: Customer service skills are essential in a clerical position. Clerks work with customers on a daily basis. They must be friendly and courteous to customers and business partners. They must be able to handle customer complaints and resolve issues. The candidate's experience in customer service will determine their ability to deal with customers and business partners.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I have experience in customer service as a cashier at a retail store. I was responsible for greeting customers, answering questions about products and assisting customers with purchases.

Clerk.question: What is your availability?
Clerk.overview: Availability is vital to the success of a clerk. They must be available to work during regular business hours. If they are unavailable for a period of time, they must notify the office manager. The candidate's availability will determine their work schedule and how much time they can dedicate to the company.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I am available to work Monday through Friday from 8:00am to 5:00pm.

Clerk.question: Tell me about a time when you had to address an unexpected problem and how did you solve it?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are responsible for addressing issues that arise in the office. They must be able to solve problems and find solutions for unexpected issues. A candidate that can solve problems with ease will be more valuable to your company. They will be able to resolve issues quickly and efficiently.
expectations: Ability to address issues quickly and efficiently
Clerk.sampleAnswer: When I worked as a clerk, I was responsible for addressing any issues that arose in the office. If a printer ran out of paper, I would find a way to get more paper. If a computer crashed, I would troubleshoot the problem and fix it.

Clerk.question: What is your favorite movie?
Clerk.overview: A candidate's favorite movie can reveal a lot about their personality. It can also help you determine if they are a good fit for your company. A candidate that enjoys comedies is more likely to be a fun person to work with. A candidate that enjoys action movies is more likely to be a thrill-seeker. A candidate that enjoys horror movies is more likely to be a risk-taker.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: My favorite movie is "The Shawshank Redemption".

Clerk.question: What are your preferred working hours?
Clerk.overview: Clerks work in a variety of office settings. Some work in a standard nine-to-five schedule, while others work during the evening or on weekends. The candidate's preferred working hours will help you determine if they are available to work your business hours.
expectations: Availability to work your business hours
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I prefer to work the standard nine-to-five schedule. I can be available to work your business hours.

Clerk.question: What do you like to do in your free time?
Clerk.overview: The candidate's answer will show you how they spend their free time. If they enjoy reading, they may be a good candidate for a clerical position that requires a lot of reading. If they enjoy sports, they may be a good candidate for a clerical position that requires a lot of physical activity.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: In my free time, I enjoy reading and spending time with my family.

Clerk.question: What kind of experience do you have?
Clerk.overview: Clerks perform a variety of tasks in an office setting. They are responsible for completing a variety of clerical duties. The candidate's experience will help you determine their proficiency and skill level. The more experience they have, the more proficient they are at their job.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I have worked as a clerk for the last five years in an office setting. I have experience in a variety of clerical duties, including data entry, document creation and processing.

Clerk.question: What is the best thing you can do as part of a team?
Clerk.overview: Teamwork is vital to the success of any business. Clerks work in teams to complete daily tasks. The candidate's answer will indicate their ability to work with others and their willingness to cooperate. A candidate that is a team player will be more likely to work well with other employees and not cause problems in the workplace.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I'm a team player and I'm always willing to help out my coworkers when they need assistance.

Clerk.question: If a customer asked where a certain product in store was, and I was cleaning up a spill, what would you do?
Clerk.overview: Clerks are responsible for assisting customers and providing them with information. They must be able to answer questions about products and services. The candidate's answer indicates that they are a people person who values customer service. They are willing to help customers and are not afraid to get their hands dirty.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: If a customer asked me where a product was, I would direct them to the sales associate who could assist them with their questions.

Clerk.question: What do you know about our company?
Clerk.overview: A candidate that knows about your company and its products or services is more likely to be a good fit for the position. They will have a better understanding of the company's goals, mission and vision. They will also be able to relate to your company's culture and values.

Familiarity with the company's goals, mission and vision
Understanding of the company's culture and values
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I know that your company is a leader in the industry. I have read about your products and services in the news.

The candidate's answer will indicate their knowledge of the program and their ability to use it to create spreadsheets.

Clerk.question: Why should we hire you?
Clerk.overview: The hiring manager wants to know why you are the best candidate for the job. You want to highlight your skills and abilities that are most relevant to the position. You should also explain how you can contribute to the company's success.

How you can contribute to the company's success
Why you are the best candidate for the job

I am detail-oriented and have a keen eye for mistakes. I am organized and multitask well in a fast-paced environment. I am a people person who values high-quality customer service and wants to serve customers better.

Clerk.question: What is your experience in this field?
Clerk.overview: Clerks work in a variety of fields. They perform clerical duties in offices, hospitals, schools, retail stores and other businesses. The candidate's experience in your industry will help you determine if they have the skills and knowledge to perform the job duties required.
expectations: Skills and knowledge to perform job duties

Clerk.question: What is the most important part of a clerk's job?
Clerk.overview: Clerks perform a variety of tasks in an office. The most important part of their job is to provide excellent customer service. They must be friendly and helpful to all customers, visitors and business partners. They must be able to communicate clearly and effectively with customers. Clerks must be able to answer questions and solve problems for customers.
Clerk.sampleAnswer: The most important part of a clerk's job is providing excellent customer service.

Clerk.question: What software applications are you familiar with?
Clerk.overview: Clerks use a variety of software applications to complete their daily tasks. They are familiar with the most common programs, such as Microsoft Office and Google Docs. The candidate's experience with these programs will determine their efficiency and speed when completing tasks.
expectations: Familiarity with a variety of software applications
Experience with Microsoft Office and Google Docs
Efficiency and speed when completing tasks
Clerk.sampleAnswer: I've used Microsoft Office and Google Docs in my previous clerical jobs. I'm familiar with the programs and can use them efficiently.

Clerk.question: Tell us about a time when you had to be flexible?
Clerk.overview: Clerks work in a variety of office settings and must adjust to the demands of each environment. They must be flexible and willing to change their work habits to fit the needs of the office. A candidate that can adjust to changes in the workplace is more likely to succeed in your company.

Clerk.question: What experience do you have that would be valuable for us?
Clerk.overview: Clerks perform a variety of tasks that are similar in all industries. A candidate with vast clerical experience in multiple industries could possess specialized skills and additional certifications in these fields.
expectations: Experience in multiple industries as a clerk
Broader understanding of information systems, standards and data processing
Familiarity with IT protocol and standard
