Assistant Store Manager.question: How many years of leadership experience do you have?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Assistant store managers are leaders, so a candidate should have demonstrable experience leading others. The number of years of experience is less important than the types of experiences and the results achieved.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I've been a leader in my church youth group for three years and in my college's student government for two. I've also led volunteer efforts for local charities.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What was your biggest failure?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to learn from mistakes and not repeat them. A candidate should be able to discuss a failure in a way that demonstrates he or she has learned from it and can apply that knowledge to future situations.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I once lost a customer's order. I was able to quickly find the order and deliver it, but I didn't do so until the customer had already left. I learned that I need to be more attentive and proactive in such situations.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you build relationships with your employees?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A good assistant store manager is a good leader, and a good leader knows how to build relationships with his or her team members. A candidate should be able to identify the strengths of each team member and how to best utilize those strengths. He or she should also be able to identify each team member's weaknesses and help them improve.
expectations: Ability to identify team member strengths and weaknesses
Ability to utilize strengths and help improve weaknesses
Ability to delegate tasks based on strengths
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I know that each of my employees has unique talents that I can use to help them succeed. I also know that each employee has areas they need to improve on. I use their talents to help them succeed and use their weaknesses as opportunities for improvement.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time you had a conflict with your co-worker and how was it handled?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate's ability to work well with others is a key trait of an assistant store manager. A candidate should be able to describe a situation in which he or she had a conflict with a co-worker and how it was resolved.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Willingness to admit fault and apologize
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I had a conflict with a co-worker over who would be responsible for a particular task. We both wanted to do it, but we couldn't agree on who should do it. We talked it over and decided that we'd each do half of the task, which worked out fine.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you have shown integrity.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to demonstrate his or her integrity in a variety of ways, including through personal example and professional experience. A candidate should be able to discuss a time when he or she demonstrated integrity in a professional setting and how it positively impacted the company, customers, co-workers and/or other stakeholders.
expectations: Ability to discuss examples of integrity in a professional setting
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been honest with my customers and co-workers. I've never tried to sell them something they don't need or want. I've also never taken advantage of a customer's ignorance or lack of knowledge about a product.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What are you going to do for us if we hire you?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: The candidate should be able to clearly articulate what he or she will do to help the company succeed. The candidate should be able to clearly articulate what he or she will do to help the company succeed.
expectations: Willingness to be held accountable for results
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'll work hard to ensure the store is well-stocked and well-maintained, and that our customers are satisfied. I'll also work with my team to ensure they're trained and motivated.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What are your expectations from this company?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should have a clear idea of what he or she wants from the company. The candidate should also be able to clearly communicate those expectations to the interviewer.
expectations: Ability to communicate those expectations effectively
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I want to be a part of a company that values its employees and provides them with opportunities for growth and advancement.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you were overwhelmed and how did you handle it.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager is often the first to know when a crisis is brewing. He or she must be able to quickly and calmly assess the situation and take appropriate action. A candidate should be able to describe a time when he or she was overwhelmed and how he or she handled it.
expectations: Calmness in the face of crisis
Ability to quickly assess a situation and take appropriate action
Willingness to delegate tasks to others
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I was overwhelmed when I first started managing a department of three employees. I didn't know how to delegate tasks effectively, so I ended up doing everything myself. I learned that by delegating tasks, I could focus on my strengths and improve my employees' performance.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to deal with conflicting priorities.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to prioritize effectively, especially when multiple tasks or projects are due at the same time. A candidate should be able to explain how he or she determined which task or project to prioritize and why.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I had to prioritize between a customer service issue and a sales goal. I chose the sales goal because it was more important to the company's success.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What would you do to turn around a weak performer with tenure?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to handle employees who are underperforming or otherwise not meeting expectations. He or she must be able to identify the root cause of the problem and implement a solution that addresses it.
expectations: Ability to identify and address the root cause of a problem
Willingness to take necessary corrective action
Ability to communicate clearly and respectfully
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd sit down with the employee and discuss the issue. If it's a performance issue, I'd offer suggestions for improvement and set a timeline for improvement. If it's a behavioral issue, I'd offer suggestions for improvement and set a timeline for improvement. If the employee fails to meet the timeline, I'd document the failure and recommend termination.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What would your former coworkers say about you?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: The best way to learn about a candidate is to ask his or her former coworkers. A candidate should have a strong reputation for honesty, integrity and professionalism. He or she should be well-liked, respected and trusted by former coworkers.
expectations: Well-liked and respected by former coworkers
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: My coworkers would say I'm a hard worker who's always willing to pitch in and help out. They'd also say I'm a great listener who's always willing to lend an ear or an opinion.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you were able to resolve a problem for an angry customer.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Assistant store managers must be able to resolve customer complaints in a way that satisfies both the customer and the company. A candidate should be able to identify the source of the complaint and address it in a way that satisfies both parties.
expectations: Ability to identify and address the root of a customer's complaint
Ability to communicate clearly and respectfully
Willingness to set and implement consequences for inadequate complianc
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I was able to resolve a customer's complaint by listening to her concerns, identifying the source of her dissatisfaction and offering her a solution that satisfied both her and my employer.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to report unethical behavior.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to recognize and report unethical behavior, whether it's from a fellow employee or a customer. A candidate should be able to clearly and calmly explain how he or she handled the situation.
expectations: Calmness in the face of unethical behavior
Ability to clearly and calmly explain how he or she handled the situation
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I was working with a customer who was very rude and uncooperative. I asked him to leave the store, but he refused. I called my manager, who told me to call the police.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How will you measure the financial strength of a store?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to assess the financial strength of a store. This includes examining the store's financial statements, like the income statement and balance sheet, and understanding how to interpret them. The candidate should also be able to assess the store's cash flow and liquidity.
expectations: Cash flow and liquidity analysis proficiency
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd examine the store's financial statements, like the income statement and balance sheet, and understand how to interpret them. I'd also assess the store's cash flow and liquidity.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What was the most difficult situation you had to deal with in your previous job?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to demonstrate how he or she dealt with a difficult situation in the past. The candidate should also be able to articulate what he or she learned from the experience and how he or she would handle it differently in the future.
expectations: Demonstrated ability to deal with difficult situations
Demonstrated ability to learn from mistakes
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had a difficult employee who was constantly late and unproductive. I tried giving him more leeway, but that only made things worse. I finally had to let him go, and it was the right decision. I learned that sometimes you have to be tough on people, even if they're friends.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Where do you see yourself in 5 years from now?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager is a long-term position, and a candidate should have a clear idea of his or her career path. The candidate should also be able to explain how the position aligns with that path.
expectations: Awareness of the position's role in those goals
Ability to explain how the position aligns with those goals
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I see myself as a store manager in five years. This position will help me gain the experience I need to be ready for that role.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you solved an obscure problem.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be a problem solver, not just a problem identifier. A candidate should be able to identify and solve problems that are not obvious or easy to identify. He or she should also be able to explain how the solution was reached and why it was the best option.
expectations: Ability to explain how a solution was reached and why it was the best option
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had a customer who had been shopping at our store for years but had never purchased anything. I asked her why and she said she didn't like any of our products. I asked her what she did like and she said she liked the store's atmosphere. I asked her if she'd like to see some new products and she said yes. I showed her some new products and she bought them.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How long have you been working here?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Assistant store managers are often promoted from within, so it's important to understand how long the candidate has been with the company. It's also important to understand why the candidate is interested in the position and what he or she has done to prepare for it.
expectations: Awareness of own history with the company
Willingness to invest in preparation for the position
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I've been with the company for two years, and I'm very interested in this position because I've been preparing myself for it. I've taken several classes on management and leadership and have shadowed several assistant store managers.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What is your current job?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to clearly and concisely describe his or her current job and responsibilities. The candidate should be able to explain how his or her job fits into the company's overall mission and strategy.
expectations: Clear and concise description of current job
Ability to explain how job fits into company's overall mission and strategy
Knowledge of company's overall mission and strategy
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'm a merchandising manager at ABC Company, where I oversee product display and placement in all of our retail locations. I'm responsible for ensuring that our products are displayed in a way that maximizes sales.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What type of customer service metrics did you have to follow in your previous role?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager is responsible for ensuring customer satisfaction through the actions of his or her team. A candidate should be familiar with common metrics like customer satisfaction, customer retention and customer loyalty. He or she should also understand how to use those metrics to improve customer service and sales.
expectations: Familiarity with common customer service metrics
Understanding of how to use those metrics to improve customer service and sales
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I had to ensure my team maintained a high level of customer satisfaction by following the company's customer service guidelines. I also had to ensure my team was properly trained in those guidelines and that they were consistently followed.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What contributions can you make to our company?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should have a clear and concise answer to this question. He or she should be able to quickly and clearly explain how he or she can help the company grow, improve or otherwise succeed.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I can help your company grow by improving sales and customer service.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you went out of your way to help someone?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be a good people person. He or she must be able to empathize with and help customers, co-workers and even subordinates. A candidate should be able to relate a specific example of going out of his or her way to help someone.
expectations: Willingness to go out of one's way to help others
Ability to relate a specific example
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I helped a customer find a product that was out of stock by calling the manufacturer and getting the item shipped overnight.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell us about a recent situation in which your team was struggling and how did you embrace the situation?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: The assistant store manager is a team leader, and a team leader must be able to lead in times of difficulty. A candidate should be able to identify the problem, devise a solution and communicate it clearly to the team. He or she should also be able to motivate the team to follow through with the solution.
expectations: Ability to identify and analyze problems
Ability to communicate solutions clearly and motivate others to follow
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: My team was struggling with customer service issues, so I sat down with each member individually and discussed the problem. I then devised a plan for improving customer service by having each member focus on one aspect of customer service, like greeting customers or helping them find items.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a situation where you had to make an unpopular decision and how did you handle it?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to make unpopular decisions when necessary, like disciplining a problem employee or terminating one. He or she should also be able to explain the decision and its rationale to employees and customers.
expectations: Ability to explain the decision and rationale
Willingness to accept responsibility for unpopular decisions
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I had to fire a problem employee who had been late repeatedly and was mistreating customers. I explained the decision and its rationale to the employee and his peers, accepting responsibility for the decision.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you were asked to take lead of a project.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Assistant store managers are often asked to take lead of projects, whether it's a new store opening, a special promotion or a new product launch. A candidate should be able to demonstrate his or her ability to take on such responsibilities and complete them effectively.
expectations: Ability to take on and complete projects
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I was asked to lead a new store opening in my last job. I was able to increase sales by 30% in the first quarter and by 50% in the second quarter.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How have you improved the customer shopping experience?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager is responsible for improving the customer shopping experience in a variety of ways. He or she must be able to identify problems and implement solutions, like improving the layout of the store or creating a better shopping experience through more effective displays. He or she must also be able to motivate and train his or her team to provide the best customer service possible.
expectations: Ability to identify problems and create solutions
Skill in motivating and training employees
Willingness to take on extra responsibility
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I've improved the customer shopping experience by reorganizing the store's layout to make it easier for customers to find what they're looking for.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you handle difficult customers?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to handle difficult customers with tact and professionalism, neither giving in to their demands nor alienating them. He or she should be able to identify the source of the customer's dissatisfaction and work with the manager to resolve it.
expectations: Tactful and professional handling of difficult customers
Ability to identify customer dissatisfaction and work with manager to resolve it
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd listen carefully to the customer's concerns and try to understand what they're really trying to say. I'd then work with my manager to resolve the issue.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How would you order inventory for a store?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to effectively manage inventory, including ordering, receiving and stocking. A candidate should be familiar with the process and have experience with it.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd first review sales data to determine what products are selling well and which are not. I'd then order enough of the former to meet demand and reduce excess stock while ordering more of the latter to meet demand.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What position are you applying for?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager is a salesperson first and foremost. He or she must be able to effectively communicate with customers and team members, both verbally and nonverbally. An assistant store manager must be able to lead a team of salespeople and motivate them to meet or exceed sales goals. He or she must be able to effectively manage the store's inventory, including ordering, receiving, stocking and tracking sales.
expectations: Ability to communicate effectively with customers and team members
Ability to lead a team and motivate them to meet or exceed sales goals
Ability to manage the store's inventory
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'm applying for the assistant store manager position.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How will you deal with difficult sales reps?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Sales reps often have a difficult job, and they may be difficult themselves. An assistant store manager must be able to work with them, but he or she must also be able to set boundaries and enforce them.
expectations: Courtesy in the face of conflict
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd first listen to the sales rep's concerns and then explain the store's policies. If the rep continues to violate those policies, I'd have to let him or her go.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you motivate your team?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager is a manager first and foremost. A candidate should be able to motivate his or her team members to perform at their best and to help them grow professionally. He or she should be able to communicate effectively with his or her team members and understand their strengths and weaknesses.
expectations: Willingness to help team members grow
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I motivate my team by being a role model for them. I do what I expect them to do, and I hold them accountable for their actions. I also make sure they know that they can come to me with any questions or concerns they have.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How will you drive business?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be a salesperson. He or she must be able to drive business through effective merchandising, marketing and product display efforts. He or she must also be able to teach those skills to team members.
expectations: Skills in merchandising, marketing and displaying product
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'll use the company's sales and inventory software to track our progress against our goals. I'll then analyze the data and make recommendations for improving our performance. I'll also train my team on how to use the software so they can help me achieve our goals.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What metrics do you track at your current job?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Assistant store managers are responsible for a variety of metrics, from sales to inventory to customer satisfaction. A candidate should be familiar with the most common metrics and be able to explain how he or she tracks them.
expectations: Ability to explain how those metrics are tracked
Willingness to track additional metrics if necessary
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I track sales, inventory and customer satisfaction metrics. I also track employee performance, including attendance and productivity.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How would you handle a situation where your store manager asked you to do something that violated company policy?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to follow the rules and policies of the company, even when they conflict with the instructions of his or her store manager. A candidate should be able to explain why he or she would or wouldn't follow a given instruction, and should be able to explain how he or she would handle the situation if the store manager were to insist.
expectations: Respect for company policies and procedures
Ability to set aside personal feelings and opinions
Willingness to stand up for what is right
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd explain to my manager that I can't do what he's asking because it violates company policy. If he insists, I'd ask him to speak with his supervisor.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to address performance issues with an employee.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to address performance issues with employees. This includes both performance issues that are the fault of the employee and performance issues that are the fault of the manager. A candidate should be able to identify the root cause of a problem and communicate clearly and effectively with the employee about how to improve.
expectations: Ability to identify and communicate with employees about performance issues
Ability to identify and communicate with employees about performance issues
Ability to identify and communicate with employees about performance issues
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I had an employee who was consistently late for work, which hurt his or her ability to do his or her job well. I sat down with him or her and explained how his or her tardiness affected our ability to meet our goals. I also explained how his or her tardiness affected him or her personally.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What is your greatest strength?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should identify a strength that is relevant to the position and that he or she can demonstrate through past experience.
expectations: A strength that is relevant to the position
A strength that the candidate has demonstrated through past experience
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: My greatest strength is my ability to work well with others. I've been able to work with a wide variety of personalities and get them all on the same page.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What is your definition of success?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to articulate a definition of success that is both personally and professionally oriented. It should be realistic and achievable, but it should also be aspirational.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: Success to me is being able to live comfortably while doing work I enjoy and being able to provide for my family.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you broke the rules and what was the result.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to make decisions and take action in the moment, even if that means breaking the rules. A candidate should have a good reason for doing so and be able to explain that reason in a way that demonstrates his or her ability to make good decisions and take appropriate action.
expectations: Ability to make good decisions and take appropriate action
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I broke the rules by allowing a customer to return an item after the return period had expired. The customer was very upset and I felt bad for her. She had bought a gift for her daughter's birthday but it didn't fit. She had no time to exchange it before the party and she was afraid her daughter would be disappointed. I let her return it because I knew she'd never forgive herself if she didn't get it exchanged in time.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How would you handle a situation where your manager asks you to do something unethical?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to trust his or her manager. A candidate should be able to recognize when a manager is asking him or her to do something unethical and, if so, refuse to comply. If the candidate is unsure, he or she should ask for clarification and, if necessary, seek advice from a trusted third party.
expectations: Willingness to seek advice from a third party
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd ask for clarification on the request and, if necessary, consult with a trusted third party. If I still wasn't sure whether the request was unethical, I'd refuse to comply.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What would you do if a rep started talking back to you publicly?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to handle a difficult situation with tact and professionalism. He or she should be able to calmly and clearly communicate expectations and consequences for failure to meet them. The candidate should also be able to recognize when a situation is beyond his or her control and delegate it to a superior.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd calmly ask the rep to step into the office. If he or she continued to act out, I'd ask him or her to leave the store.

Assistant Store Manager.question: If we decided not to hire you, what would be your next move?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should always be prepared to move on to the next opportunity, whether it's with the company or another. If the candidate is certain he or she will not accept a job offer, he or she should be prepared to explain why.
expectations: Willingness to accept rejection and move on
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd thank you for your time and consideration and ask if there's anything else I can do to help you make your decision. If not, I'd follow up with a letter thanking you again for your time and reiterating my interest in the position.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What is the most difficult situation you have faced with a customer?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to handle any customer situation, from a simple complaint to a complex problem. A candidate should be able to calmly and effectively resolve the issue while maintaining a positive relationship with the customer.
expectations: Ability to communicate clearly and respectfully
Willingness to set and implement consequences for inadequate complianc
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had a customer who was upset about a product's price. I explained that the price was set by the manufacturer and that I couldn't change it. He then became angry and started yelling at me. I remained calm and told him that if he didn't stop yelling, I'd have to ask him to leave. He apologized and left without further incident.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you build a team?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be able to build a team that can work together to achieve the company's goals. A candidate should be able to identify the strengths and weaknesses of team members and assign them tasks accordingly. He or she should also be able to motivate and inspire team members to work hard and achieve their goals.
expectations: Ability to identify strengths and weaknesses of team members
Ability to motivate and inspire team members
Ability to assign tasks according to strengths and weaknesses
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd first get to know each member of the team and learn what motivates them. I'd then assign tasks according to each person's strengths and weaknesses. I'd also make sure they know how much I appreciate their hard work.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when your integrity was questioned and how did you deal with it?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: An assistant store manager must be a role model for integrity, honesty and fairness. A candidate should be able to demonstrate a history of integrity and honesty in his or her personal and professional life. A candidate should be able to demonstrate how he or she would handle a situation where his or her integrity was questioned.
expectations: Integrity and honesty in personal and professional life
Ability to handle a situation where integrity is questioned
Willingness to admit mistakes and take responsibility for them
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I've never had my integrity questioned, but if I did I'd admit my mistake and take responsibility for it.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What makes you the best candidate for this position?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: The best assistant store manager candidates are the ones who can clearly and concisely explain why they're the best. They should be able to point to specific examples of their past success in similar roles and demonstrate how they'll apply those skills to this new position.
expectations: Demonstrated ability to apply skills to new situations
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I've been a top performer in every sales role I've had, including my current one. I'm confident I can do the same here.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you hold your staff accountable to their goals?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to demonstrate a history of holding his or her own staff accountable to their goals. He or she should also be able to explain how he or she does so.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I hold my staff accountable by reviewing their performance on a weekly basis, and I give them the opportunity to explain any issues or concerns.

Assistant Store Manager.question: What do you like to do in your free time?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate's answer to this question can be revealing. It can demonstrate a candidate's interests, hobbies, personality and values. It can also reveal whether the candidate is a good fit for the job.
expectations: Demonstrates a fit with the job
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I like to read, play video games and go to the movies.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How would you measure a bathroom for tile?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A bathroom is a small space, so it's important to choose the right tile for the job. The candidate should know how to measure the space to determine how much tile is needed. He or she should also know how to calculate the amount of grout needed.
expectations: Familiarity with common types of tile
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I'd measure the room and calculate the amount of tile and grout needed.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you manage your team?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Assistant store managers must be able to effectively manage their team members. A candidate should be able to delegate tasks and responsibilities, provide constructive feedback, and resolve conflicts.
expectations: Ability to delegate tasks and responsibilities
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I make sure my team members know what's expected of them and how they can improve. I also make sure they know I'm there to support them.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How did you overcome major personnel problems and long term employees that have been taught very different ways of doing projects, and bring them together?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be able to demonstrate his or her ability to resolve personnel problems and bring together a diverse group of employees. This is a key skill for an assistant store manager, who must be able to lead a team of employees with varying levels of experience and training.
expectations: Ability to lead a team of varying experience levels
Willingness to delegate tasks to others
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I've had to do this at my last job, where I had to lead a team of employees with varying levels of experience and training. I was able to do so by delegating tasks and responsibilities to others while providing clear, consistent direction and support.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time you failed.
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate who has never failed at anything is either lying or has never done anything. A candidate who has failed but doesn't know how to learn from it is also not a good fit. A good candidate will have a story of failure that he or she can discuss with humility and honesty, and will have learned from it.
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I once failed to meet a sales goal by $10,000. I took the time to analyze the problem and found that I had been spending too much time on the floor interacting with customers and not enough time on the phone closing deals. I adjusted my schedule accordingly and met my goal the next quarter.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How do you motivate your employees?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: Motivation is a key component of employee performance. A motivated employee is a productive employee. An assistant store manager must be able to motivate his or her team members to achieve the company's goals. This involves understanding each employee's strengths and weaknesses and using that knowledge to motivate them.
expectations: Understanding of employee strengths and weaknesses
Willingness to delegate tasks to motivate employees
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: I motivate my employees by praising them when they do well and offering constructive criticism when they don't.

Assistant Store Manager.question: How did your last job measure its KPIs?
Assistant Store Manager.overview: A candidate should be familiar with the key performance indicators of the position, including sales, profit, customer satisfaction, employee satisfaction and safety. He or she should also be familiar with how those KPIs are measured and how they are used to make decisions.
expectations: Familiarity with how the KPIs are measured and used to make decisions
Assistant Store Manager.sampleAnswer: My last employer used a combination of sales data, customer surveys and employee satisfaction surveys to measure its KPIs.

Assistant Store Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to choose between two competing tasks?

Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a lot of experience in the industry and have worked with many companies like yours. I've been able to help them improve their performance and achieve their goals. I'm passionate about my work, and I'm excited to bring my skills to your company.

Consultant.question: What is recursion and how can it be applied?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of computer science and ability to think critically. Recursion is a programming technique that involves repeating a process within itself. The answer should include an example of how recursion can be applied in a real-world situation.
expectations: Ability to explain complex concepts in a clear manner
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Recursion is a programming technique that involves repeating a process within itself. For example, if you wanted to print out the numbers 1 through 10, you could write a program that would print out the numbers 1 through 9, then print out the number 10, then go back to printing out the numbers 1 through 9 again. This is an example of recursion. Recursion can be applied in many different ways. For instance, it can be used to solve complex problems or create algorithms for sorting and searching data.

Consultant.question: What kind of companies do you typically work with?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's understanding of the consulting industry and the types of companies that hire consultants. It also shows how well the applicant knows your company.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of your company and industry

Consultant.sampleAnswer: I typically work with companies in the manufacturing, retail and technology industries. I enjoy working with these types of businesses because they are constantly changing and growing. I think my experience in these industries will be a great fit for your company.

Consultant.question: What are your long-term goals?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant has a plan for his or her career. A consultant's career path may be less linear than that of a traditional employee, so the answer should show that the applicant is thinking about the future.
expectations: Ability to set and achieve goals
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I want to continue to grow my business and expand my client base. I also want to continue to learn and improve my skills. I believe these two things will help me achieve my long-term goal of becoming a leader in my industry.

Consultant.question: Why do you want to work with us?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to gauge the applicant's interest in your company and the position. An applicant should be able to explain why they want to work with you and how their skills and experience will help you achieve your goals.

I think I can bring a lot of value to your organization. I have a lot of experience working with companies like yours, and I know how to help them reach their goals. I'm also very interested in the position because it will allow me to use my skills in a new way.

Consultant.question: Why should we hire you over other candidates?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the applicant can sell themselves. They should be able to explain their skills and experience in a way that makes them stand out.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a highly motivated individual who is eager to learn and grow. I have a proven track record of success in my field and I'm excited to bring that experience to your company. I'm very familiar with your industry and I've worked with companies just like yours. I know what it takes to succeed in this role and I'm confident that I can help you achieve your goals.

Consultant.question: What was good and bad in your past projects?
Consultant.overview: This question gives you insight into the applicant's past work experience. Look for a candidate who has a history of working on successful projects.
expectations: Applicant's ability to identify and learn from mistakes

I've also learned from my mistakes. On one project, I didn't do enough research before beginning. The project ended up taking longer than expected, and I had to spend extra time and money to complete it.

Consultant.question: How does your background fit in?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to think on your feet and to understand the position you're interviewing for. It also gives you insight into the applicant's experience and how they think about their own career.
expectations: Applicant's ability to explain how their background fits in with the job
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a lot of experience working with companies in the retail industry. I've worked with many different types of retailers, including department stores, specialty stores and online retailers. I've also worked with companies that provide services to retailers, such as manufacturers and distributors. I've learned a lot from my experiences and I'm excited to put that knowledge to use for your company.

Consultant.question: Why do you want to work in this position?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant is a good fit for the job. The interviewer wants to see if the applicant has researched the position and understands the responsibilities. Applicants should also explain why they are interested in the position, how they can contribute and how they will fit in with the team.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've been interested in this position since I saw it posted. I think it's a great opportunity to work with a growing company and help it reach its goals. I'm passionate about helping companies grow and develop. I think my experience working with companies in a variety of industries will be an asset to this company. I'm excited about working with a team that is so passionate about its work.

Consultant.question: What areas do you need to improve your technical skills?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test the applicant's self-awareness and ability to identify areas of improvement. The answer should show the candidate is willing to work hard to improve their skills and is open to feedback.
expectations: Ability to identify areas of improvement
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm always looking for ways to improve my skills. I've recently been working on improving my presentation skills and my ability to work with clients. I've also been looking into new technologies that can help me do my job better. I'm always open to feedback and I'm committed to working hard to improve my skills.

Consultant.question: What is your experience with software systems?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test the applicant's knowledge of software systems and how they can be used to improve business processes. The answer should demonstrate the applicant's ability to understand how software can be used to solve problems and improve efficiency.
expectations: Ability to identify and explain software system issues
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have extensive experience with software systems. I know that many companies use them to improve efficiency and productivity. I've worked with a variety of systems, including customer relationship management, enterprise resource planning, and supply chain management. I've also worked with custom-built systems that were designed specifically for a company's needs. I've been able to help companies identify issues and develop solutions that have led to greater efficiency and profitability.

Consultant.question: How do you handle pressure?
Consultant.overview: This question tests how well applicants handle stress and pressure. It also reveals how they deal with difficult situations and how they respond to criticism.
expectations: Applicant's ability to remain calm under pressure
Ability to remain focused on the task at hand

When I'm under pressure, I make sure to take the time to think through my plan and make adjustments as needed. I also like to have a few back-up plans in case things don't go as expected. When I'm working on a project, I like to think of it as a puzzle. I break the project down into small steps and focus on completing each one before moving on. This helps me stay organized and focused.

Consultant.question: Why do you want to be an intern with us?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the applicant understands your company and its goals. Applicants should show they have done their research and are genuinely interested in the internship.

Consultant.question: How would you obtain information if going to work for a client in an industry that was not familiar with?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to research a new industry and company. It also shows how the applicant would approach a new project and what steps he or she would take to learn about the business.

Ability to adapt to new industries and companies

I would attend industry events and conferences, read trade publications and speak with consultants who have experience in the industry.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a time you failed.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to learn from mistakes and move forward. Candidates should share a failure that taught them a lesson and how they applied that lesson to future projects.
expectations: Applicant's ability to learn from mistakes
Ability to explain how they learned from a failure
Ability to communicate the lesson learned

I was so frustrated that I almost quit the project. However, I decided to stick it out and focus on my work. I learned that this client was just very difficult to please. I also learned that I needed to be more patient and understanding when working with clients.

Consultant.question: What is your role when you are part of a team or group working towards common goals?

Consultant.question: What are some of your achievements?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate will respond to a challenge. The interviewer wants to know how the applicant will respond to a problem and how they will present their achievements.

Consultant.question: What were your responsibilities as BA?

I worked with clients to understand their needs and then documented those needs in a way that was easy to understand. I also worked with development teams to ensure the requirements were met. I was responsible for testing the software to ensure it met the requirements.

Consultant.question: How will you interact with clients in the petroleum business?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's understanding of the industry and how he or she will approach clients. The answer should show that the applicant has done research on the industry and has a plan for working with clients.

I've also worked with government agencies and nonprofits. I understand that every client has different needs, so I always take time to learn about their business and how they operate. I also like to get to know the people I'm working with on a personal level, which helps me establish trusting relationships.

Consultant.question: How do you approach a new project?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work independently and manage multiple projects. It also gives you insight into how the applicant will approach a new project.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I like to start by learning about the company and its goals. I then identify the problems that are holding the company back from reaching its goals. I think about what solutions I can offer that will help the company reach its goals. I also consider how my work will fit into the company's larger strategy. I like to be as proactive as possible, so I also like to identify any potential roadblocks before they occur.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a time when you had to work in a team.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work with others and communicate effectively. It also shows whether the applicant has experience working in a team environment.

Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have always worked in teams, whether it was with my classmates in school or with my colleagues at work. I think teamwork is essential to achieving success. I believe that each person brings something unique to the table, and when we combine our strengths, we can accomplish more than we could alone. I have always been a team player.

Consultant.question: What is the most difficult situation you have faced in your previous job?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to handle pressure and work through a difficult situation. It also shows whether the candidate has faced any challenges in the past and how they overcame them.

I had spent a lot of time on the project, but I knew it wasn't what my boss wanted. I had to present it anyway and explain why I thought it was the best solution. In the end, my boss was pleased with my work and agreed with my conclusions.

Consultant.question: What do you hope to gain out of this job?

Consultant.question: How many tennis balls can you fit in a room?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your creativity and ability to think outside the box. It also shows whether you can apply your problem-solving skills to a hypothetical situation.

Consultant.question: What difference do you want to make in IBM?

Consultant.question: How will you manage in project crunch situations?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well you handle pressure. It's important for consultants to be able to manage their time and workload effectively.

I also like to work with a team, so I make sure everyone is on the same page. If we're all working toward the same goal, it's easier to manage the project crunch.

Consultant.question: What are the domains in which we operate?

Consultant.question: What is cloud computing?

Consultant.sampleAnswer: Cloud computing is a term used to describe a network of remote servers that store data and software applications. Cloud computing allows companies to store and access data from any location, on any device. Cloud computing is a great way for companies to save money and resources by outsourcing their IT needs.

Consultant.question: What modules have you worked in ServiceNow?

Consultant.question: What motivates you?

Consultant.question: What kind of technologies are you interested in?

I would also look for any correlations between different variables. Finally, I would create a hypothesis for what I think the outcome will be and test it against the data.

Consultant.question: What is your definition of an insight?

Consultant.question: What do you think a consultant does?

I want to work with a company that will help me achieve my career goals.

Consultant.question: Why are you leaving your current job?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to be honest and professional. The interviewer wants to know if the candidate is leaving for a better opportunity or because of a conflict. The answer should be positive and show the applicant is looking forward to the next step in his or her career.
expectations: Ability to explain why he or she is leaving without sounding negative
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm leaving my current job because I'm ready for a new challenge. I've learned a lot at my current company, and I'm ready to put that knowledge to work in a new environment. I'm excited about the opportunity with your company and look forward to contributing my skills and experience.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a person that you had difficulty working with.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the candidate's ability to work with others and their interpersonal skills. The answer also shows the candidate's ability to handle conflict and resolve issues.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once worked with a team member who was very talented but had a difficult personality. He was very critical of others' work and often made them feel bad. I was able to work with him because I was able to build a trusting relationship with him. I was honest about my feelings and he was able to understand how his behavior affected others. We were able to work together and he became more open-minded and respectful of others' opinions.

Consultant.question: Describe a project in Change Management you have led.
Consultant.overview: Change management is a broad term that encompasses many different types of projects. This question is designed to see how well applicants can tailor their responses to the specific type of project they're being asked about. The answer should show the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to work in a team.
expectations: Applicant's ability to tailor answers to specific project types
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I led a project in change management at a large company that was in the process of merging with another company. The company was undergoing a lot of changes, including new leadership, which meant employees were feeling anxious and unsure about the future. I worked with the leaders to develop a strategy for communicating with employees and helping them understand how the merger would affect them. I also worked with employees directly, helping them understand what to expect and how they could prepare for the changes ahead.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a time when you had to convince your manager that your view was the correct one.
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to communicate effectively and work well with others. It also reveals how the applicant approaches conflict and shows how they handle stress.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I had a situation where I was working with a group of people on a project. I was in charge of the project, but I had to work with a team of people who were not familiar with my work style. I had to convince them that my way of doing things was the best way. I did this by being open and honest about my process and showing them how it would help the team meet its goals.

Consultant.question: What was the last conflict you had with a client?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate deals with conflict. It also shows how well the applicant can communicate and work with others.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I recently had a conflict with a client over the scope of a project. The client wanted me to complete the project in less time than I had estimated. I explained that I could not complete the project in the time frame they wanted without sacrificing quality. The client was not happy with my response, but I stood my ground. In the end, we compromised on a schedule that was acceptable to both of us.

Consultant.question: How would you approach a CEO?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your ability to think on your feet and communicate effectively. The answer should show that you have a solid understanding of the CEO's role in the company and how you would approach him or her.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think on their feet
Knowledge of the CEO's role in the company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first do some research on the company and its CEO. I would then schedule a meeting with the CEO and make sure I was prepared with a few key talking points. I would also want to know what the CEO's goals are for the company and how my work could help him or her achieve those goals.

Consultant.question: What experience do you have in the pharmaceutical industry?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of the industry and your ability to think on your feet. It also shows how well you can explain your experience and how you can add value to a company.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of the pharmaceutical industry
Ability to explain how their experience can be applied to a new company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've worked with pharmaceutical companies for more than 10 years. I've worked with large firms and small startups. I've helped companies develop strategies for growth and improve their bottom line. I've also helped companies develop new products and bring them to market. I'm very familiar with the industry and the challenges it faces.

Consultant.question: What kind of data would you prefer to work with?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and how they prefer to work with data. The answer should show an understanding of the different types of data and how they can be used.
expectations: Applicant's preference for working with certain types of data
Ability to understand and analyze data
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I prefer to work with qualitative data. I think it's more useful in the long run because it helps me understand the underlying reasons for a problem or opportunity. Quantitative data is great for measuring performance, but it doesn't always give me a complete picture of what's going on.

Consultant.question: What is the notice period of your current job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant handles a potentially uncomfortable situation. It's important to hire people who are honest and direct.
expectations: Applicant's ability to be honest and direct
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a two-week notice period with my current employer.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a time you resolved a conflict in a group setting.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well you can handle conflict. It's important for consultants to be able to work with others and resolve issues. This question is also a good way to see how well you can communicate and work with others.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I recently worked on a project with a team of people from different departments. We had to come together to solve a problem that was affecting the entire company. We were all very passionate about our ideas, but we had to find a solution that everyone could agree on. I was able to help the team reach a compromise by listening to everyone's opinions and coming up with a solution that everyone felt good about.

Consultant.question: How will you write a query for the given situation?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to write a query letter. The query is the first document a consultant sends to a potential client. It should be short and to the point, highlighting the consultant's experience and expertise.
expectations: Applicant's ability to write a concise and persuasive query letter
Ability to tailor the query to the client's needs
Ability to research the client and demonstrate understanding of their business
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would begin by introducing myself and my firm. I would then explain why I am writing and what I have to offer. I would then describe my experience and expertise in the area of consulting that is relevant to the client's needs. I would conclude by asking for an opportunity to speak with the client about my qualifications.

Consultant.question: Why are you looking for a new job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test the applicant's honesty and integrity. Candidates should be prepared to explain why they are looking for a new job and how it will benefit the company.
expectations: Ability to explain why they are looking for a new job
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a new job because I want to work for a company that has the same values as I do. I believe in hard work and doing what's best for the customer. I also want to work for a company that has a strong commitment to its employees. I've been working as a consultant for several years and have learned a lot about business and how companies operate. I'm ready to take my knowledge and apply it in a new environment.

Consultant.question: Why do you want to be a consultant?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see whether the applicant has done research on the industry and understands what it takes to succeed. The answer should show that the applicant is passionate about the field and has a clear idea of what it takes to succeed.
expectations: Motivation for entering the consulting field
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've always been fascinated by how businesses work and how they can be improved. I've worked with a number of companies over the years, and I've seen firsthand how consultants can help them improve performance. I want to be a consultant because I enjoy working with businesses and helping them grow.

Consultant.question: What is your dream job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant thinks about their career. It's a good way to see whether they are motivated by money or by the work itself.
expectations: Applicant's willingness to take on new challenges and learn new skills
Consultant.sampleAnswer: My dream job would be to work as a consultant for a company that is passionate about its products and services. I want to work with a company that is committed to its customers and has a strong vision for the future. I want to be able to work with a team that is willing to push the boundaries of what's possible and help the company grow.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a time when you had to make an unpopular decision.
Consultant.overview: This question tests how well applicants can handle conflict and difficult situations. It also gives you insight into the applicant's leadership skills and ability to make tough calls.
expectations: Applicant's ability to make unpopular decisions
Ability to lead others through a difficult situation
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I had to make an unpopular decision when I was working with a client who was struggling with a new product launch. The client was having trouble getting the product into stores, and I had to tell the client that we needed to change the product's packaging. The client didn't want to hear it, but I knew it was the right decision. We ended up changing the packaging, and the product became a huge success.

Consultant.question: What do you know about change management?
Consultant.overview: Change management is a critical part of any consulting project. Companies hire consultants to bring about change, and the consultant must be able to manage that change. This question tests the applicant's knowledge of change management and ability to explain how he or she would handle it.
expectations: Applicant's understanding of the importance of change management
Ability to explain how he or she would handle change management
Ability to explain how he or she would handle resistance to change
Consultant.sampleAnswer: Change management is an important part of any consulting project. It's the process of helping employees adjust to new processes, procedures and systems. Change management is often necessary when a company is implementing new technology or changing its business model. I think the most important part of change management is communication.

Consultant.question: What skills do you have to pursue as a consultant?
Consultant.overview: This question tests your knowledge of the skills needed to succeed as a consultant. It also reveals whether you have researched the profession and are familiar with the skills that are most important.
expectations: Applicant's understanding of the skills needed to be a consultant
Ability to explain how they will acquire those skills
Knowledge of the industry and its trends
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I have a strong background in business and finance, which will help me understand the company's goals and how I can help achieve them. I also have experience in sales, which will help me sell my services to clients. I am a quick learner and have excellent communication skills. I am also a self-starter who can work independently and manage my time effectively.

Consultant.question: What challenges do you foresee?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think critically and anticipate problems. It also shows whether the candidate has done any research on your company.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I see a few challenges ahead. First, I think the company is going to need to make some changes in its leadership structure. I've noticed that the company is very siloed and that communication is lacking. I think the company will need to make some changes in order to be more efficient.

Consultant.question: How would you handle a situation where client wants you implement a particular solution but your team does not think it will be effective and presents another solution?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to handle conflict and build consensus. It also reveals how the candidate thinks about client satisfaction. Look for an answer that shows the applicant is willing to listen to others and consider their ideas.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first make sure my team and I understand the client's goals and objectives. Then, I would explain our concerns and offer an alternative solution. I would also suggest a trial period so we can test the effectiveness of the solution. If the client is not satisfied with our solution, we will work together to find a better one.

Consultant.question: How did you help yourself to learn quickly during your internship?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant learns and grows. The interviewer wants to know how the applicant will take on new challenges and responsibilities.
expectations: Ability to adapt to new situations
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I always made sure I was prepared for meetings and presentations. I read up on the company and the industry, and I learned about the company's goals and challenges. I also made sure to ask questions during meetings and take notes so I could review them later.

Consultant.question: What was a time you worked in a group with conflict?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to work with others and resolve issues. It also gives you insight into the candidate's personality and how he or she deals with conflict.
expectations: Ability to be a team player
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very outgoing person and I enjoy working with others. I've never had a problem working in a group, but there have been times when I've had to deal with conflict. In one situation, I was working on a team that was having trouble coming to a consensus on a project. I stepped in and helped the team reach an agreement by encouraging everyone to express their opinions. I also helped the team come up with solutions that would work for everyone.

Consultant.question: Tell me about a time when you had to deliver something in a timeline that was not possible?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think on their feet and come up with a solution. It also shows how they handle pressure and whether they can deliver under pressure.
expectations: Applicant's ability to think quickly and solve problems
Ability to prioritize and manage time
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I once had to deliver a project that was due in two weeks. The client was very clear that the project needed to be done in two weeks, but I knew it would take me longer than that. I met with the client and explained that I could deliver the project in two weeks, but it would be of lower quality than if I had more time. The client agreed to give me more time, and I delivered the project on time and within budget.

Consultant.question: How would you deal with being in a hotel every night for the next few months?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the applicant will react to a situation that may be uncomfortable. It's important for consultants to be able to work independently and not be distracted by factors outside their control.
expectations: Ability to adapt to new situations
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very independent person, so I'm not worried about being in a hotel for a few months. I'm sure it will be a little strange at first, but I'm sure I'll get used to it. I know that the company wants me to be as productive as possible, so I'll make sure to get a good night's sleep and work hard during the day.

Consultant.question: Give me examples of complex situations that you have managed.
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates handle pressure and difficult situations. It also tests their ability to think on their feet and come up with solutions. Applicants should focus on situations that show their problem-solving skills, leadership and ability to work with other people.
expectations: Ability to think critically and creatively
Ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I've managed several complex situations in my career. One of my first projects was for a large company that wanted to expand into a new market. I was tasked with helping the company develop a plan for entering the new market and making recommendations for the best approach. I had to work with several departments within the company, as well as outside consultants, to develop a strategy that would be successful. The project took several months, but we were able to come up with a plan that was approved by the board of directors.

Consultant.question: How will you design a fault tolerant application or service?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test your knowledge of computer science and software development. It's also a good way to see how you think through problems and how well you can communicate your ideas.
expectations: Applicant's ability to design a fault tolerant application or service
Knowledge of computer science and software development
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first identify the most common faults that could occur in the application or service. Then I would design the system to handle those faults. For example, if the system is supposed to send an email, I would make sure it can handle a server crash or network failure. I would also make sure the system can handle a large number of users at once.

Consultant.question: How would you approach a project of this sort?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's ability to think critically and address specific issues. The answer should show a clear understanding of the project and the steps the applicant would take to complete it.
expectations: Ability to follow a project from start to finish
Ability to research and understand the project
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I would first do some research on the company and its goals. I would then talk with the company's leadership to understand their vision for the project. I would also want to speak with employees who will be involved in the project so I can get a better idea of what they need from me. After that, I would create a plan for completing the project and set deadlines for each step. I would also make sure to keep everyone involved in the loop as I progress through the project.

Consultant.question: What is the software development life cycle?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of software development and the SDLC. The SDLC is a process that software developers use to create, test and deploy software. It's important for consultants to understand this process and how it can be applied to different types of projects.
expectations: Ability to apply the SDLC to different types of projects
Ability to explain the SDLC in a way that is easy to understand
Consultant.sampleAnswer: The software development life cycle is a process that software developers use to create, test and deploy software. It's important for consultants to understand this process and how it can be applied to different types of projects. The SDLC consists of five steps: analysis, design, implementation, testing and deployment. Each step has its own purpose and is critical to the success of the project.

Consultant.question: How do you work in a team?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate can work with others. It also reveals whether the applicant has a collaborative or independent style. Look for an answer that shows the applicant can work well with others and is able to communicate effectively.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work in a team
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm a big believer in teamwork. I think it's important for consultants to be able to work with others and share ideas. I've found that when consultants work together, they can come up with better solutions and ideas than they could alone. That's why I'm always open to working with others and sharing my ideas.

Consultant.question: What do you expect from the job?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate understands the role and the company. The answer should show the applicant's interest in the position and understanding of what will be expected of them.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a position that will allow me to use my skills and experience to help a company achieve its goals. I'm interested in a position that will allow me to work with a variety of clients and projects. I'm also looking for a company that values teamwork and collaboration.

Consultant.question: What are the likely macro economic developments and how should Cognizant position itself in global markets?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the industry and ability to think critically about the future. The answer should show the candidate's ability to analyze trends and make predictions.
expectations: Applicant's ability to analyze macroeconomic trends
Ability to think critically about the future
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I believe the global economy will continue to grow at a steady pace. I think the biggest challenge for Cognizant will be keeping up with demand for its services. I think Cognizant should focus on expanding its services in emerging markets, especially in Asia. I think Cognizant should also invest in research and development to ensure it stays ahead of the curve.

Consultant.question: What courses did you take in college that will help you with this position?
Consultant.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the skills needed for the job. It also shows how well the applicant researched the company and position.
expectations: Applicant's knowledge of the skills needed for the job
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I took a number of courses in college that will help me with this position. I took a class on business strategy that taught me how to identify and solve problems. I also took a class on marketing that taught me how to develop a brand and promote it effectively. I think these skills will help me do my job well.

Consultant.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Consultant.overview: This is a classic interview question, but it's still one of the most important. The answer should be honest and show the candidate's ability to self-evaluate. Look for an answer that shows the applicant is aware of his or her weaknesses and is working to improve them.
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I'm very organized and detail-oriented. I'm also very good at building relationships with clients and colleagues. My weakness is that I can be too focused on the details. I need to remember that sometimes it's more important to look at the big picture.

Consultant.question: How did you go about getting help on a project?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate approaches problems and how he or she works with others. The answer should show that the candidate is proactive and willing to seek help when needed.
expectations: Applicant's ability to work with others
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I always try to solve problems on my own first. If I can't solve the problem, I reach out to my manager or a colleague for help. I like to work independently, but I also know that sometimes it's better to ask for help.

Consultant.question: Where do you see yourself fitting in?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate understands the role of a consultant. Applicants should be able to explain how they will contribute to the company and what they can do to help it achieve its goals.
expectations: Applicant's understanding of the role of a consultant
Ability to explain how they will contribute to the company
Consultant.sampleAnswer: I see myself as a valuable asset to your company. I am a skilled problem-solver who will work with your team to identify issues and find solutions. I will also work with you to develop a plan that will help you achieve your goals.

Consultant.question: Why did you choose NCS?
Consultant.overview: This question is designed to test your knowledge of the company and your interest in working for it. It's also a chance for you to show your enthusiasm and interest in the position.
