Office Manager.overview: This is a fun question that gives the applicant an opportunity to show their personality. A good answer will be honest and show that they're a good fit for the company.
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: My superpower is my ability to multitask. I can always find a way to get everything done and I'm always willing to help out when needed.

Office Manager.question: What are your goals for the next position?
Office Manager.overview: An office manager should be able to articulate their goals for the next position. They should be able to express their desire to grow and develop as an employee and how they plan to do so.
expectations: A desire to grow and develop
A desire to learn new skills
A desire to improve their current skills,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I want to continue to grow as a leader and manager. I'm always looking for ways to improve my skills and I'm always open to new opportunities.

Office Manager.question: Why do you want to work in Dental?
Office Manager.overview: This question is designed to find out if the applicant has any experience or knowledge of the dental field. It's important that they have some understanding of the field so they can be a good fit for the position.
expectations: Willingness to learn about the field,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I've always had a passion for helping people and I think working in a dental office would be a great way to do that. I'm looking forward to learning more about the field and becoming an effective member of your team.

Office Manager.question: How does your past experience help you in this role?
Office Manager.overview: This question is designed to give you an idea of how the candidate has performed in previous roles. It's important to find someone who has experience working in a similar position. If they haven't worked in a similar role before, it's important that they be able to demonstrate that they have the skills and abilities needed to succeed in the position.
expectations: Experience working in a similar position
Willingness to talk about their past experience,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I've been working as an office manager for over five years. I've been able to use my experience to streamline office procedures and make sure that the office is running smoothly.

Office Manager.question: How would you handle 2 employees who are in a disagreement about something work related?
Office Manager.overview: Office managers are responsible for maintaining a positive and productive work environment. This means that they'll have to step in when there are conflicts between employees. A good candidate will be able to handle these situations in a way that is fair to both parties and doesn't disrupt the workflow of the office.
expectations: Ability to remain calm and objective
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand what the disagreement was about and then talk to each employee individually. I would try to find out what each person's concerns were and then try to come up with a solution that satisfied both of them.

Office Manager.question: How would you move doubledutch to the new space?
Office Manager.overview: The office manager is responsible for overseeing the move of the company to a new location. This includes making sure that all of the necessary equipment and supplies are moved to the new location and that the employees are able to continue working as normal. It's important that the candidate be able to provide a detailed plan of how they would go about this process.
expectations: Ability to work with a team,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first make sure that all of the equipment and supplies were packed and ready to move. I would then schedule a moving company to transport everything to the new office. Once everything was in place I would make sure that all of the employees were able to access their workstations and get back to work as soon as possible.

Office Manager.question: Why do you think we should consider you for this position?
Office Manager.overview: This is a great opportunity for the applicant to showcase their knowledge of the company and their understanding of the position. A good candidate will have done some research on the specific needs of the company and should be able to answer in a way that showcases their understanding of the position along with any relevant skills they possess.
expectations: Focus on leadership and the needs of the team
Recognition of their impact on the team,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I'm very interested in this position because I believe I have the skills and experience to make a valuable contribution to your team. I've done some research on your company and believe I can help you reach your goals.

Office Manager.question: How do you define customer service?
Office Manager.overview: A good candidate will be able to explain what customer service means to them and how they would apply it to the office environment. It's important that they understand the importance of customer service in an office setting and how it can affect the overall success of the company.
expectations: A focus on the needs of the customer
Willingness to go above and beyond for customers
Understanding of how customer service affects a company's success,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: Customer service is about going above and beyond for your customers. It's about making sure they're happy with your product or service and that they'll want to come back again.

Office Manager.question: Tell me a time when you had to say "no" to an employee and how did you handle it?
Office Manager.overview: An office manager is responsible for managing the performance of their staff. They should be able to provide direction and guidance to their employees while also being able to say "no" to requests that may not be in the best interest of the company. A good candidate will be able to provide an example of a time when they had to say "no" and how they handled it in a professional manner.
expectations: Ability to say "no" in a professional manner
Ability to provide direction and guidance
Willingness to take responsibility for their decisions,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I had an employee who was consistently coming in late and leaving early. I had to let him go because his performance was not up to par with the rest of the team. I explained my decision to him and he understood, but it was still a difficult situation.

Office Manager.question: How do you handle a bad situation?
Office Manager.overview: The best way to answer this question is to give an example of a time when you had to deal with a difficult situation. You should talk about how you handled the situation and what the outcome was.
expectations: Ability to think on their feet
Willingness to talk about a bad situation,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I had a situation where one of my employees was having trouble getting along with another member of the team. I sat down with both of them and explained that they needed to work together and resolve their issues. They came to an agreement and have been working well together since then.

Office Manager.question: What makes you think we should hire you?
Office Manager.overview: This is a great opportunity for the applicant to showcase their enthusiasm for the position and why they're the best person for the job. They should focus on how they can benefit the company and what skills they can bring to the table.
expectations: Focus on how they can benefit the company
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I'm very excited about this position and believe I have a lot to offer your company. I'm a hard worker and have a lot of experience working in an office environment. I'm sure I would be a great addition to your team.

Office Manager.question: How do you stay organized in a work environment?
Office Manager.overview: An office manager should be able to keep track of the many different tasks that need to be completed on a daily basis. A good candidate will be able to explain how they stay organized and how they make sure that their work is completed on time and according to company standards.
expectations: Ability to set and meet deadlines
Awareness of the importance of organization,
Office Manager.sampleAnswer: I'm very organized. I keep a calendar where I write down all my daily tasks and appointments. I also use a planner to keep track of my long-term goals and objectives.

Adult SLPs.question: Walk me through an Oral Motor exam.
Adult SLPs.overview: This question assesses your ability to conduct a thorough oral motor examination, a critical skill for SLPs working with patients who may have speech or swallowing disorders. The interviewer is looking for a step-by-step understanding and your ability to identify issues through the examination.
expectations: Detailed explanation of the steps involved in an oral motor exam Knowledge of what to look for during each step Ability to articulate how the findings guide treatment
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: When conducting an oral motor exam, I begin by assessing the patient's facial symmetry and muscle tone. Next, I evaluate the range of motion, strength, and coordination of the lips, tongue, and jaw by asking the patient to perform specific movements, such as smiling, sticking out their tongue, and opening and closing their mouth. I also assess the patient's ability to perform diadochokinetic tasks, such as rapidly repeating syllables like "pa-ta-ka." Additionally, I observe the patient's ability to manage secretions and assess their gag reflex. These observations help me determine the presence of any motor impairments that could affect speech and swallowing, guiding my treatment plan.

Adult SLPs.question: Walk me through a bedside swallow evaluation.
Adult SLPs.overview: This question examines your approach to evaluating swallowing function in a clinical setting without instrumental assessments. The interviewer wants to see your ability to observe and infer potential issues through a bedside examination.
expectations: Systematic approach to the evaluation Understanding of risk factors and red flags Explanation of how findings would influence your treatment recommendations
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: During a bedside swallow evaluation, I start by reviewing the patient’s medical history, paying close attention to any conditions that may impact swallowing. I then assess their level of alertness, posture, and ability to follow directions. I observe the patient’s oral hygiene and look for signs of dysphagia, such as drooling or coughing. I then introduce different food and liquid consistencies, starting with water and gradually moving to more complex textures. I carefully observe the patient’s ability to manage the bolus, swallow initiation, and any signs of aspiration, such as coughing or a wet vocal quality. Based on my findings, I might recommend further instrumental assessments or immediate dietary modifications.

Adult SLPs.question: What are your strengths?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question is an opportunity to highlight the key skills and attributes that make you a valuable addition to the team. The interviewer is looking for specific examples that demonstrate your strengths in practice.
expectations: Identification of relevant strengths Concrete examples illustrating these strengths Connection to the role you’re applying for
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: One of my key strengths is my ability to build strong rapport with patients, which I believe is essential in therapy. For example, I worked with a patient who initially resisted therapy, but through consistent communication and empathy, I was able to gain their trust, leading to significant improvements in their speech and swallowing. Additionally, I am highly organized, allowing me to manage a large caseload efficiently without compromising the quality of care. These strengths have consistently enabled me to achieve positive outcomes for my patients.

Adult SLPs.question: What are your weaknesses?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question requires self-reflection and honesty. The interviewer wants to see that you are aware of your areas for improvement and are actively working on them. It’s essential to frame your weakness in a way that shows growth potential.
expectations: Genuine acknowledgment of a weakness Explanation of steps taken to improve Positive spin or demonstration of growth
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: One area I’m continually working on is delegating tasks when I have a heavy caseload. Early in my career, I would try to manage everything myself, which sometimes led to burnout. I've since learned the importance of teamwork and have started collaborating more closely with assistants and other team members to ensure that all patients receive the best care without overwhelming myself. This change has not only improved my work-life balance but also enhanced the quality of patient care.

Adult SLPs.question: Why do you want to work in a rehab hospital?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question allows you to express your motivation for choosing this specific setting. The interviewer wants to understand your passion for rehab hospitals and how it aligns with your career goals
expectations: Clear reasoning for choosing a rehab hospital Connection between your skills and the setting Reflection on how this setting helps you achieve your professional goals
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: I’m drawn to working in a rehab hospital because I find the rehabilitation process incredibly rewarding. Seeing patients regain their independence and improve their quality of life is what motivates me. My experience with adult neurogenic populations has given me a solid foundation in managing complex cases, and I believe that the interdisciplinary approach in a rehab hospital will allow me to collaborate effectively with other professionals to provide comprehensive care. The dynamic and fast-paced environment also aligns with my desire for continuous learning and growth.

Adult SLPs.question: Walk me through a PMV assessment.
Adult SLPs.overview: This question assesses your knowledge and ability to perform a Passy-Muir Valve (PMV) assessment, a critical component for patients with tracheostomies. The interviewer is looking for a step-by-step explanation and your understanding of its significance.
expectations: Detailed explanation of the assessment steps Understanding of indications and contraindications Explanation of how the assessment impacts patient care
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: During a PMV assessment, I first review the patient's medical history and ensure that the tracheostomy tube is properly positioned and that the patient can tolerate cuff deflation. After obtaining medical clearance, I deflate the cuff and attach the Passy-Muir Valve to the tracheostomy tube. I closely monitor the patient’s breathing, vocal quality, and ability to manage secretions. If the patient demonstrates good tolerance, I assess their speech and swallowing functions while the valve is in place. The information gathered from this assessment helps guide decisions about the patient’s readiness for speaking, eating, and potentially decannulation.

Adult SLPs.question: Why would you recommend MBSS vs. FEES?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question tests your knowledge of instrumental swallowing assessments and your ability to choose the appropriate evaluation based on patient needs. The interviewer wants to understand your clinical decision-making process.
expectations: Understanding of the differences between MBSS and FEES Explanation of scenarios where one is preferred over the other Clinical reasoning behind your recommendation
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: I would recommend a Modified Barium Swallow Study (MBSS) when I need a comprehensive view of the entire swallowing process, especially the oral and esophageal phases, and when I want to observe the impact of various food consistencies on swallowing. MBSS is particularly useful for patients who may have esophageal involvement or when assessing the effectiveness of compensatory strategies. On the other hand, I would recommend FEES when a detailed view of pharyngeal structures is needed, or if the patient cannot tolerate transport to radiology for an MBSS. Both have their place in clinical practice, but I choose the study based on the patient’s specific needs and the questions I need answered.

Adult SLPs.question: Tell us about a time you gave advice or recommendations with which another healthcare professional disagreed.
Adult SLPs.overview: This question assesses your interpersonal and conflict resolution skills in a multidisciplinary team. The interviewer wants to see how you handle professional disagreements while maintaining patient-centered care.
expectations: Clear description of the situation Diplomatic handling of disagreement Focus on collaboration and patient outcomes
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: There was a situation where I recommended a specific diet modification for a patient with dysphagia, but the attending physician disagreed, believing the patient could handle a more advanced diet. I approached the disagreement by scheduling a meeting with the physician to discuss my concerns. I presented objective data from my assessment, including the patient’s risk of aspiration. Through open communication, we found a middle ground by agreeing to monitor the patient closely while trying a modified version of the recommended diet. Ultimately, the patient’s safety was prioritized, and our collaboration improved patient care.

Adult SLPs.question: Tell us about a patient you’ve had who has been challenging to work with. What did you do, and how might you have gone about things differently?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question examines your problem-solving skills and ability to reflect on past experiences. The interviewer is interested in how you handle difficult situations and what lessons you’ve learned.
expectations: Description of a challenging case Steps you took to address the situation Reflection on what you would do differently in the future
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: I once worked with a patient who was resistant to therapy due to frustration and fatigue following a stroke. Despite multiple attempts to engage them, progress was slow. I decided to modify my approach by incorporating their interests into therapy sessions, such as using music they enjoyed during speech exercises. This helped build rapport and eventually led to more active participation. However, in hindsight, I realize I could have involved the patient’s family earlier in the process to provide additional support and motivation. This experience taught me the importance of a holistic approach that includes family involvement from the beginning.

Adult SLPs.question: What does Post-Traumatic Amnesia tell you about a TBI?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question assesses your understanding of the relationship between post-traumatic amnesia (PTA) and traumatic brain injury (TBI). The interviewer is looking for knowledge of how PTA reflects the severity and recovery trajectory of a TBI and its implications for speech-language therapy.
expectations: Clear explanation of what post-traumatic amnesia is Understanding of its significance in TBI assessment and prognosis Connection to implications for therapy planning Awareness of how PTA duration correlates with recovery outcomes
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: Post-Traumatic Amnesia (PTA) is a critical indicator in assessing the severity of a traumatic brain injury. It refers to the period of confusion, disorientation, and memory loss following the injury, where the patient cannot form new memories. The duration of PTA often correlates with the severity of the TBI—longer PTA suggests a more severe injury and can indicate a more extended recovery process. In terms of therapy, understanding the duration and nature of PTA helps guide my approach, as it informs the level of cognitive support needed and influences how I structure therapy to accommodate memory and orientation deficits. Monitoring PTA also helps in setting realistic goals and expectations for the patient's recovery.

Adult SLPs.question: Have you had experience with Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS)?
Adult SLPs.overview: This question explores your familiarity with the Glasgow Coma Scale, a critical tool in assessing the level of consciousness in patients with head injuries. The interviewer wants to know if you can interpret GCS scores and use them to inform your therapeutic approach.
expectations: Demonstrated knowledge of the Glasgow Coma Scale and its components Experience using or interpreting GCS scores in a clinical setting Explanation of how GCS informs treatment planning Connection between GCS scores and the role of an SLP in managing TBI patients
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: Yes, I have experience with the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) from my work with TBI patients in both acute and rehab settings. The GCS is a valuable tool for assessing a patient's level of consciousness by scoring eye-opening, verbal response, and motor response. While I don’t administer the GCS myself, I often reference the scores to understand the severity of the injury and to guide my therapy approach. For instance, a lower GCS score might indicate the need for more intensive cognitive-linguistic support and gradual therapy progression, while a higher score could suggest that the patient is ready for more active participation in therapy. The GCS is also helpful for tracking recovery and adjusting treatment goals over time.

Adult SLPs.question: Tell me about your current training/job/caseload.
Adult SLPs.overview: This question allows the interviewer to gauge your current professional standing, the diversity of your experiences, and your ability to manage a varied caseload. It's also an opportunity to highlight any specialized training or unique experiences that make you a strong candidate.
expectations: Clear and concise description of your current role Overview of caseload diversity and management strategies Mention of any specialized training or certifications Reflection on how current experiences will benefit the potential role
Adult SLPs.sampleAnswer: In my current position as a Speech-Language Pathologist, I manage a diverse caseload that includes patients with a range of communication and swallowing disorders, predominantly adults in a post-acute setting. My training includes specialized certifications in dysphagia management and cognitive-communication disorders. I typically handle around 15-20 patients daily, balancing time between therapy sessions, evaluations, and team meetings. The complexity of cases, such as working with individuals who have had strokes or traumatic brain injuries, has refined my diagnostic and intervention skills. This experience will allow me to bring effective, evidence-based strategies to your team.

Dental Assistant.question: Why would you choose to work for Affordable Dentures and Implants?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question gives you an opportunity to learn about a candidate’s interest in the position and whether they’re a good fit for your office.
expectations: Desire to work for the company
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: Affordable Dentures and Implants is a well-established practice with a reputation for providing quality care. I’m impressed with the number of patients who have been treated by Dr. Smith and would be proud to work for such a reputable dentist.

Dental Assistant.question: Tell me about your self.
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine if a candidate has the ability to effectively communicate their personality, skills and experience. Answer this question by providing a brief overview of your background, highlighting your strengths and explaining why you are the best candidate for the job.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m a hardworking, dedicated dental assistant who has been in the field for five years. I’ve worked in two different offices and learned a lot from each experience. I’m looking for a new opportunity to further my career and I’m confident that I can make an immediate impact in your office.

Dental Assistant.question: Do you have all the credentials for this position?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant who is qualified for the job will have the necessary credentials. This question is designed to determine if a candidate has all the required certifications and licenses to perform the job.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: Yes, I have all the necessary certifications and licenses. I’m certified in CPR and first aid, I’m licensed as a dental assistant in the state of Florida and I’m certified in Dentrix.

Dental Assistant.question: What is your favorite procedure to assist the Doctor in during a Dental Procedure?
Dental Assistant.overview: Dental procedures can be long and tedious, so it’s important to find a candidate who can stay focused and maintain a positive attitude. This question will help you determine if a candidate is capable of remaining engaged and upbeat throughout the day.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I enjoy assisting the doctor with placing temporary fillings. It’s a short procedure that requires me to be quick and precise. I also enjoy assisting with placing crowns. The procedure is lengthy, but I enjoy being able to see the finished product at the end.

Dental Assistant.question: What can you bring to the company?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine if a candidate has a clear understanding of the company’s needs and how they can fulfill them.
expectations: Ability to fulfill the company’s needs
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’ve been working in the dental field for five years and have experience with all aspects of the profession. I’m a team player and am willing to take on any task that is required of me. I’m also computer literate and am proficient with Dentrix, which is the software used in your office.

Dental Assistant.question: Where do you see yourself in the next 5 years?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question gives you insight into a candidate’s career goals and how they plan to achieve them. A dental assistant who has a clear vision of their future will be more likely to remain with your practice.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’d like to become a dental hygienist. I’ve always had a passion for the field and would like to continue my education.

Dental Assistant.question: What is your biggest weakness?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate’s ability to identify and acknowledge their shortcomings. A dental assistant who can identify their weaknesses and explain how they plan to overcome them will be a valuable asset to your practice.
expectations: Ability to recognize and address shortcomings
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m a perfectionist. I want everything to be done right the first time and I’m not afraid to ask for help if I need it. I’ve learned that sometimes it’s better to ask for help than to try and do everything myself.

Dental Assistant.question: What will prevent you from coming into work?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine the candidate’s commitment to their job. A dental assistant who is unable to come into work due to illness or injury will be unable to complete their duties, causing the office to suffer.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m very dedicated to my job and will always make it a priority to come into work. If I’m sick, I’ll make sure to communicate with my manager so that they can find a replacement.

Dental Assistant.question: Why do you want to work for us?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine if a candidate has researched the company and understands the role. The candidate should be able to explain why they’re interested in the position, what they like about the company and how they can contribute to the organization.
expectations: Desire to work for this employer
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’ve been a fan of your practice for years. I’ve always admired your commitment to patient care and your dedication to providing quality dental care. I’m confident I can contribute to your team by helping you provide the best possible experience for your patients.

Dental Assistant.question: What are your strengths?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to help you learn more about the candidate’s personality and work ethic. Asking this question will help you determine if the candidate is a good fit for your office culture.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m a very organized person and I’m able to multitask well. I’m also very friendly and I enjoy helping others.

Dental Assistant.question: Why do you want to become a dental assistant?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant’s job is to assist the dentist in providing a positive patient experience. This question will help you determine if a candidate is interested in the profession and if they possess the necessary skills to succeed.
expectations: Desire to create a positive patient experience
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’ve always been interested in the dental field and I’m excited to learn more about the profession. I want to become a dental assistant because I enjoy helping people and I want to be part of a team that provides excellent care.

Dental Assistant.question: When are you available?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant’s availability is a key factor in the hiring process. A candidate who is available to work full-time, Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM, is more likely to be hired than someone who is only available part-time.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. I’m also willing to work weekends and evenings if needed.

Dental Assistant.question: What experience do you have in the dental profession?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question provides an opportunity to learn about a candidate’s experience in the dental field. Ask this question to determine how long they’ve been working in the industry, what type of work they’ve done and what they’ve learned from their past experiences.
expectations: Length of time in the field
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’ve been a dental assistant for five years. I started out as a receptionist and was promoted to dental assistant after three years. During my time in the field, I’ve worked in a variety of dental offices, including general dentistry, pediatric dentistry and orthodontics.

Dental Assistant.question: Why do you think you are a good fit for this position?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate’s enthusiasm for the position and their desire to work for your dental office.
expectations: Desire to work for your dental office
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m a dedicated and hardworking individual who is eager to learn and grow in my career. I’m confident that I can make a positive impact in your dental office.

Dental Assistant.question: When did you graduate from college?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is asked to determine the candidate’s level of commitment to their education. A dental assistant who graduated from college within the last two years will have a higher level of knowledge and skill than one who graduated ten years ago.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I graduated from college in May of 2018.

Dental Assistant.question: How would you resolve a conflict that occurred in the workplace?
Dental Assistant.overview: Conflicts can arise in any workplace, but a dental assistant who can resolve the issue quickly and effectively will improve the office environment. This question will help you determine if a candidate is capable of resolving conflicts in a professional manner.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would first try to resolve the issue by talking with the other party and explaining my point of view. If I feel the conversation isn’t going anywhere, I would bring in a third party to mediate. If that doesn’t work, I would take the issue up with my manager.

Dental Assistant.question: What was the most stressful situation you had in your last job?
Dental Assistant.overview: A stressful situation can arise at any time, but a candidate who can remain calm and think on their feet will be able to resolve the issue and maintain a positive attitude.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Ability to adapt to and manage stress
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I was working with a patient who was in extreme pain. I was able to quickly locate the source of the problem and schedule an appointment for treatment. However, the patient was in so much pain that they refused to wait for treatment. I had to call security to escort the patient out of the office.

Dental Assistant.question: What are your expectations?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine how a candidate will fit into the office culture. It’s important to understand how a candidate will work with others, their level of commitment and their overall personality.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m a dedicated and hardworking individual who is eager to learn and grow in the dental assisting field. I’m looking for a position where I can be challenged and learn new skills. I’m also looking for an office that is supportive of my professional development.

Dental Assistant.question: How many years of experience do you have in Dental Assisting?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine the candidate’s experience level and how they’ve grown professionally. The answer will also reveal what type of dental office they’re accustomed to working in and what type of work they’re most familiar with.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have three years of experience in a general dental practice. I’ve worked with a variety of patients, from children to seniors, and have assisted in all aspects of the practice, from cleanings to fillings.

Dental Assistant.question: How do you deal with mean patients?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant must be able to maintain a professional demeanor and remain calm in the face of adversity. This question will help you determine if a candidate is equipped to handle difficult patients and remain composed.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I always try to remain calm and professional. I listen carefully to what the patient is saying and try to understand their concerns. I then explain the dentist’s recommendations and why they are necessary. If the patient continues to be unruly, I will meet with the dentist in private to discuss the situation.

Dental Assistant.question: How would you handle a disrespectful patient who is adamant about not receiving the treatment recommended?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant who can effectively communicate with patients and resolve conflicts will improve the office environment and ensure a positive patient experience.
expectations: Ability to adapt to and manage stress
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would first ask the patient to explain their concerns. I would then explain the treatment plan and why it’s necessary. If the patient still refuses treatment, I would schedule a follow-up appointment to further discuss the situation.

Dental Assistant.question: How would your friends describe you?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is intended to learn more about the candidate’s personality and how they interact with others.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: My friends would describe me as a hard worker, a loyal friend and someone who is always willing to help.

Dental Assistant.question: What is something that you enjoyed at a job?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question will help you learn what a candidate values in their work environment. The answer will also give you insight into the candidate’s personality and work ethic.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I enjoyed working with my coworkers and the ability to work independently. I also enjoyed the flexibility of my schedule and the opportunity to work with a variety of patients.

Dental Assistant.question: What is your expected salary?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine if a candidate has a realistic expectation of the salary range for the position. It’s important to ensure you’re offering a competitive salary to attract the best talent.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m looking for a salary of $40,000 to $45,000 annually.

Dental Assistant.question: Why is it important to have a good relationship with your doctor?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant’s relationship with their doctor is vital to the success of the practice. A strong working relationship will ensure a smooth operation, increase productivity and improve patient satisfaction.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: A good relationship with my doctor is important because it allows me to work more efficiently. I can easily ask questions and get clarification on any issues I have. I can also provide feedback on how I think we can improve our office and patient experience.

Dental Assistant.question: Do you have any experience in denture?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant with experience in denture will be able to provide a more thorough explanation of the process and the steps involved. This question will help you determine if a candidate is familiar with the procedure and can provide you with a detailed description of their experience.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’ve had extensive experience in denture. I’ve worked with patients who have had partial and full dentures. I’ve also made dentures from scratch, including taking impressions and making wax models.

Dental Assistant.question: What does a team player mean to you?
Dental Assistant.overview: A team player is someone who is willing to go above and beyond to ensure the success of a dental office. This question will help you understand how a candidate will contribute to the overall success of your practice.
expectations: Willingness to work as part of a team
Ability to work well with others
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: A team player is someone who is willing to go above and beyond to ensure the success of a dental office. I’m always willing to pitch in and help wherever needed. I’ve been known to stay late or come in early if needed.

Dental Assistant.question: How would you explain to a parent that their child needs a root canal?
Dental Assistant.overview: A root canal is a dental procedure that requires a great deal of patience and understanding. This question will help you determine if a candidate can effectively communicate with patients and their families, especially in times of stress and anxiety.
expectations: Comfort level in discussing sensitive topics
Ability to remain calm under pressuref
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would first ask the parent if they have any questions about the procedure. Then, I would explain the reason for the treatment and what it entails. I would also discuss the benefits of having the procedure done now versus waiting until the tooth is more damaged.

Dental Assistant.question: Share an instance on how you worked well under stress.
Dental Assistant.overview: This question will help you determine how a candidate will perform under pressure. Stressful situations can occur in the workplace, such as a patient who is unhappy with their treatment, a dental emergency or a sudden influx of patients.
expectations: Ability to remain calm and focused
Ability to adapt to and manage stressf
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I was assisting a dentist with a root canal when the patient began to feel pain. The dentist was able to stop the procedure and give the patient medication to ease their discomfort. I remained calm and assisted the dentist with preparing for the next patient.

Dental Assistant.question: Are you willing to work full time?
Dental Assistant.overview: Dental assistants who are willing to work full-time hours will be more reliable and committed to the position. This question will help you determine if a candidate is willing to work the hours required for the job.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I am willing and able to work full-time hours. I am available Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. and can occasionally work Saturdays from 8 a.m. to noon.

Dental Assistant.question: Why are you leaving your current job?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to learn why a candidate is seeking a new position. It will help you understand if they are leaving to pursue a better opportunity, are unhappy with their current role or are seeking a change.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m leaving my current job because I’m looking for a position that offers more opportunities for growth and advancement. I’ve been with my current employer for five years and have learned everything I can from them. I’m ready to move on to the next step in my career.

Dental Assistant.question: How do you maintain patient privacy?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant must be aware of the importance of patient privacy and maintain confidentiality at all times. This question will help you determine if a candidate is aware of the importance of patient privacy and how they go about maintaining it.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I always keep the door closed when entering or exiting the operatory room. I also make sure to keep all patient information confidential by not discussing their treatment with anyone outside of the office.

Dental Assistant.question: What made you choose this profession?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to reveal a candidate’s motivation for pursuing a career in dental assisting. The answer will also provide insight into the candidate’s personality and work ethic.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I was drawn to this profession because I enjoy helping people feel better about themselves. I love the opportunity to work with patients of all ages and build relationships with them. I also enjoy working in a fast-paced environment where I can make a difference in someone’s life every day.

Dental Assistant.question: How would you explain a procedure to your parents?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question will help you determine if a candidate can effectively communicate with patients of all ages.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would explain the procedure by first explaining what the problem is and why it’s important to fix it. I would then explain how the dentist will fix it and what to expect when they return for their next appointment.

Dental Assistant.question: What is your experience?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to determine if a candidate has the necessary experience to perform the job. While a dental assistant’s level of experience will vary depending on the position, this question will help you determine if the candidate is qualified for the role.
expectations: Ability to adapt to and manage stress
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’ve been a dental assistant for five years and have worked in two different offices. I’ve gained experience in all aspects of the profession, including patient care, sterilization, record keeping and insurance billing.

Dental Assistant.question: What are your future goals?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question will help you determine if a candidate has a long-term career plan or is simply looking for a job.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’d like to become a dental hygienist in the next five years. I’m currently taking classes to earn my degree and I’m confident I’ll be able to achieve my goal.

Dental Assistant.question: How old are you?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is illegal to ask in many states and countries. However, if asked, you can use it to your advantage. If the candidate is too young, you can ask them if they are mature enough to handle the responsibilities of the job. If they are too old, you can ask them if they are willing to learn new technologies and techniques.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m 24 years old. I’ve been working in a dental office for five years and have been exposed to many different situations. I’m confident that I can handle the responsibilities of a dental assistant and am willing to learn new technologies and techniques.

Dental Assistant.question: How do you resolve conflicts in the dental office?
Dental Assistant.overview: Conflicts arise in every workplace, but a dental assistant who can resolve issues in a professional manner will improve office morale and ensure the practice runs smoothly.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I take a step back and assess the situation. If the conflict is between two patients, I ask them to step into the hallway so I can speak with them individually. I listen to both sides of the story and help them come to a resolution. If the conflict is between two employees, I bring them into the break room or schedule an appointment with the dentist to discuss their concerns.

Dental Assistant.question: What will you contribute to Multnomah County if hired?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to learn about a candidate’s personal and professional goals. It will help you understand how the candidate will add value to your dental office and what they hope to gain from the position.
expectations: How they will contribute to the team
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m looking for a dental assisting job that will allow me to grow professionally and personally. I want to be challenged and work with a team that is dedicated to providing exceptional patient care. I’m excited to join your team!

Dental Assistant.question: What was the most challenging situation you have ever encountered in your life and how did you deal with it?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question will help you determine how a candidate will handle stressful situations. A dental assistant who can remain composed and maintain a positive attitude will be able to effectively communicate with patients and co-workers when the pressure is on.
expectations: Ability to remain calm and composed
Ability to work well under pressure
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I was working at a dental office where the dentist was very demanding and critical of his staff. He would often yell at us for minor mistakes, which made me feel like I was constantly under a microscope. I learned to take his criticism with a grain of salt and focus on my work. I also learned to communicate with him in a professional manner, which helped me gain his respect.

Dental Assistant.question: What did you do when you made a mistake on your job?
Dental Assistant.overview: Mistakes are inevitable, but how a candidate handles the situation is what determines their success. This question will help you determine if a candidate is able to learn from their mistakes and take steps to prevent them from happening again.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I was working with a patient and accidentally dropped a tray of instruments. I apologized to the patient and immediately cleaned up the mess. I then went back to the office and cleaned the instruments, ensuring they were properly sterilized before returning them to their proper storage location.

Dental Assistant.question: What is your availability?
Dental Assistant.overview: A dental assistant’s schedule should be flexible enough to accommodate the needs of the office and the dentist. This question will help you determine if a candidate can work with your office’s schedule and be available for last-minute emergencies.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I’m available to work Monday through Friday from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm. I can also work some Saturdays and am willing to take on additional hours if needed.

Dental Assistant.question: What do you like most about being a dental assistant?
Dental Assistant.overview: A candidate’s answer to this question will reveal their passion for the profession and what they find most enjoyable about the job.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I love being a dental assistant because I get to work with patients and help them achieve a healthy smile. I enjoy educating patients on proper oral hygiene and showing them how easy it is to maintain their smile.

Dental Assistant.question: What is your greatest strength?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question is designed to help you determine if a candidate possesses the skills and abilities that will allow them to succeed in the role.
expectations: Ability to work in a team
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have excellent communication skills. I’m able to clearly explain procedures and answer questions in a way that is easy for patients to understand. I also have the ability to work well in a team, which is important because I’m often working with other dental professionals.

Dental Assistant.question: What was your most satisfying experience and or greatest achievement?
Dental Assistant.overview: This question will help you determine what a candidate finds most rewarding about their profession. It will also give you insight into their personality and how they view their role in the dental office.
Dental Assistant.sampleAnswer: My greatest achievement was when I was able to help a patient who had been in pain for years. I was able to successfully complete a root canal and restore the patient’s smile.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: An employer may ask this question to learn about your critical thinking and decision-making skills. When providing an answer for this question, you can talk about how you either asked for help or sought out information to help you make an informed decision. It will be helpful to use the STAR method when describing the situation.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: This is one of the most commonly asked interview questions. Be sure that you are speaking to your professional “self” when responding to this question. Rely on your resume as an outline to respond to this question. Give a brief outline of how you got to where you are at, and why you are passionate about the field that you are going into.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: The Healthcare Industry services many diverse populations and changing demographics require an understanding of diversity. Even if you are not an expert, be genuine and discuss your experiences with people of different cultures and/or training you may have received with your past employer(s). If you can, provide specific examples. If not, talk about how you would develop your multicultural awareness in order to provide the best service to the patient.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: This is a great opportunity to talk about your prioritization and organization skills. Discuss specific examples where possible, explaining your rationale. While summarizing, explain why one task is more important than another and how you effectively communicate with others.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: If you are new to healthcare, you may have just learned about HIPAA. These guidelines are extremely important, and it would be a good idea to brush up on them prior to going into an interview. To answer this question, you can discuss how you ensured the protocols were followed in a past role or, if you don’t have previous Healthcare experience, you can discuss the training you received on HIPAA from your program coursework.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: If you have prior Healthcare experience, talk about EMR/EHR. If not, expand on the training you received in your coursework. Talk about the electronic health records and how you applied those skills to a project or assignment. Feel free to add additional computer and technology skills, as well as your eagerness to learn any new programs and continually develop technology skills.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: We all have areas of development where we can grow. Think about a conversation where one of your areas of development was addressed. This could be something simple such as learning more about a subject area or new technology. Try to approach it from a positive light rather than talking about negative qualities such as tardiness, lack of organization, poor communication, etc. Once you identify an area of development, explain how you are working on developing and improving it.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: Provide an example and talk about how you maintained composure and handled the situation professionally. Discuss the steps you took (briefly) to achieve an outcome for both parties. Feel free to talk about something you learned from the conversation such as how to best approach a similar situation differently in the future, to improve the outcome one step further.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: This is a common interview question no matter what the industry is. It is structured as an open-ended question to allow you opportunity to showcase your skills. The employer NEEDS to learn about who you are and if your personality will fit with the team. Most people don’t feel comfortable bragging about themselves but in this question, the answer should include some great qualities you possess. Tell the employer concisely, how you will use your talents/passions to help the company succeed.

Medical Administrative Assistant.question: Can you describe a multicultural experience that was significant or meaningful to you?
Medical Administrative Assistant.sampleAnswer: Be prepared to address this type of question if it is asked. Do your research on what the salary range might be for the type of position that you are interviewing for and the city that you will be working in. Be sure to mention the salary RANGE and mention that your salary is negotiable based on the full compensation package.

Medical Assistant.question: What is customer service to you?
Medical Assistant.overview: Customer service is a huge part of a medical assistant's job. You want to know how the candidate views customer service and what they think it means to be a good customer service representative.
expectations: Ability to work in a team
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: Customer service is the ability to work with people and provide them with the best possible care. It's about making sure they are comfortable and have everything they need. It's about making sure they are satisfied with their visit and will come back again.

Medical Assistant.question: Why are you leaving your current job?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask to see if the candidate is honest and forthcoming. If they are leaving for a reason that is not positive, you may want to reconsider hiring them.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm leaving my current job because I'm looking for a new challenge. I've been working in the same office for the past three years and I'm ready for a change. I'm looking for a company that will challenge me and allow me to grow professionally.

Medical Assistant.question: How do you feel about working on a team?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question will give you a good idea of how the candidate feels about working with others.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have always been a team player. I have worked with groups in my training program, and I have worked on teams in my internship. I believe teamwork is the best way to get a job done.

Medical Assistant.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a classic interview question and can be a tricky one. You want to know what the candidate considers their strengths and weaknesses, but you don't want to hear them say they don't have any weaknesses.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I consider myself a hard worker and am always willing to go the extra mile to get the job done. I also consider myself a good listener and am able to communicate well with others. My only weakness is that I can be a bit of a perfectionist at times.

Medical Assistant.question: Tell me about your self.
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a standard question that will give you a chance to get to know the candidate.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very outgoing person who loves to be around people. I'm very friendly and enjoy helping others. I'm a hard worker and will always do my best to get the job done.

Medical Assistant.question: What is your biggest weakness?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a classic interview question, but it's important to know what a candidate's biggest weakness is. It's important to know if they are aware of their weaknesses and how they plan to improve upon them.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: My biggest weakness is my ability to multi-task. I'm a very focused individual and can get easily distracted when I have too many things going on at once. I've learned to be more aware of my surroundings and how I can better manage my time.

Medical Assistant.question: How do you build trust with your managers and coworkers?
Medical Assistant.overview: Trust is a very important part of any working relationship. You want to know how a candidate builds trust with their managers and coworkers.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very open person and I like to be upfront with my coworkers. I think that's the best way to build trust. I also try to be a team player and work well with others. I'm always willing to help out and pitch in wherever needed.

Medical Assistant.question: Where are you interested in working?
Medical Assistant.overview: It's important to know where the candidate is looking to work. If they are looking for a specific location, it's good to know if you have an office in that area.
expectations: Interest in working with your company
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a job in the area of my internship. I really enjoyed working with the pediatrician's office and would like to continue working with children.

Medical Assistant.question: What was the biggest challenge you faced?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to find out what challenges the candidate faced in their past jobs and how they dealt with them.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: The biggest challenge I faced was when I was placed on a new team at my internship. I had to learn how to work with new people and adapt to a new environment. I was able to overcome this challenge by working hard and being open to learning from my coworkers.

Medical Assistant.question: Why do you want to work for us?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask because it will give you an idea of how well the candidate knows your company.
expectations: Why they want to work for you
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I've been a fan of your company for years. I've always been impressed with the work you do and the way you treat your clients. I've been following your company for years and have always wanted to work for you.

Medical Assistant.question: How do you handle pressure?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question will give you a sense of the candidate's ability to handle pressure.
expectations: Ability to work in a fast-paced environment
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very organized person, and I'm good at handling pressure. I've always been able to juggle multiple tasks at once, and I'm comfortable working in a fast-paced environment.

Medical Assistant.question: How long have you been a medical assistant?
Medical Assistant.overview: It's important to know how long a candidate has been a medical assistant. They may have just finished their training and only have internship experience so will need to decide if they are a good fit for you in other ways.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I've served as an intern as past of my medical assistant program. I just completed my program in June, and at the conclusion of my year of training, I was placed in a pediatrician's office as an intern. I shadowed and worked with the other medical assistants in the office, and I can say my time there really reaffirmed my belief that this is the right profession for me.

Medical Assistant.question: How do you deal with challenges?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates react to challenges and how they deal with them.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I've found that the best way to deal with challenges is to face them head on. If I'm having trouble with a task, I'll ask for help or try a different approach. I'm always willing to learn new things, so I'm always open to suggestions.

Medical Assistant.question: What would you do if a patient fainted?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question will give you a sense of how the candidate would handle a common medical emergency.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would call for help immediately and check the patient's pulse and breathing. If they were breathing, I would lay them down and elevate their feet. If they were not breathing, I would begin CPR.

Medical Assistant.question: How would you handle a difficult patient?
Medical Assistant.overview: Candidates should be able to talk about how they would handle a difficult patient.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would do my best to diffuse the situation. I would try to calm the patient down and explain to them that I was only trying to help. I would also try to get another medical assistant or the doctor involved in the situation.

Medical Assistant.question: Tell me about a time when you and your coworker didn't get along.
Medical Assistant.overview: This question will help you determine how well a candidate can work with others.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I had a coworker who was very negative and would complain about everything. I tried to work with her, but she was always negative and made me feel like I couldn't do anything right. I eventually had to go to my boss and ask that she be moved to another department.

Medical Assistant.question: Why did you apply to this position?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask because it will help you understand if the candidate is truly interested in the position or if they are just applying to every job they can find.
expectations: Why they are a good fit for the position
Why they would be a good fit for your company
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I really enjoy working with people and helping them. I feel that this position would allow me to do just that. I've been a medical assistant for two years and have learned a lot about the profession. I feel that my experience would make me a great fit for this position.

Medical Assistant.question: Tell us about a time when you had to deal with a difficult co-worker or patient.
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to see how candidates deal with difficult situations. You want to see if they can remain calm and professional when dealing with a difficult person.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I had a situation with a patient who was very upset. She was yelling at me and the other medical assistant in the room. I remained calm and did my best to help her understand what we were doing and why. I was able to get her to calm down and she was able to understand what we were doing.

Medical Assistant.question: If we were to call your current manager, what is something negative they would say about you?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to see how candidates handle criticism. You want to see if they can take it in stride and learn from it, or if they get defensive and try to explain away the criticism.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm sure my manager would say that I'm a little too hard on myself sometimes. I know I can do better and I always strive to do my best. I think that's a good quality, but it can be frustrating when you're not satisfied with your work.

Medical Assistant.question: What do you know about McLeod?
Medical Assistant.overview: It's always good to know what a candidate knows about your company. This question will give you a chance to see if they've done their research and know about your company.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I know that McLeod is a large company that has been in business for over 50 years. I know that you have a large presence in the medical community and that you are well respected.

Medical Assistant.question: How would you describe your experience?
Medical Assistant.overview: Candidates may have a lot of experience or they may be new to the field. Find out how much experience they have and what kind of work they've done.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have a lot of experience in medical assisting. I completed my training program in June and have been working in a pediatrician's office since then. I've been doing everything from taking vital signs to assisting with physicals and immunizations. I've also had the chance to work with patients of all ages, so I'm comfortable working with children and adults alike.

Medical Assistant.question: What was your biggest mistake in the previous externship and how did you try to fix it?
Medical Assistant.overview: You want to know how the candidate handled a mistake. Did they own up to it? Did they try to fix it? Did they learn from it?
expectations: Ability to own up to mistake
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I was assigned to work with a physician who had a very specific way of doing things. I was not aware of his preferences and made the mistake of not asking him how he wanted his charts organized. He was very clear in his instructions, and I took the time to ask him how he wanted things done in the future.

Medical Assistant.question: Why do you think you are a good fit for this position?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great opportunity for the candidate to sell themselves. You want to hear how they can contribute to your company and what they can do for you.
expectations: Why they are a good fit
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very hard worker and I'm always looking for ways to improve my skills. I've been told that I'm a quick learner and that I'm very personable. I think I'd be a great fit for this position because I really enjoy working with people and I'm very dedicated to my work.

Medical Assistant.question: What would you do if the physician asked you to do something not in your job description and you are forbidded to do it?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask to see how the candidate will handle a situation that may arise. You want to know if they will try to do the job anyway or if they will follow the rules.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would ask the physician if I could help in some way. If he or she still wanted me to do the job, I would do it. If not, I would ask if there was another task I could help with.

Medical Assistant.question: What are some commonly prescribed medications?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask because it will help you gauge how much experience the candidate has with common medications.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: Commonly prescribed medications include antibiotics, pain relievers and cold medicine. I've been trained on all of these medications and have experience with them in my internship. I was also trained on common illnesses and how to treat them.

Medical Assistant.question: What is the most difficult obstacle you have encountered in your worklife and how did you overcome it?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask candidates to see how they handle challenges. It's important to know how they respond to difficult situations and how they work through them.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I had a difficult time with my first patient at my internship. I was nervous and was not sure what to do. I was able to talk with my supervisor and she gave me some pointers on how to handle the situation. I was able to go back and complete the task successfully.

Medical Assistant.question: What makes you think that you would be a good fit here?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to see how well the candidate understands the company and the position. If they can't come up with a good answer, it's a red flag.
expectations: Why they would be a good fit
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I think I would be a great fit here because I have a strong work ethic and I'm very detail oriented. I'm very comfortable with medical terminology and I'm very familiar with medical office procedures. I've been told that I'm a great team player and that I have a positive attitude.

Medical Assistant.question: Tell me about a time when you disagreed with your manager's decision.
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to see how candidates handle conflict. You want to know if they can work well with others and if they can stand up for themselves.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I had a disagreement with my manager at my internship. I was working with a patient who was very sick and had a lot of medical issues. I felt that the patient needed to be seen by a doctor right away, but my manager disagreed. We had a discussion about the situation and I was able to convince her that the patient needed to be seen right away.

Medical Assistant.question: Which department would you like to work in?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to see if the candidate has done their homework and researched your company. It's also a good way to see if they are a good fit for your company.
expectations: Desire to work in a specific department
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would love to work in the lab. I've always been interested in the medical field and I've heard that the lab is a great place to work. I know that you have a lab on site, so I'm really interested in working there.

Medical Assistant.question: What was the most difficult situation you have faced?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to find out how a candidate reacts to stressful situations.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I had a patient who was very ill and needed to be admitted to the hospital. I was able to get her there quickly, and she was able to get the care she needed. It was a stressful situation, but I was able to keep my cool and do what needed to be done.

Medical Assistant.question: What do you know about Planned Parenthood?
Medical Assistant.overview: You want to know if the candidate has any knowledge of Planned Parenthood and what they do.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have heard of Planned Parenthood, but I don't know much about them. I will be happy to learn more about their services and how they can help women.

Medical Assistant.question: What is your expected salary?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a question that is asked to see if the candidate is willing to negotiate.
expectations: Ability to ask for a higher salary
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm looking for a salary of $45,000 a year.

Medical Assistant.question: How do you handle stress?
Medical Assistant.overview: Stress is a part of the job, so you want to know how the candidate reacts to it.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I'm a very organized person, so I find that when I'm faced with a stressful situation, I can take a step back and look at the situation from a different angle. I've learned to take a deep breath and think things through before making any rash decisions.

Medical Assistant.question: What is customer service to you?
How do you manage your time?
Medical Assistant.overview: This question is a great way to see how well a candidate can prioritize their tasks and manage their time.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I am very good at managing my time. I'm able to prioritize my tasks and get them done in a timely manner. In my training program, we were assigned a number of tasks each day, and I was able to complete all of them on time. In my internship, I was able to complete my tasks in a timely manner as well.

Medical Assistant.question: What are your goals in the next 5 years?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to ask to see if the candidate is interested in growing with your company.
expectations: Desire to grow with your company
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I would like to continue to grow in my career and eventually become a medical assistant manager. I love working with patients and helping them get better, so I would like to be able to help other medical assistants succeed as well.

Medical Assistant.question: What was one time you had a conflict with someone and how did you handle it?
Medical Assistant.overview: This is a great question to see how a candidate deals with conflict. It's important to know how they will handle it if they are working with you and someone else in the office.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I had a conflict with one of my classmates in my training program. We were both working on the same project and I was given the task of creating a PowerPoint presentation. I was working on it for hours and my classmate came in and took over, claiming she could do it better than me. I was upset, but I realized she was right and let her take over. She ended up doing a great job, and we worked together on the project.

Medical Assistant.question: How will you handle a situation where there is a conflict between you and another employee?
Medical Assistant.overview: Conflicts between employees can be a big problem in the workplace. You want to know how the candidate will handle a situation where they are in conflict with another employee.
expectations: Ability to work in a team
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have never had a conflict with another employee, but I am sure I would handle it professionally. I would talk to the other employee and try to come to an understanding. If that doesn't work, I would talk to my supervisor about the issue.

Medical Assistant.question: How do you handle unhappy customers?
Medical Assistant.overview: As a medical assistant, you will be dealing with unhappy patients. You want to know how a candidate will handle an unhappy patient and how they will handle the situation.
Medical Assistant.sampleAnswer: I have had the opportunity to deal with unhappy customers in my internship. I was able to talk with the patients and their families and explain what was going on. I was also able to talk with the doctors and nurses about the patients' concerns and relay that information back to the patients.

Medical Assistant.question: How many years of customer service experience do you have?
Medical Assistant.overview: If the candidate has customer service experience, ask them to describe their duties and responsibilities.
