Data Analyst.question: Have you ever had a difficult boss and how did you deal with them?
Data Analyst.overview: This question is designed to see how candidates handle difficult situations. It also gives you insight into how they view their bosses.
expectations: Ability to see the big picture
Ability to work well with others
Data Analyst.sampleAnswer: I've had a few difficult bosses in my career. The first was when I was a junior analyst and the second was when I was a senior analyst. In both cases, I tried to understand where they were coming from and what they wanted. I also tried to be as helpful as possible and to anticipate their needs.

Data Analyst.question: How will you sort lines in a txt file by one of the columns using shell scripting?
Data Analyst.overview: This question is a good way to assess how well candidates can think on their feet and how well they can communicate.
expectations: Ability to explain process with clarity
Ability to explain process with clarity and brevity
Data Analyst.sampleAnswer: I would use the sort command to sort the lines by the column I want. I would use the cut command to cut out the column I want and then use the paste command to paste it into a new file.

Data Analyst.question: What are your interests?
Data Analyst.overview: This question is a way to get to know the candidate better. It also helps you assess if the candidate will fit in with the rest of the team.
expectations: Ability to work well with others
Data Analyst.sampleAnswer: I love to travel. I've been to Europe, Asia and Africa. I also love to read. I'm currently reading "The Art of War" by Sun Tzu.

Data Analyst.question: Tell me about your previous role.
Data Analyst.overview: This question is a standard for data analyst interviews. It gives you a chance to see how well candidates can communicate. It also lets you see how well they can talk about themselves and their accomplishments.
Data Analyst.sampleAnswer: I was a data analyst at HTWW Company. I worked with a team of five people to collect and analyze data for the company's environmental impact study. I was responsible for collecting and cleaning the data, and then creating tables and graphs in Excel. I also did some data mining to find correlations between the data.

Data Scientist.question: What are some of the assumptions required to accurately perform a linear regression analysis?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate's knowledge of linear regression and their ability to explain the necessary assumptions for it.
expectations: Identify and list the key assumptions Explain why each assumption is necessary
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Some of the key assumptions for linear regression are linearity, independence, homoscedasticity, normality, and no multicollinearity. These assumptions ensure the model is unbiased, consistent, and efficient in estimating the relationship between variables.

Data Scientist.question: What is a decision tree, and how do you use this in your job as a data scientist?
Data Scientist.overview: The interviewer wants to know if you're familiar with decision trees and how you utilize them in your role as a data scientist.
expectations: Define what a decision tree is and what is it used for Provide an example of how you have used it
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: A decision tree is a graphical representation that breaks down decisions into a series of questions and possible outcomes. It's commonly used in classification tasks where the output is a discrete class. In my previous job, we used decision trees to predict customer churn. We first trained the model using historical data, and then used it to predict the probability of churn for new customers. Decision trees are easy to interpret and can handle a mix of categorical and continuous variables, but they can be prone to overfitting and are sensitive to small changes in the data.

Data Scientist.question: How do you stay current with the latest developments and advancements in the field of data science, and how do you determine which developments are worth investing time and resources into?
Data Scientist.overview: This is a behavioral question that aims to understand how a data scientist stays up-to-date with the latest trends and developments in the field of data science. The interviewer wants to see if the candidate is proactive in learning and growing as a data scientist.
expectations: Discuss latest advancements in the field of data science Mention relevant resources and methods for staying informed
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: I stay up-to-date with the latest developments and advancements in the field of data science by attending industry conferences, following relevant publications, and participating in online data science communities. I prioritize those developments that align with the organization's goals and objectives, as well as those that have the potential to improve the efficiency and accuracy of our data-driven processes.

Data Scientist.question: What data visualization tools do you have experience using? Which one is your favorite to use and why?
Data Scientist.overview: This question is asked to determine your familiarity with different data visualization tools and your experience using them. The interviewer is interested in understanding which tools you prefer to use and your reasoning behind your choice.
expectations: Discuss about data visualization tools and their features Articulate the strengths of your preferred tool
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: I have experience using Tableau, Power BI, and QlikView. Although I have used all three tools, my favorite tool to use is Tableau. The reason I prefer Tableau is that it has a wide range of visualization options, is user-friendly, and has robust data connection options. Additionally, it provides more advanced features for data blending and joining, which I have found to be useful for complex data analysis tasks.

Data Scientist.question: What inspired you to pursue a career in data science, and what motivates you to continue working in this field?
Data Scientist.overview: This is a behavioral interview question that aims to understand your motivation and interest in the field of data science.
expectations: Discuss about what inspired you to pursue a career in data science Reasons that keep you motivated to continue a career in this field
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: I was always fascinated by numbers and their ability to reveal hidden patterns and insights. During my undergraduate studies, I took a course in data analysis, and that's when I discovered the power of data science in solving complex business problems. I find it gratifying to use data-driven insights to drive decision-making and bring value to the organization. The potential to make an impact through data analysis and the constant learning opportunities in this field keep me motivated to continue working in data science.

Data Scientist.question: Which algorithm is used to generate recommendations for customers based on purchase history?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of collaborative filtering and machine learning.
expectations: Knowledge of building recommendation engines Basic knowledge of machine learning algorithms
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: A recommendation engine can be generated by utilizing collaborative filtering which explains user behaviors and their purchasing patterns in terms of ratings, selection, and other factors. This way, by using the preferences of other users as the basis, the engine predicts what might appeal to a particular user.

Data Scientist.question: Can you compare SAS, R, and Python programming tools and describe their use in Data Science?
Data Scientist.overview: This is a technical question that requires you to compare three programming languages and their uses in data science. It is an opportunity for you to showcase your technical knowledge and expertise in data science.
expectations: Provide a clear comparison of the three programming languages Discuss their strengths and weaknesses in data science
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: SAS is a proprietary language used primarily for data analysis and visualization. R is an open-source language that offers a wide range of statistical and graphical techniques, making it very useful for data exploration and visualization. Python, on the other hand, is a general-purpose programming language with a strong focus on data analysis and machine learning. It offers a vast range of libraries, including Pandas and NumPy, which make it easy to work with large data sets. In terms of their use in data science, R is great for exploratory data analysis and visualization, SAS is ideal for statistical modeling and analysis, and Python is widely used for machine learning and deep learning.

Data Scientist.question: What is data cleansing and why is it important for a data scientist?
Data Scientist.overview: The interviewer wants to know if you are familiar with data cleansing, its significance, and how it affects the quality of the results in a data science project.
expectations: Define data cleansing and explain its importance Provide examples of your experience with data cleansing
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Data cleansing is the process of identifying and correcting or removing errors and inconsistencies in a dataset to improve its quality. As a data scientist, it's important to clean data before analyzing it to ensure accuracy in the results. This process includes handling missing values, identifying and correcting duplicate or incorrect data entries, and standardizing data formats. For example, in a recent project, I cleaned a large dataset by removing duplicate values, correcting incorrect entries, and replacing missing data with the median or mean values. This led to more accurate results and improved the overall quality of the analysis.

Data Scientist.question: Can you define cross-validation and describe how you use this process when analyzing a data set?
Data Scientist.overview: This is a technical question asking for both the definition of the term and an explanation of how you use it in your work as a data scientist.
expectations: Describe cross-validation and why it is important Discuss your practical experience with the technique
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: As a data scientist, I use cross-validation to assess how well the analysis model I am using will perform on a new and independent dataset. A typical way to use cross-validation is to split the data into two sets. You then use one data set to build the model and the second one to test your analysis. This helps to improve the accuracy of and my trust in the results of the analysis.

Data Scientist.question: What statistical software programs do you have experience using in past positions in this field? Which one do have you the most experience with or feel the most confident using?
Data Scientist.overview: The question is about the data analytics software the candidate has experience with, and their ability to adapt to new software.
expectations: Provide details around what software you've worked with Discuss your ability to work with different software
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: I have experience working with Tableau, Statgraphics, and JMP Statistical Software. Additionally, I have worked with Salesforce Analytics Cloud and MATLAB in previous roles. I find it relatively easy to transition to new analytics software because of the similarities in features and user interfaces between the different packages.

Data Scientist.question: What are some of the differences between a histogram and a box plot?
Data Scientist.overview: The interviewer is asking a technical question, seeking your knowledge and ability to compare different types of visual models used to analyze data. Your answer should be brief and to the point.
expectations: State the differences between a histogram and a box plot Provide an example of how each is used in data analysis
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: So, boxplots and histograms are both used to illustrate a data distribution that communicates information in different ways. Histograms are bar charts that illustrate the frequency of a numerical variable's values. While boxplots do not illustrate the shape of the distribution, they enable us to view information such as the quartiles, the range, and outliers.

Data Scientist.question: Can you discuss some of the weaknesses of a linear analysis model?
Data Scientist.overview: The interviewer is looking to assess your knowledge of linear analysis models and your ability to provide a balanced view of their strengths and weaknesses.
expectations: Describe the weaknesses of a linear analysis model Highlight the impact of these limitations
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Sure. A primary issue is that the model makes strong assumptions that may not apply to the specific data set. Secondly, the linear analysis model assumes normality between variables, minimal multicollinearity, homoscedasticity, and a linear relationship. Also, it cannot be used for binary or discrete outcomes. Despite these limitations, the linear analysis model can be very useful when used appropriately.

Data Scientist.question: Describe to me your experience with machine learning methods. Is there a particular method you have more experience with than others?
Data Scientist.overview: This question aims to assess the candidate's knowledge and experience with machine learning methods.
expectations: Discuss your machine learning experiences Provide your preferred machine learning method and the rationale behind it
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Since most of my work was focused on filtering spam within the email application we developed, I utilized the Classification methodology of machine learning, specifically the NaiveBayes algorithm. This allowed us to address the large data set we used for training and the multiple attributes we filtered for.

Data Scientist.question: Data visualization is an important skill that will be used often when communicating results with stakeholders. Describe to me one of your most innovative data visualization ideas that went beyond pie and bar charts.
Data Scientist.overview: The question seeks to understand how you present complex data with innovative ideas in a manner that is easy to understand and utilize.
expectations: Discuss an idea that you implemented in the past Explain how you used them to achieve a clear understanding of the results
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: I always keep in mind the stakeholders' objectives when presenting my data analysis results. I often use visual representations of the data along with the actual numbers. In a recent study on the implementation of process improvement and the results it generated, I used a photo of the actual production line, and animated it. As the process improved, I increased the speed of the line, and reduced the production times, adding actual percentages of the time saved above the line. This helped the management team easily understand the results which were achieved, and they were able to utilize the information effectively.

Data Scientist.question: Is it better to use many small decision trees or one large decision tree?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate's understanding of decision tree models and their ability to explain the advantages and disadvantages of using small or large decision trees.
expectations: Identify the preferred decision tree model Provide a rationale for your choice
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: In my opinion, one large decision tree is usually more accurate than many small decision trees. Small decision trees can be limited in options and may not fit the problem well. On the other hand, a larger decision tree model with multiple options and a clear direction can provide a more accurate decision process model. I would aim to create a decision tree model that looks more like a forest with distinct branches to navigate through different scenarios. However, the size of the decision tree model should be appropriate to the data set and should be evaluated for overfitting.

Data Scientist.question: Explain how you calculate accuracy using a confusion matrix.
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s technical knowledge of the accuracy formula and its use in the confusion matrix.
expectations: Formula for accuracy Basic knowledge of the concept of the confusion matrix
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: We can calculate accuracy by dividing the sum of true positives and negative positives by the sum of all entries of the confusion matrix or total observations.

Data Scientist.question: What is the importance of the P-value?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of the P value and its uses.
expectations: Definition of P-value Knowledge of the advantages of P-value
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: In statistics, the P value refers to the probability of a specific statistical model that is equal to or more extreme than the observed results when the null hypothesis is true. Its significance lies in its use to evaluate the importance of observational data. There is always a chance that a correlation between two variables that researchers find to be apparent could simply be a coincidence. To ascertain whether the observed relationship could be the result of chance, a p-value calculation is used.

Data Scientist.question: In a linear regression model, how do you find the RMSE and MSE?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of linear regression models and techniques to find mean square errors.
expectations: Definition and fullform of RMSE and MSE Knowledge of mean square error techniques
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: RMSE is calculated by taking the square root of MSE. RMSE is known as Root Mean Square Deviation and it measures the average magnitude of the errors that are concerned with the deviations from the actual value. The target variable's square is used to measure MSE, while the target variable itself is used to measure RMSE. MSE effectively penalizes larger errors more severely because of the way it is constructed, just like the squared loss function from which it derives.

Data Scientist.question: What are dimensionality reduction and its benefits?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of dimensionality reduction in converting datasets.
expectations: Definition of dimensionality reduction Ability to explain its benefits
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: The transformation of a data set with many dimensions into data with few dimensions (fields) in order to communicate similar information succinctly is referred to as dimensionality reduction. The benefits of dimensionality reduction include improved data compression, reduced storage space and computation time, decreased computing time, and removal of redundant features.

Data Scientist.question: What are the feature selection methods that are used to select the right variables?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of feature selection methods and variables in machine learning.
expectations: Knowledge of feature selection methods Ability to choose the right variables
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: There are several feature selection methods that can be used depending on the dataset, the problem at hand, and the type of model being used. It is often necessary to try different methods and evaluate their performance to determine the most suitable one for a given problem. Some of the feature selection methods include filter, wrapper, embedded, Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), and tree-based methods.

Data Scientist.question: How do you carry out logistic regression?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of logistic regression and related techniques.
expectations: Definition of logistic regression Ability to carry out logistic regression
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Logistic regression is a statistical technique used to model the relationship between a binary response variable (such as yes/no, 0/1) and one or more predictor variables. The logistic regression model estimates the relationship between the predictor variables and the outcome variable. This is done by fitting a logistic function to the observed data, which gives the probability of the outcome being in one category (e.g., "yes") versus another (e.g., "no") as a function of the predictor variables. Maximum likelihood estimation is used to find parameter values that will maximize the likelihood of the observed data given the model. After fitting, it can be utilized to make predictions on new data by plugging in values for predictors and calculating its associated probability of belonging to each category.

Data Scientist.question: In your opinion, is mean square error a good or bad measure of model performance?
Data Scientist.overview: This question gives recruiters clarity on the candidate’s area of expertise and preferred way of conducting model performance.
expectations: Knowledge of model testing procedures Ability to gauge the better option
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: In my opinion, using the mean square error, or MSE, as a measure of a decision model's performance is flawed. The problem is that it weights larger errors more than smaller ones. Thus, the large deviations in the data are given greater weight. As a result, I prefer using mean absolute deviation, or MAE, which is a more robust model and provides a more accurate measure of a model's performance.

Data Scientist.question: How do you use data analysis to benefit the company?
Data Scientist.overview: This question evaluates the candidate’s knowledge of data analysis and its benefits.
expectations: Knowledge of data analysis Knowledge of its benefits
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: One of the most important uses of data analysis is to drive growth and improve performance. To use data analysis to benefit the company, I typically follow a structured process that involves several steps. The first step is to collaborate with stakeholders to identify key business questions. I then gather and clean relevant data sources by using SQL query databases and tools like Excel or Python. Followed by this, I apply various statistical methods and visualization tools to identify trends, patterns, and insights by building predictive models or using dashboards to visualize key metrics. Finally, I communicate the findings to stakeholders to help them make informed, data-backed decisions and mitigate risks.

Data Scientist.question: Before applying machine learning algorithms to your data, do you wrangle and clean the data?
Data Scientist.overview: This is an operational question asked by recruiters to learn more about how the candidate executes everyday tasks like wrangling and cleaning data.
expectations: Knowledge of data wrangling and cleaning Ability to ensure that the data sets are appropriate for analysis
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: It is essential to perform both data wrangling and data cleaning before applying machine learning algorithms. By doing this, I will ensure that the data set fits my analysis, that their standard deviations meet the guidelines for the study, that their relationships are valid, and that the data is normalized and standardized. As a result, I eliminate outliers and variables that could potentially affect my results.

Data Scientist.question: How can you use statistics to analyze data and develop business recommendations?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of statistical techniques and their application at various stages of the data analysis process.
expectations: Knowledge of statistical techniques Ability to apply those techniques during data analysis Ability to derive business recommendations by analyzing data
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: There are many statistical techniques that can be used to analyze data and derive business recommendations. The first step is to identify the business problems and the data that will be used to analyze and solve the problem. Followed by that, the data needs to be cleaned and processed to ensure the accuracy of the analysis. The third step is to conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA) which includes summarizing the main characteristics of the data, such as central tendency, dispersion, and shape. This helps in identifying patterns, relationships, and trends in the data. Based on the EDA, appropriate statistical models can be selected to analyze the data. The choice of model depends on the type of data and the research question. After analyzing the data, the final step is to interpret the results in the context of the business problem. Business recommendations can be then developed based on the insights gained from the analysis.

Data Scientist.question: How do you ensure that a regression model fits the data?
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of regression analysis and model validation techniques.
expectations: Uses of regression models Knowledge of regression analysis Knowledge of model validation techniques
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: You can ensure that a regression model fits the data through graphical residual analysis. The residual plots from a fitted model provide information regarding the adequacy of different aspects of the model. R2 statistics is another numerical method for model validation that is also useful, but to a lesser extent than graphical methods. Model validation using graphic methods is advantageous over numerical methods because they are capable of illustrating a wide range of complex aspects of the model-data relationship. Most numerical methods for model validation focus on a particular aspect of the relationship between the model and the data and attempt to condense that information into a single descriptive number or test result.

Data Scientist.question: Explain the difference between supervised and unsupervised learning.
Data Scientist.overview: This question tests the candidate’s knowledge of machine learning, data classifications, and dataset relationship.
expectations: Definition of supervised and unsupervised learning Ability to differentiate between the two
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Supervised machine learning is used to classify data and/or make predictions, while unsupervised learning is used to analyze relationships within datasets. The former is used in logistic regression, linear regression, decision trees, and support vector machine while the common uses for unsupervised learning include semantic clustering, market basket analysis, recommender systems, etc.

Data Scientist.question: Describe a time when you think you made a significant impact on the company’s strategy development process as a data scientist. Explain your role and contribution.
Data Scientist.overview: This question assesses the candidate's ability to contribute to the company’s business objectives through their role.
expectations: Specific examples and quantified achievements Understanding of the role Previous contributions
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: In my previous role, I was involved in a crucial prototyping project for developing user-centric software products for the company. To help the stakeholders finalize the best software products that the company could capitalize on, I conducted thorough customer & market requirement analysis, competitive research, and trends analysis. This allowed stakeholders to make an informed, data-backed decision about the product choice which went on to generate a revenue of 500 crores in the first quarter.

Data Scientist.question: Describe a project where you faced difficulty working with unstructured data. How did you resolve the bottlenecks and which tools did you use?
Data Scientist.overview: This question shows the candidate’s experience in working with unstructured data and their problem-solving skills.
expectations: Experience with unstructured data Problem-solving skills Familiarity with tools
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: Recently, I worked on a project where I was tasked with helping the sales team improve its customer relationship management process. But the long waiting period required for detecting new and changed data led to some delays. Then to expedite the process, I utilized a combination of FastScan Data Discovery, NoSQL database, and Amazon's Simple Storage Service (S3) to collect and analyze the data for producing the desired results before the deadline.

Data Scientist.question: What experience do you have conducting text analytics? Describe a project you worked on that required text analytics.
Data Scientist.overview: The interviewer wants to know if the candidate has worked on projects that require text analytics, and how they used their skills to achieve project goals.
expectations: Define your experience in conducting text analytics Explain how you have applied it to a project
Data Scientist.sampleAnswer: In my previous role, I worked on a project where we analyzed customer feedback from different social media platforms. We used text analytics to classify the feedback into categories such as positive, negative, or neutral. This helped us to identify areas where we could improve our product and customer service.

Devops.question: How do you explain the importance of the CALMS framework in your DevOps projects?
Devops.overview: This question invites candidates to share how they've navigated complex challenges in a DevOps setting to demonstrate their problem-solving approach, adaptability, and technical prowess in implementing effective solutions.
expectations: A clear understanding of CALMS components Real-world application examples Benefits w.r.t teamwork and efficiency
Devops.sampleAnswer: In implementing CALMS, I've seen firsthand its impact on our projects. For example, by automating deployment processes, we've reduced errors and sped things up significantly. Lean practices helped us identify and eliminate inefficiencies, improving our overall workflow. The real game-changer was fostering a culture of measurement and sharing; it not only enhanced our transparency but also boosted our team's morale, as everyone could see the value of their contributions. Overall, CALMS has been instrumental in not just achieving but exceeding our project goals.

Devops.question: Describe a CI/CD pipeline you've set up or worked with. What were the key components?
Devops.overview: This question offers an opportunity to showcase your practical skills in creating and managing CI/CD pipelines, highlighting your familiarity with automation tools, version control, and deployment strategies.
expectations: Experience with version control systems Knowledge of automated testing and deployment tools Understanding of pipeline integration and monitoring
Devops.sampleAnswer: I worked on a CI/CD pipeline using Git for version control, Jenkins for automation, and Kubernetes for deployment. Our goal was streamlining deployments and improving code quality. We integrated automated tests to catch bugs early. Jenkins handled the automation, running tests on each commit, and if successful, Kubernetes rolled out updates seamlessly. This setup minimized downtime and improved our team's efficiency, making our deployment process more reliable and faster.

Devops.question: Can you share an experience where a configuration management tool significantly streamlined a project's workflow?
Devops.overview: This question invites candidates to illustrate their problem-solving capabilities and practical experience with configuration management tools such as Ansible, Chef, or Puppet, focusing on a specific challenge they addressed.
expectations: Ability to identify and solve technical problems Experience with at least one configuration management tool Understanding the impact of their solution
Devops.sampleAnswer: Once, we encountered repetitive deployment failures due to configuration inconsistencies across environments. I used Ansible to automate the configuration tasks to ensure uniformity. This not only resolved the deployment issues but also streamlined our entire deployment process and significantly reduced manual effort and errors. It was a game-changer for our project's efficiency and reliability.

Devops.question: Which cloud services have you used in your DevOps practices, and how did they enhance your project's efficiency?
Devops.overview: This question explores your experience with cloud services in DevOps, focusing on how specific platforms were leveraged to improve project outcomes.
expectations: Familiarity with cloud services Impact on project efficiency Real-world application examples
Devops.sampleAnswer: I've heavily utilized AWS Lambda and Azure Functions for their scalability and suite of services. Utilizing them allowed us to implement serverless architectures that significantly reduced infrastructure costs and improved scalability. This approach enabled the team to focus more on development and less on managing servers, enhancing our project's efficiency by allowing us to deploy features more rapidly and reliably.

Devops.question: Can you share your experience integrating Docker and Kubernetes into your development cycle?
Devops.overview: This question aims to gauge your practical experience with containerization tools, Docker and Kubernetes, and how they are integrated into the development process to enhance efficiency and scalability.
expectations: Hands-on experience with Docker and Kubernetes Impact on the development cycle Challenges and solutions encountered
Devops.sampleAnswer: Absolutely! With Docker, we tackled environment inconsistencies by packaging our application and its dependencies into containers. This eliminated the 'it works on my machine' problem and ensured that our application ran smoothly in any environment. Kubernetes further enhanced our deployment scalability and management by automating container orchestration. For example, scaling our application to handle increased load became a matter of a few commands and drastically reduced our response times to demand spikes.

Devops.question: Give me an example of a task you automated that significantly improved your workflow.
Devops.overview: This question seeks to uncover your ability to leverage automation for enhancing operational efficiency, a core component of DevOps practices.
expectations: Demonstrated automation of a routine task Impact on workflow or project efficiency Reflection on the learning or outcomes
Devops.sampleAnswer: Certainly! I automated our nightly database backups using Cron for scheduling and Bash scripts for both execution and verification. This approach significantly streamlined the process and ensured fail-proof backups, automatically addressed errors, and sent notifications for any issues, thereby enhancing our operational efficiency and response capability.

Devops.question: Discuss how you've used tools like Prometheus or ELK stack to address a specific monitoring or logging challenge.
Devops.overview: This question evaluates your ability to leverage monitoring and logging tools, like Prometheus or ELK stack, for overcoming specific challenges in maintaining system health and performance.
expectations: ELK stack, or similar tools Identification and resolution of a monitoring/logging challenge Impact on system performance or reliability
Devops.sampleAnswer: I used the ELK stack to tackle a challenge we had with log management in a distributed system. Our issue was the sheer volume of logs and the difficulty in extracting meaningful insights. By setting up Elasticsearch for log storage, Logstash for log processing, and Kibana for visualization, we created a centralized logging system. This allowed us to quickly identify and address issues, in turn, significantly reducing downtime. Also, the detailed dashboards in Kibana provided real-time insights into our system's health for improving our response to incidents.

Devops.question: How do you incorporate security into the software development lifecycle in your DevOps practice?
Devops.overview: This question explores how DevOps practices integrate security measures throughout the software development lifecycle to ensure continuous delivery without compromising security.
expectations: Understanding of DevSecOps principles Examples of security tools and practices used Impact on the development process and product security
Devops.sampleAnswer: I've always believed in integrating security early and throughout our development cycle. For instance, I integrated static code analysis tools right into our CI/CD pipeline to catch vulnerabilities early. Regular security training sessions for the team ensured everyone was on the same page and enhanced our overall security posture. This approach not only reduced our vulnerability exposure but also embedded a strong security culture within our team.

Devops.question: Describe a situation where effective communication between the development and operations teams led to a successful outcome.
Devops.overview: This question assesses the candidate's ability to foster collaboration between development and operations teams for showcasing a scenario where effective communication led to project success.
expectations: Example of cross-team collaboration Communication strategies used Outcome of the collaboration
Devops.sampleAnswer: In a recent project, a deployment issue was causing delays. I organized a joint session between the dev and ops teams to collaboratively troubleshoot. We used open communication, shared logs, and walked through the deployment process together. This approach not only resolved the issue more quickly but also led to establishing a regular sync-up meeting between the teams. The results showed a significant improvement in our project's deployment cycle and reduced future delays.

Devops.question: What's a complex challenge you've faced in a DevOps environment, and how did you tackle it?
Devops.overview: This question delves into the candidate's problem-solving skills within a DevOps context and asks them to reflect on a particularly challenging situation and their approach to overcoming it.
expectations: Identification of a DevOps challenge Strategy and tools used to resolve it Reflection on the impact and learning
Devops.sampleAnswer: A significant challenge I faced was managing service scalability under unexpected traffic spikes. I tackled this by implementing auto-scaling policies and load balancers in our cloud environment, which allowed our services to automatically adjust resources based on traffic. This prevented downtime during peak loads while optimizing our resource usage and costs. It was a valuable lesson in proactive infrastructure planning and the importance of scalability in maintaining service reliability.

Front End Developer.question: What happens when the user enters a URL?
Front End Developer.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the HTTP protocol. It's a basic question that can help you determine whether the person you're interviewing has a solid grasp of the basics of web development.
expectations: Examples of how the applicant uses this knowledge in their work
Confidence in explaining this process to any audience
Front End Developer.sampleAnswer: The user enters a URL into their browser and the browser sends a request to the server hosting the website. The server then sends back a response that includes the HTML for the page. The browser then renders the page based on this HTML.

Front End Developer.question: How will you differentiate between == and ===?
Front End Developer.overview: This question tests the applicant's knowledge of the JavaScript language and their ability to spot the difference between two similar operators.
expectations: A clear explanation of the difference between these two operators
An example of when to use each operator

Product Manager.question: How will you describe the operation of Layer 2 (Data Link Layer) of the 7-layer ISO stack?

Product Manager.sampleAnswer: Layer 2 is responsible for data link functions such as error checking and frame synchronization. It also provides a connectionless service to upper layers. It's made up of two sublayers: Logical Link Control (LLC) and Media Access Control (MAC). The LLC sublayer provides services such as flow control, error control and multiplexing. The MAC sublayer provides services such as media access control, addressing and frame format.

Project Manager.question: How do you manage changes in a project?

Project Manager.question: How would you improve project management?

Project Manager.question: What do you know about pro-bono work?

Project Manager.question: Tell me about your experience onboarding a SaaS product from start to finish.
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's experience with managing a complex project, and their ability to work with a team to ensure that all deliverables are met on time and on budget.

Project Manager.question: Why do you want to work for us?

Project Manager.question: What is your biggest weakness?

Project Manager.question: What are your strengths that will help you in this project?

Project Manager.question: What do you know about country risk?

Project Manager.question: What are the challenges you face while setting up an offshore team?
Project Manager.overview: While the ability to manage an offshore team is a valuable skill, it is also a complex and challenging task. This question can help to gauge how the candidate approaches this type of project management.

Project Manager.question: How would you define scope?
Project Manager.overview: Scope is a fundamental concept in project management, and can be a source of conflict and confusion. This question helps to determine how the candidate defines scope, and how they would approach managing scope creep.

Project Manager.question: How do you motivate difficult people to complete assigned tasks?
Project Manager.overview: A project manager must be able to motivate and inspire a team to work together and complete a project. This question can help to determine how the candidate approaches difficult situations and how they deal with underperforming team members.

Project Manager.question: How would you give the bad news to your manager that you're about to miss a money earning milestone?
Project Manager.overview: While it is important to be able to give good news, it is equally important to be able to deliver bad news. Project Manager.question: What will you do if the client doesn't approve the new functional specification?
Project Manager.overview: It is the project manager's job to ensure that the client is happy with the final product. This question helps to determine how the candidate will handle a situation where the client is not satisfied with the final product.

Project Manager.question: What are your interests and healthcare?

Project Manager.question: How would you set up a piece of software from beginning to end?

Project Manager.question: What is your experience working with difficult customers?
Project Manager.overview: In a project management role, the candidate will inevitably be required to interact with a number of different stakeholders, all with their own unique needs and expectations. This question can help to determine how the candidate approaches and handles these situations.

Project Manager.question: Tell me about a time you oversaw a complete product life cycle.
Project Manager.overview: A good project manager must be able to oversee the entire life cycle of a project, from the initial planning stages to the final implementation. This question can help to determine how well the candidate can handle the various stages of a project.

Project Manager.question: What do you do when a project has cross functional teams?
Project Manager.overview: Projects that involve multiple departments or teams can often be more difficult to manage. This question can help to identify how the candidate will handle working with other teams and departments to ensure that the project is completed successfully.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I try to work closely with all of the relevant teams and departments to ensure that everyone is on the same page and that we are all working towards the same project goals. I also try to keep an open door policy so that anyone on the team can come to me with questions or concerns.

Project Manager.question: How would you deal with a complaint from an operator that his/her supervisor is sexually harassing her/him?
Project Manager.overview: A project manager must be able to handle a wide range of issues and problems that arise during the course of a project. This question can help to gauge how the candidate will deal with a sensitive and potentially volatile situation.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to speak with the operator and his/her supervisor individually to get their sides of the story. If the problem persists, I would then bring in an outside mediator to help resolve the issue.

Project Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you failed at something, what did you do and how did you learn from it?
Project Manager.overview: The ability to learn from mistakes and to be able to reflect on past experiences is a key quality in a good project manager. This question can help to gauge how the candidate approaches failure and what they have learned from it.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I once failed to properly communicate a change in direction to my team, which led to a number of delays and setbacks. I learned that it is important to be clear and direct with the team at all times, and that it is my responsibility to make sure that everyone is on the same page.

Project Manager.question: Tell us about any project that failed and what you learned from it.
Project Manager.overview: While not every project will be a success, the ability to learn from failure and bounce back is a key quality in a good project manager. This question can help to gauge how the candidate approaches failure and what they learned from it.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: On one of my first projects as a project manager, I was in charge of a team that was tasked with developing a new product for the company. I learned that sometimes it's better to admit defeat and move on to the next project than to try and force something that just isn't going to work out.

Project Manager.question: What kind of experience do you have in selling a product?
Project Manager.overview: A project manager is often responsible for the success of a product or service, and must be able to sell their vision and ideas to a team and an organization. This question helps to determine how the candidate approaches this challenge.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have experience in selling a variety of products and services, from new technologies to consumer goods. I am able to quickly assess the needs of my audience and tailor my pitch accordingly.

Project Manager.question: Can you give me an example of a time when your project was resisted?
Project Manager.overview: In every project, there are going to be people who are resistant to change. This question helps to gauge the candidate's ability to handle resistance and keep the project moving forward.

Project Manager.question: How will you handle people in your team who are not performing as per expectation?
Project Manager.overview: While it is the project manager's job to keep the team motivated and on track, it is also their responsibility to identify and address performance issues. This question can help to gauge how the candidate approaches this delicate balance.

If this does not work, I would try to identify what is causing the problem and work with my manager and the team member in question to come up with a solution that helps them to get back on track.

Project Manager.question: What drives you?

Project Manager.question: How do you manage your projects?

Project Manager.question: Why did you apply for this position?

Project Manager.question: Design a kitchen for your home.

Project Manager.question: What would you like to tell me about yourself?

Project Manager.question: How do you learn best?

Project Manager.question: Tell me about the worst experience you've had in your life and how you handled it.

Project Manager.question: What was the most difficult situation you have faced?

Project Manager.question: How do you feel about rapidly changing work streams and deadlines?
Project Manager.overview: Projects are often subject to change, and a good project manager must be able to adapt to shifting priorities and deadlines. This question can help to determine how the candidate will react to a constantly changing environment.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I feel that the more fluid the environment, the more important it is to be flexible and adaptable. I like to keep an open line of communication with my team so that we can all work together to prioritize tasks and adjust our approach as needed.

Project Manager.question: Why did you leave your last job?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to help determine the candidate's reasons for leaving their last position. While there are many reasons why someone may leave a job, the answer to this question can help to identify whether or not the candidate is looking for a new position to advance their career, or if they are simply looking for a new job for the sake of a new job.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I left my last job because I felt that I had reached a plateau in my career and wanted to take on new challenges.

Project Manager.question: What was the biggest problem you faced at your previous job?
Project Manager.overview: Every project manager will face a number of challenges and obstacles along the way. The ability to identify and solve problems quickly and efficiently is a key skill in the profession.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: The biggest problem I faced at my last job was managing a team of remote workers. While I was able to successfully manage the team, I found that it was difficult to keep everyone on the same page, especially when it came to scheduling and deadlines.

Project Manager.question: Redesign a mobile site that you use.
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to see how the candidate thinks about design and how they approach problem solving.
expectations: Ability to work in a team
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would redesign the mobile site to be more user friendly and intuitive. I would also make it easier to find the information that users are looking for.

Project Manager.question: How would you handle an upset customer?
Project Manager.overview: In a project management role, there will inevitably be situations where a customer is upset or dissatisfied with the work that has been done. The ability to handle these situations diplomatically and effectively is a key skill for a project manager.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would try to identify the root cause of the customer's dissatisfaction and work with them to come up with a solution that would satisfy their needs while also ensuring that the project's objectives were met.

Project Manager.question: How do you resolve conflicts with your co-workers?
Project Manager.overview: In a project management role, it is inevitable that there will be disagreements and conflicts that arise between team members. The ability to resolve these issues quickly and effectively is a sign of a good project manager.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the root of the conflict and identify the best way to resolve it. I would then work with the team member in question to come up with a solution that works for everyone involved.

Project Manager.question: How do you resolve conflicts with your co-workers?
Project Manager.overview: In a project management role, it is inevitable that there will be disagreements and conflicts that arise between team members. The ability to resolve these issues quickly and effectively is a sign of a good project manager.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the root of the conflict and identify the best way to resolve it. I would then work with the team member in question to come up with a solution that works for everyone involved.

Project Manager.question: What kind of experience do you have?
Project Manager.overview: A candidate's experience is a good indicator of their ability to perform the job. A project manager with a proven track record of success will likely be a better fit for the position than someone who has less experience.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been working as a project manager for the past 5 years, and have managed projects in a variety of industries including technology, finance, and retail.

Project Manager.question: What is the acronym for a Service Level Agreement at a hosting provider?
Project Manager.overview: A Service Level Agreement (SLA) is a contract between a client and a hosting provider that outlines the responsibilities of each party in terms of uptime, performance, and other key metrics. This question can help to determine if the candidate has the basic knowledge of the industry and is familiar with industry terminology.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: The acronym for a Service Level Agreement at a hosting provider is SLA.

Project Manager.question: How do you deliver on time, on budget with quality while having competing projects?
Project Manager.overview: While the ability to deliver on time and on budget is a given, the ability to do so while juggling multiple projects is a skill that can be honed with experience. This question helps to gauge how the candidate approaches this type of situation.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I always try to keep my team focused on the most important deliverables first, and then work down the list of priorities. I also try to keep an eye on the big picture and make sure that we are not overcommitting ourselves or spreading ourselves too thin.

Project Manager.question: What is your dream job?
Project Manager.overview: While this question may seem like a simple icebreaker, it can actually reveal a lot about the candidate's personality and career aspirations.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I am interested in working in a management position with a company that is at the forefront of technology and innovation.

Project Manager.question: How would you lead a project that had previously been attempted and failed?
Project Manager.overview: Projects that have been attempted and failed in the past are often the most challenging to manage. This question helps to gauge how a candidate will approach a project that has been tried and failed before, and how they will keep the team motivated and focused on the ultimate goal.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to identify why the previous project failed, and then work with the team to develop a plan that would ensure that we would not make the same mistakes again. I would also work with the team to identify what went right in the previous project, and use that as a foundation for our new plan of attack.

Project Manager.question: What was a mistake you made in the past and how did you fix it?
Project Manager.overview: Mistakes are inevitable in the world of project management. The ability to learn from past mistakes and identify areas for improvement is a key quality in a good project manager.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had a project that was running over budget and behind schedule. I was able to identify the root cause of the issue and take steps to correct it, which allowed me to get the project back on track.

Project Manager.question: What is a failed project you have worked on?
Project Manager.overview: While a candidate's past work experience is always a good indicator of their skills and abilities, it is important to understand how they have dealt with adversity and failure. This question can help to gauge how they respond to failure and how they learn from their mistakes.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I was once in charge of a project that was supposed to launch a new product line for Company X. Unfortunately, the project was plagued by delays and setbacks, which ultimately led to the cancellation of the product line. I learned a lot from this experience, and since then I have been able to apply my knowledge to better manage projects with similar challenges.

Project Manager.question: What are your strengths as a team leader?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to help the hiring manager get a sense of the candidate's self awareness and ability to identify their own strengths and weaknesses.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would say my greatest strength as a team leader is my ability to keep the team focused on the project goals and objectives. I am also very good at identifying and communicating with team members who are struggling or having issues.

Project Manager.question: What was your last project?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's experience in the field and industry of the job posting. It can also help to identify if the candidate has any relevant experience that may be helpful to the company.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: My last project was a rebranding initiative for Company X's international division. I led a team of creative, technical and administrative staff and was able to ensure that all deliverables were met on time and on budget.

Project Manager.question: How will you deal with difficult people?
Project Manager.overview: Difficult people are a fact of life, and a good project manager must be able to handle them effectively. This question can help to determine how the candidate will deal with conflict and difficult personalities.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would try to identify the root cause of the conflict and work with the team member in question to resolve the issue. If this was not possible, I would try to identify a mutually beneficial solution that would allow the team member to work effectively while maintaining a positive working relationship.

Project Manager.question: What do you know about our company?
Project Manager.overview: A good project manager should be able to quickly identify the needs of their team and company, and be able to work with them to achieve common goals. This question can help to gauge how well the candidate will fit in with the team.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been following your company for some time now, and I am very excited about the opportunity to work with you. I have been following your company's progress in the industry and I am very impressed with your growth and success.

Project Manager.question: What is the most important role responsibility of a PM and why?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to help the hiring manager understand what the candidate considers to be the most important aspect of the job, and how they would prioritize their time and efforts.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: The most important role of a project manager is to keep the project on track and on time. This means that I must be able to manage my team effectively and efficiently, while also keeping an eye on the big picture.

Project Manager.question: What is your experience in project management?
Project Manager.overview: This question can help to determine the candidate's level of experience and how well they have been able to apply their skills in a professional setting.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been working as a project manager for Company X for the past three years. During that time, I have managed over a dozen projects of varying size and complexity, and have been able to successfully deliver on all of them.

Project Manager.question: What is your educational background?
Project Manager.overview: While a candidate's educational background may not be the most important factor in the hiring process, it can provide a good indication of their ability to learn and adapt to new situations.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration from University X.

Project Manager.question: What is your opinion about the project you've worked on?
Project Manager.overview: This question can help to gauge the candidate's level of satisfaction with their previous projects and how they feel about the work they've done.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I am very proud of the work that I've done on this project. I was able to successfully manage a team of over 20 people and ensure that all deliverables were met on time and on budget.

Project Manager.question: What are you not doing at your current job that you wish you could be doing?
Project Manager.overview: This question can help to determine what the candidate is looking for in their next position, and whether or not they are a good fit for the position.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I'm not currently working on any large scale projects, which is something that I would love to do in my next position.

Project Manager.question: How long have you been in the Army?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's experience and tenure in the Army.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been in the Army for the past 10 years. Answer Description: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's experience and tenure in the Army.

Project Manager.question: What was your role at the previous employer?
Project Manager.overview: This question can help to determine what the candidate's role was in the past, and what they are looking for in their next position.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: As the project manager for Company X, I was responsible for managing a team of five project managers and ensuring that all deliverables were met on time and on budget.

Project Manager.question: What kind of projects do you prefer to work on?
Project Manager.overview: Every project manager has their own strengths and weaknesses, and this question can help to identify what those are.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I prefer to work on projects that are highly creative and require a lot of teamwork and collaboration. I enjoy the challenge of working with a diverse team to complete a project on time and on budget.

Project Manager.question: What made you interested in this job?
Project Manager.overview: This question can help to determine the candidate's level of enthusiasm for the position, and whether or not they are a good fit for the company.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I am very interested in the work that Company X does in the field of [insert industry] and I am excited to have the opportunity to contribute to the team.

Project Manager.question: What is a project where you had to develop a business case for approval by senior management?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's ability to work with senior management and to develop a plan that will be approved and implemented.
expectations: Ability to work with senior management
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I was able to develop a business case for approval by senior management by outlining the project goals and objectives, identifying the resources required to complete the project, and outlining the expected results.

Project Manager.question: When can you interview?
Project Manager.overview: The hiring manager may be looking for a specific time frame in which they can schedule the candidate for an interview.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I am available to meet with you on Tuesday afternoon at 3:00pm.

Project Manager.question: How many hours do you work per week?
Project Manager.overview: This question can help to determine how much time the candidate is able to devote to the position.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I work a minimum of 40 hours per week.

Project Manager.question: How have you rolled out or implemented a new idea or procedure at your company?
Project Manager.overview: The ability to implement new ideas and procedures is a key component of a project manager's job. This question can help to gauge how the candidate will approach implementing new ideas and procedures within their team.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first work with the team to identify the most efficient way to implement the new idea or procedure, and then work with each team member to ensure that they are on board with the new process.

Project Manager.question: What are the 3 words that you would use to describe your colleagues?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's ability to work with others and their level of self awareness.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would describe my colleagues as hardworking, dedicated and loyal.

Project Manager.question: How do you resolve conflicts?
Project Manager.overview: Conflicts and disagreements are an inevitable part of any team. A good project manager must be able to resolve conflicts in a productive and professional manner.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I try to approach conflicts as a team building opportunity. I believe that by working together, we can find a solution that works for everyone involved.

Project Manager.question: On a scale of one to ten how competitive are you?
Project Manager.overview: This question is designed to gauge the candidate's drive and ambition. A competitive attitude can be a good thing, but it can also lead to unnecessary conflict and tension in the workplace.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would say that I am a competitive person, but I try to channel that energy into my work and not let it get in the way of my relationships with my coworkers.

Project Manager.question: What would you do if you got this position?
Project Manager.overview: This question is a great way to gauge the candidate's enthusiasm for the position and their level of preparation. It can also help to determine if the candidate has done their homework and researched the company and position.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first take some time to get to know the team and the company culture, and then I would dive right into the project. I would first work with my team to identify our top priorities for the project, and then I would make sure that we are all on the same page with regards to our goals and objectives.

Project Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you solved a difficult problem.
Project Manager.overview: This question is a great way to gauge how a candidate approaches problem solving. It can help to determine how they think through a problem, and what steps they take to resolve it.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I recently had a situation where a team member was struggling with a particularly difficult task. I took the time to sit down with them and walk them through the steps that they needed to take in order to complete the task successfully. By taking the time to walk them through the process, I was able to help them understand what they needed to do, and they were able to complete the task without any further issues.

Project Manager.question: What are the current methodologies you use for your projects?
Project Manager.overview: A good project manager is able to keep up with the latest trends and methodologies in their field. This question can help to determine how well the candidate is able to adapt to new situations and challenges.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I am constantly researching and learning about new methodologies and best practices in my field, and I try to incorporate these into my projects whenever possible.

Project Manager.question: How do you manage risks in your project?
Project Manager.overview: Managing risk is a fundamental part of the project management process. This question can help to identify how a candidate will approach risk management and how they will handle inevitable setbacks.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I like to keep an eye on the big picture and try to identify risks as they develop, so that I can work with my team to develop contingency plans in advance.

Project Manager.question: What are the reasons that make you interested in this position?
Project Manager.overview: While it is important to be able to communicate a candidate's interest in the position, it is also important to be able to identify the reasons why they are interested in the position. This question can help to determine if the candidate is truly interested in the position, or if they are just looking for a job.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I am very interested in this position because I feel that my experience and skills would be a great fit for the company's needs. I am also very interested in working with a team of professionals who are as passionate about their work as I am.

Project Manager.question: What do you like least about project management?
Project Manager.overview: While project management is a rewarding and challenging career, it is also a high pressure position that requires a great deal of time and attention. This question can help to determine if the candidate is aware of the demands of the job, and if they are willing to make the necessary sacrifices.
Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I think one of the most challenging aspects of project management is the need to balance the needs of the project with the needs of the team. Although I always try to give my team members as much space and freedom as possible, there are times when I need to step in and help them to prioritize their work.

Senior Project Manager.question: How do you handle negative people on the team?
Senior Project Manager.overview: The ideal candidate will have experience dealing with negative people and know how to handle them in a professional manner. The applicant's response will help you gauge their ability to deal with difficult people and how they handle stressful situations.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I always try to remain positive when dealing with negative people. I know that they are likely having a bad day and do not mean to be rude. I try to find out what is bothering them and work with them to resolve the issue.

Senior Project Manager.question: What will you do if your timelines are crunched from 4 weeks to 4 days?
Senior Project Manager.overview: The ideal candidate will have the ability to remain calm in stressful situations. The applicant's response will help you gauge how well they can handle unexpected changes and if they are able to remain focused on the task at hand.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: In my last position, we were given a one-week deadline to complete a project. I was able to get the team together and we were able to complete the project on time.

Senior Project Manager.question: Why do you want to be a project manager?
Senior Project Manager.overview: The ideal candidate will have a passion for the field of project management and will be able to explain why they want to be a project manager. Do they mention the ability to work with different teams?
expectations: Passion for the field of project management
Ability to work with different teams
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been interested in the way people work together to complete a project. I want to be a project manager because I want to help others succeed and ensure that projects are completed on time.

Senior Project Manager.question: Why do you want to work with us?
Senior Project Manager.overview: The ideal candidate will have researched the company and know why they are interested in working for the organization. The applicant's response will help you determine if they are truly interested in the company or if they are just looking for a job.
expectations: Desire to work with a specific team,
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been interested in your company for years and would love to work with your team. I am a huge fan of your products and believe that I can bring value to your organization.

Senior Project Manager.question: If you were in the elevator with the Mayor, what is one project that would help economic development?
Senior Project Manager.overview: As a product manager, you should be aware of the current state of your industry and what is going on in the world. The ideal candidate will be able to think on their feet and come up with a project that would help the local economy.
expectations: Ability to think on one's feet
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: If I was in an elevator with the mayor, I would suggest that we create a mobile application that allows citizens to report issues in their neighborhoods. This would allow the city to fix problems faster and increase citizen satisfaction.

Senior Project Manager.question: What kind of contribution can you make as a PM?
Senior Project Manager.overview: Product managers are responsible for the success of a product. The ideal applicant will have the ability to explain how they can help the company succeed and how they will be able to contribute to the company's bottom line.
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I can help increase sales by creating a product that is easy to use and meets the needs of my customers. I can also help reduce costs by finding ways to cut down on expenses and improve efficiency.

Senior Project Manager.question: What is your experience with kanban?
Senior Project Manager.overview: Kanban is a method of managing work that is often used in agile environments. The ideal candidate will have experience with the method and be able to explain how it works.
expectations: Ability to explain how it works,
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been using kanban for the past two years. I find it to be a great way to keep track of tasks and ensure that they are completed on time.

Senior Project Manager.question: Please give an analogy, or explanation, of how you would describe Project Management to a 5 year old.
Senior Project Manager.overview: Project managers are responsible for many different tasks and it is important to be able to explain the role to others. The ideal candidate will be able to explain the role in a way that is easy for others to understand.
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I would explain that project managers are like the coaches of a sports team. They are responsible for making sure that everyone is working together and staying on track.

Senior Project Manager.question: How would you deal with a client who is constantly changing the requirements of the project?
Senior Project Manager.overview: Clients can be demanding and it is the responsibility of a project manager to ensure that the client's needs are met. The ideal candidate will have experience with clients who are constantly changing their minds and how they respond to such situations.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: In my last position, the client was constantly changing their mind about what they wanted. I would sit down with them and explain that we could not continue to work on the project until they were sure of what they wanted.

Senior Project Manager.question: How will you assess the existing site?
Senior Project Manager.overview: As a senior product manager, you will be responsible for assessing the current state of a website or application. The ideal candidate will be able to explain how they will evaluate the current state of the product and how they will determine what needs to be fixed.
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: I will use the Pareto principle to determine what 20% of the issues are causing 80% of the problems. I will then focus on fixing those issues first.

Senior Project Manager.question: How will you benefit from the successful project delivery, team dynamics and managing clients?
Senior Project Manager.overview: The ideal candidate will be able to explain how they will benefit from the project's success. Do they mention a desire to learn more about the company's products?
expectations: Desire to learn more about the company
Desire to learn more about the industry
Desire to learn more about the team,

Senior Project Manager.question: How do you handle bad requirements?
Senior Project Manager.overview: Product managers are often in charge of handling issues regarding a product. The ideal candidate will have the ability to handle bad requirements and communicate with the customer to ensure that the issue is resolved.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Senior Project Manager.sampleAnswer: In my last position, I was given a requirement that was not feasible for the product. I worked with the customer to find a solution that would work for both of us.

Senior Project Manager.question: Can you please describe a situation when you had to deliver bad news?
Senior Project Manager.overview: Bad news is inevitable in the workplace and the ideal applicant will have experience delivering such news. Did they mention that they were able to deliver the news in a professional manner?
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Ability to remain professional in the face of adversity,

Senior Project Manager.question: What was a difficult situation on a project that happened to you, and how did you handle it?
Senior Project Manager.overview: Product managers are responsible for handling issues that arise during the development of a product. Did they have to deal with a disgruntled customer?
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations

Senior Project Manager.question: What product or service would you like to work on?

Senior Project Manager.question: Walk me through how you would develop a strategy to cut costs for a particular process or project.

Senior Project Manager.question: How comfortable are you with managing projects that have teams not versed in or supportive of process governance?

Senior Project Manager.question: How will you help the team?

Senior Project Manager.question: Where do you see yourself in the next five years?

Senior Project Manager.question: What are your strengths and weaknesses?
