Front Desk Agent.question: What is the most important thing for a front desk agent?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents are the first and last person many guests will see when they enter and leave a hotel. This means they will need to be friendly and welcoming to all guests, regardless of their status. A good answer will also emphasize the importance of being able to handle a variety of situations.
expectations: Ability to handle a variety of situations
Ability to work well with others,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: The most important thing for a front desk agent is to be friendly and welcoming to all guests. It's also important to be able to handle a variety of situations, from helping guests with directions to solving problems that may arise.

Front Desk Agent.question: Without having any hotel experience, why would you choose a Crowne Plaza hotel as opposed to a Mariott?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is designed to see how well the candidate understands the hotel industry and how they would choose a hotel to work at. A good answer will show that they have a good understanding of the hotel brands and their relative strengths and weaknesses.
expectations: Good understanding of the relative strengths and weaknesses of different hotel brands,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've always been a fan of Crowne Plaza's hotels. They have a reputation for being more upscale than Mariott, which I think would be a great fit for me given my experience in the hospitality industry.

Front Desk Agent.question: What would be the reasons for you to miss work?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is meant to gauge how responsible a candidate is and how they handle their personal affairs. A good answer should show that they are responsible and will be able to handle the job well.
expectations: Willingness to take on extra work,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I would miss work if I were sick or if I had a family emergency. I would also miss work if I had a doctor's appointment or if I had to attend a funeral.

Front Desk Agent.question: Tell me about your career.
Front Desk Agent.overview: This is a simple question that can be used to gauge a candidate's experience in the hospitality industry. It's also a good way to see if they have any experience in the type of hotel you're hiring for.
expectations: Experience in the type of hotel you're hiring for,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've been working at hotels for the past three years. I started off as a front desk agent and worked my way up to the position I'm in now.

Front Desk Agent.question: What are your examples of the 4 C's?
Front Desk Agent.overview: The 4 C's are the four main components of customer service: courtesy, communication, competence, and consistency. This question will give you an idea of how well a candidate understands these concepts and how they apply to their work.
expectations: Knowledge of the hotel's services and amenities,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I always want to be courteous to guests when I'm at work. I'll always greet them with a smile and a "hello" or "good morning" when they come in. I'll also make sure to answer any questions they have with a friendly tone and good eye contact.

Front Desk Agent.question: Why did you choose Sheraton Chicago?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This is a question that can be asked of any candidate for any position. It's a good way to gauge a candidate's interest in the company and their knowledge of the brand.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I chose Sheraton Chicago because I've always been a fan of the brand. I've stayed at many Sheraton hotels in the past and have always been impressed with their service and quality.

Front Desk Agent.question: How would you handle a difficult guest?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents will often have to deal with difficult guests, so asking how they would handle such a situation is a good way to gauge their ability to deal with such people. The ideal candidate will have good communication skills and be able to remain calm and collected under pressure.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: If a guest was being difficult, I'd try to remain calm and professional. I'd listen to what they had to say and try to resolve the issue as best as I could. If that didn't work, I'd ask them if there was anything else I could do for them before they left.

Front Desk Agent.question: Tell me about a time when you had to give guests different options.
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents will often need to give guests different options when it comes to their stay. This can include things like different room types, room locations, or other amenities. The ideal candidate will be able to give a good answer that shows they understand the importance of giving guests options and are capable of doing so in a friendly and professional manner.
expectations: Knowledge of the hotel's amenities and services
Ability to clearly and concisely convey information,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I once had a family come in asking for a room with two beds. Unfortunately, we didn't have any available at the time, but I was able to offer them a room with one king-sized bed instead.

Front Desk Agent.question: How do you think your experiences would make you a good fit for this position?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is a good way to gauge a candidate's self-awareness and ability to sell themselves. A good answer will show that they have the skills and experience needed for the job and that they are capable of understanding how they can contribute to the hotel.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've been working at hotels for the past three years and have been exposed to all aspects of the job. I've learned how to handle all kinds of situations, from dealing with upset guests to solving problems with room bookings. I've also learned how to prioritize my work and how to work well with others.

Front Desk Agent.question: How do you resolve conflicts?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents are often the first point of contact for guests and employees alike. As such, they will need to be able to resolve conflicts between the two parties. This question will give you an idea as to how they handle such situations and how they go about solving them.
expectations: Ability to listen and empathize with others
Willingness to help and to find new solutions to problems,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I would try to resolve the conflict by talking with both parties separately and getting their side of the story. Once I had a good idea of what happened, I'd try to come up with a solution that would make both parties happy.

Front Desk Agent.question: How do you handle stressful situations?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents are often put in stressful situations, such as dealing with upset guests or handling a large number of people at once. A good answer will show you how they deal with these situations and how they respond to stress.
expectations: Ability to remain professional under pressure,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I always try to remain calm and collected when dealing with stressful situations. I believe it's important to keep a level head and not let your emotions get the better of you.

Front Desk Agent.question: How have you prepared for this interview?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is designed to see how well a candidate has researched the company and position. A good answer will show that they have done their research and are familiar with the company's history, mission, and goals.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've read up on the history of your company and have seen the photos of your hotel on your website. I've also read up on the job description and have a good idea of what it entails.

Front Desk Agent.question: What is your biggest strength?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This is a straightforward question that gives you a chance to see how well the candidate will fit in with the rest of the staff. A good answer will be positive and highlight a skill or trait that will be useful in the position.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'm a hard worker and I'm always willing to help out my coworkers. I think my biggest strength is my ability to work well with others.

Front Desk Agent.question: What would you do if a high risk person enters the facility?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Hotels are often targets for criminals, so it's important to know how a candidate would handle a situation in which a dangerous person enters the building. This question will show you how they react to stressful situations and how they prioritize the safety of the hotel and its guests.
expectations: Ability to think clearly under pressure
Willingness to put guests' safety above all else,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: If a high risk person entered the facility, I would make sure to keep an eye on them while also keeping other guests out of harm's way. I would also call for backup from security and inform any guests that may be in the area of the situation.

Front Desk Agent.question: What can you offer our team?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is a good way to gauge a candidate's interest in the position. A good answer should show that they are enthusiastic about the job and have a desire to make a positive impact on the company.
expectations: Desire to make a positive impact on the company
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'm very excited to be applying for this position. I've always wanted to work in the hospitality industry and I think this would be a great opportunity for me. I'm very eager to learn and I think I can bring a lot of enthusiasm and positivity to the team.

Front Desk Agent.question: What is your experience in customer support?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is a great way to gauge a candidate's experience in customer service. It will also give you an idea of how they handle themselves in a work environment.
expectations: Ability to work well with others,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've been working in customer service for the past three years. I've worked at a few different places, but I've always enjoyed helping people and making sure they have a good experience.

Front Desk Agent.question: How would you deal with a supervisor who made a decision you didn't agree with?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents will often need to work with supervisors and other management to fulfill their duties. Asking how a candidate would deal with a situation in which they disagreed with a decision is a good way to gauge how they would respond to this situation.
expectations: Ability to work well with others,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I would do my best to respectfully explain my position on the matter and why I believe it's the right course of action. If the supervisor still disagreed, I'd be willing to discuss it further and find a compromise that would satisfy both of us.

Front Desk Agent.question: How do you react to criticism?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents will often be criticized for their work, whether it be from guests or their superiors. A good answer should show that they can take criticism well and learn from it. Additionally, they should show that they have a good attitude and are willing to improve.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I always try to take criticism in stride and use it to improve myself. If I made a mistake, I'd try to figure out what I did wrong and how I can avoid making the same mistake in the future.

Front Desk Agent.question: Tell me about a time you overcame a challenge at your previous job.
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is designed to gauge a candidate's ability to deal with challenges. A good answer will show that they were able to overcome a challenge and learn from it, ideally impressing upon you the importance of being able to do so.
expectations: Ability to learn from past experiences,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I had a guest who was very upset about the room they were given. They claimed that the room was too small and that the bed was uncomfortable. After talking with them for a while, I realized that they were just upset about their breakup and were taking it out on me. I apologized for their experience and offered them a complimentary bottle of wine for their troubles.

Front Desk Agent.question: If a pre-booked guest wanted a nonsmoking room but the only availability was smoking, how would you handle the situation?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents will often be asked to deal with situations in which they can't provide what a guest wants. This question will give you an idea of how they would respond to such a situation, giving you a good idea of how they handle conflict.
expectations: Willingness to help and to find new solutions to problems
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: If a guest wanted a nonsmoking room but the only availability was smoking, I would offer to see if we could find them another hotel nearby that had the room type they wanted. If that wasn't possible, I would offer them a discount on their stay as compensation for the inconvenience.

Front Desk Agent.question: What brought you to hotels?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is meant to gauge a candidate's interest in the hospitality industry. A good answer should show they have a passion for the industry and a desire to work in it.
expectations: Desire to work in the hospitality industry,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've always been interested in the hospitality industry and I've always wanted to work in it. I've always enjoyed meeting new people and making them feel welcome, so this seemed like a natural fit for me.

Front Desk Agent.question: Are you available to work anytime?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents are often required to work at all hours of the day and night. Asking about their availability will give you a good idea of how flexible they are, as well as their ability to work under pressure.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'm available to work anytime, though I'm not sure if that's a good thing or not. I'm always willing to put in the extra time to help out my coworkers and guests.

Front Desk Agent.question: Why did you choose customer service?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is meant to gauge the candidate's interest in the field and their reasons for wanting to work at a hotel. A good answer will show that they have a genuine interest in the position and the industry as a whole.
expectations: A desire to work in a customer-facing position,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I've always loved helping people. I've worked as a volunteer at my local church for years now and I've always enjoyed it. I think customer service is a great way to do that on a larger scale.

Front Desk Agent.question: What is your availability?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is a simple way to gauge how flexible the candidate is. A good answer will show that they are willing to work whatever hours are needed, even if they are not the most desirable.
expectations: Willingness to work extra hours when needed,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'm available to work any time of the day or night. I'm also willing to work overtime if needed.

Front Desk Agent.question: How far are you willing to relocate?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is a good way to gauge how willing a candidate is to move for a job. It also shows how flexible they are in terms of their career, which can be important for someone who will be working in the hospitality industry.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'm willing to relocate anywhere as long as I'm able to find a job in the hospitality industry.

Front Desk Agent.question: What do you expect from this company?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This is a good question to ask to gauge a candidate's expectations for their career. You want to hire someone who is ambitious and willing to work hard, but you also want to avoid hiring someone who expects to be promoted quickly or who has unreasonable expectations for their salary.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I expect to learn a lot from this company and to grow as a person. I'm also hoping to be promoted within the next few years.

Front Desk Agent.question: What would you do if there was a fire alarm in the middle of the night and a guest is upset?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Fires are rare but they do happen, especially in hotels. As such, front desk agents will need to be prepared for this eventuality. A good answer will show you that the candidate is capable of handling a situation that could potentially be dangerous and stressful.
expectations: Confidence in their ability to handle the situation
Ability to remain calm under pressure,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'd try to get the guest to safety first and foremost. If they had any belongings that were left behind, I'd make sure they were taken care of. Once the guest was safe, I'd contact the fire department and let them know what happened.

Front Desk Agent.question: What do you think will be the most challenging part of this job?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question will give you a good idea of what the candidate thinks will be the most difficult part of the position. It's also a good way to see if they have any reservations about taking the job.
expectations: A willingness to take on challenges
Confidence in their ability to handle the job,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: The most challenging part of this job will be keeping up with the high volume of guests we get during peak season. I'm confident that I can handle it though, as I've had plenty of experience working in busy environments.

Front Desk Agent.question: Do you have a car?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is asked to see if the candidate has a car and if they are willing to use it for work. If they do have a car, you can ask them to describe it and what they use it for.
expectations: Willingness to use car for work,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: Yes, I have a car. It's a [Car Make] and I use it mainly for work-related errands.

Front Desk Agent.question: What was the most challenging experience in your life?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is designed to gauge a candidate's ability to handle difficult situations. It will also give you a chance to see how they respond to stressful situations and how they deal with adversity.
expectations: Confidence in their ability to handle difficult situations
Ability to remain calm under pressure
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: The most challenging experience in my life was having to take care of my grandmother after she was diagnosed with cancer. I had to juggle school and work while also taking care of her, but I was able to make it through thanks to the support of my family and friends.

Front Desk Agent.question: Tell me about the worst customer experience you've had and how did you handle it?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Front desk agents will often have to deal with difficult guests. This question will give you an idea of how they handle these situations, as well as how they view their role in the hotel.
expectations: Willingness to help guests and solve problems
Ability to remain calm under pressure,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: The worst customer experience I've had was when a guest came in and demanded a room upgrade without any reason. I tried to explain that we were fully booked but he wouldn't listen. I had to call a manager over to handle the situation and the guest eventually left without getting what he wanted.

Front Desk Agent.question: What was a time you had to overcome a challenge and how did you do so?
Front Desk Agent.overview: Every job will have its challenges, and front desk agents are no exception. This question will give you a chance to see how a candidate deals with these challenges and how they overcome them.
expectations: Willingness to work hard and overcome obstacles
Ability to learn from mistakes and improve,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I had to learn how to use the hotel's new reservation system when it was installed a few months ago. It took me a while to get used to it, but I eventually learned how to use it without any problems.

Front Desk Agent.question: What do you think the purpose of fuzz is on a tennis ball?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This is a question that tests an applicant's ability to think on their feet. The best answers will be ones that show a good sense of humor and a willingness to play along.
expectations: Willingness to go with the flow,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I think the fuzz is there to make the tennis ball more aerodynamic so it can fly faster and farther.

Front Desk Agent.question: What is the nicest hotel you have ever stayed in and what made it great?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is designed to see if the candidate has any experience with hotels and what they look for in a hotel stay. It will also show you how well they can describe their experiences and how well they can relate to you.
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: The nicest hotel I've ever stayed in was a small bed and breakfast in the mountains. The view from our room was incredible and the staff was very friendly. I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a nice getaway.

Front Desk Agent.question: Why did you apply for this job when you have no relevant experience or qualifications?
Front Desk Agent.overview: This question is a good way to see how a candidate will respond when they don't have the experience or qualifications for a job. It will show you how they will handle themselves in a situation where they are not the most qualified candidate for the job.
expectations: Confidence in their ability to do the job
A positive attitude towards the job and the company,
Front Desk Agent.sampleAnswer: I'm confident that I can do this job well. I've had plenty of experience dealing with customers in my previous jobs and I know I can use that knowledge to help guests feel welcome and comfortable here.

Service Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had multiple projects and how did you manage your time?
Service Manager.overview: As a service manager, your candidate will be responsible for overseeing multiple projects at once. Therefore, it is important that they have a clear understanding of how to prioritize their work and manage their time effectively. Asking about a time when they were faced with multiple projects will allow you to see how they handled the situation and if they are able to effectively juggle multiple tasks.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: When I was in college, I had a part-time job as a tutor and also worked as a sales associate at a clothing store. I had to make sure that I was able to balance my time between both jobs so that I could get my schoolwork done and still have time to go out with my friends.

Service Manager.question: What kind of job do you want?
Service Manager.overview: This is a great opportunity to see if your candidate is a good fit for your organization. You want to hire someone who has a clear understanding of what they want out of their career and the skills necessary to achieve their goals.
expectations: Desire to grow with your company,
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I am looking for a position that will allow me to use my customer service skills while also helping me grow my business acumen.

Service Manager.question: Tell me about a time you helped your company make more money and how did you do it?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be in charge of helping your firm make more money by increasing customer satisfaction and retention. As such, they should be able to show that they have a strong understanding of how to create a strategy that will allow your company to accomplish this goal.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I once helped my company increase its revenue by 15% by creating a new service package that was more affordable for our clients.

Service Manager.question: Tell me about a time you implemented a plan, and describe the process in which you did it, and what the outcome was.
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be responsible for implementing plans that will help your business grow. As such, you are looking for an applicant who has a strong understanding of how to create and execute on a plan that will help your organization reach its goals.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I once worked with a client who was interested in expanding their business into a new market. I created a plan to help them do so by creating a marketing campaign that would target potential clients in the new area.

Service Manager.question: How do you handle a frustrated customer?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be the first person your clients speak to when they are upset about their experience with your company. As such, it is important that they have a clear understanding of how to handle these situations in a way that is productive and does not further upset the client.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I always make sure to listen to what the customer has to say and try to understand their point of view. Then I ask them what they would like me to do to make things right.

Service Manager.question: What are you interested in the position?
Service Manager.overview: A service manager is a crucial role in your organization, so you want to make sure that the person you hire is passionate about the job. Asking this question will allow you to gauge your candidate's interest in the position and their enthusiasm for the work that they will be doing.
expectations: Interest in working for your company,
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I am very interested in working with your company because I have heard great things about your customer service and I think it would be a great opportunity to learn from a successful business.

Service Manager.question: What is your weakness?
Service Manager.overview: This is a classic interview question that is designed to see how your candidate reacts when put on the spot. The best way to answer this question is to admit to a weakness that is not relevant to the position you are interviewing for. For example, if you are hiring for a customer service position, admitting that you are not great at public speaking would be a good way to go.
expectations: Acknowledgement of a weakness that is not relevant to the position
Ability to think quickly on their feet,
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I am not the best at public speaking, but I am working on it.

Service Manager.question: Why did you apply for this job?
Service Manager.overview: This is a great question to ask your candidate to see if they are truly interested in the position and have done their research on your organization. Your interviewee should be able to clearly articulate why they are interested in working for your company and what they hope to gain from the experience.
expectations: Knowledge of your company's mission and values,
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I've been a fan of your company for years and I think it would be a great opportunity to work for a company that I believe in.

Service Manager.question: What is a difficult goal you were given and how did you achieve it?
Service Manager.overview: As a service manager, your candidate will be tasked with setting goals for their team and working to achieve them. This question will allow you to see how they go about this process and what types of goals they are able to set.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: When I was in charge of my organization's social media presence, I set a goal of increasing our followers by 10 percent each month. I was able to achieve this by creating a plan for content creation and promotion that was able to be replicated by my team.

Service Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to complete a long list of things by a short deadline.
Service Manager.overview: As a service manager, your candidate will be responsible for managing the workload of a team of customer-facing employees. Therefore, they will be required to have a strong sense of time management and the ability to prioritize tasks effectively. As such, you should ask about a time when they had to complete a long list of things by a short deadline.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had to finish an important project for my boss in time for her to present it at a conference. I was able to get it done by the deadline by working late every night for two weeks straight.

Service Manager.question: How will you handle an employee who is upset he didn't get your position?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be in charge of hiring and training new staff, so it is likely that they will have to deal with employees who are disappointed that they did not get a promotion. As such, you should be looking for a candidate who is able to handle these situations with tact and professionalism.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I would sit down with the employee and explain that I am sorry he was disappointed but that I felt that someone else was a better fit for the job.

Service Manager.question: How do you handle stressful situations?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be dealing with a variety of situations that can be stressful, including dealing with difficult clients, handling emergencies and making quick decisions. As such, you are looking for an applicant who is able to remain calm and collected under pressure.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I always make sure to take a deep breath before I start talking to a customer so that I can stay calm and collected.

Service Manager.question: Tell me about a time you had to prioritize work assignments.
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be in charge of a team of customer-facing employees, so it is important that they have experience delegating tasks and making sure that their staff is able to complete them on time. As such, you want to make sure that your candidate has a clear understanding of how to prioritize work assignments and that they have the ability to effectively communicate with their team.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had to prioritize work assignments when I had two employees out sick and two others who were out on vacation. I had to make sure that all of the clients' needs were met while also ensuring that the staff was able to take care of their own work.

Service Manager.question: What kind of sales experience do you have?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be responsible for ensuring that your clients are getting the most out of their products. As such, it is important that your candidate has a strong understanding of how to sell your products and services effectively.
expectations: Previous experience selling products or services
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been selling my own artwork online for the past five years. I have learned a lot about how to market my work and have seen my sales increase steadily over time.

Service Manager.question: Please tell us about your experience.
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be in charge of a team of customer-facing employees, so it is important that they have experience working with others. This question will allow you to gauge your candidate's ability to work with others in a professional and effective manner.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been working with a team for the past five years. I am very comfortable delegating tasks and making sure that my employees are able to complete their work efficiently.

Service Manager.question: What do you think about our pay and benefit package?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be working with your customer service team on a daily basis, so it is important that they are happy with the compensation and benefits package that you offer. As such, you will want to ask about their thoughts on the current pay and benefits structure.
expectations: Positive attitude towards compensation and benefits
Ability to work well with others,
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I think the pay and benefits are very competitive.

Service Manager.question: What would you do if one of your direct reports is accused of theft or harrassment?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be responsible for hiring and training a team of customer-facing employees, which means they will be the first to know if one of their workers is accused of theft or harrassment. As such, it is important that your candidate has a clear plan for how they would handle such a situation.
expectations: Clear plan for handling employee theft or harassment
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first make sure that the accusation was true and then take appropriate action.

Service Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to overcome a difficult challenge.
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be responsible for dealing with a variety of situations that may arise during the course of their work. As such, your candidate should be able to show that they have the ability to overcome these challenges and come out on top.
expectations: Examples of past challenges and how they were overcome
Ability to deal with difficult situations
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had to deal with a difficult client who was upset that we could not fulfill their order. I was able to talk them through the situation and find a solution that worked for everyone.

Service Manager.question: What is a situation that was difficult and how did you solve it?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be in charge of solving problems that arise with clients and making sure that their needs are met. As such, your candidate should be able to demonstrate that they have a strong sense of problem-solving and can think on their feet.
expectations: Ability to think on their feet
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had a client who was unhappy with the quality of the product we were providing and wanted to cancel their order. I was able to convince them to give us another chance by offering a discount on their next order.

Service Manager.question: If you were asked to fix a problem in the same day and you didn't know how to solve it, what would you do?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be the person your clients come to when they need help with a problem. As such, it is important that they have a plan for dealing with situations that they have not encountered before. Your candidate should be able to show that they have a strong work ethic and are willing to put in the time and effort necessary to solve problems effectively.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I would start by researching the problem online and then ask my team for their input. If I still had not found an answer, I would call other service managers in the industry for advice.

Service Manager.question: What is your interest in Google?
Service Manager.overview: Google is a company that is constantly innovating and changing the way it does business, and your service manager will be responsible for making sure that your organization is able to keep up with the changes. As such, you are looking for an applicant who has a strong interest in Google's business model and is able to think critically about how it can be applied to your own organization.
expectations: Strong interest in Google's business model
Ability to think critically about Google's business model
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been interested in how Google has been able to stay at the forefront of technological innovation.

Service Manager.question: How do you live the values of 24 Hour Fitness?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be the face of your company, so it is important that they are able to represent your brand in a positive light. As such, you should ask them about how they live your company's values on a daily basis. This will allow you to see if they are able to articulate their understanding of your organization's mission and goals and if they are able to incorporate them into their daily lives.
Service Manager.sampleAnswer: I always make sure to keep my word and do what I say I am going to do. I think this is a great way to live the values of 24 Hour Fitness.

Service Manager.question: How do you deal with an employee who doesn't perform?
Service Manager.overview: Your service manager will be responsible for overseeing a team of customer-facing employees, so they will have to deal with issues that arise from time to time. Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have helped to reduce our energy consumption by implementing energy-efficient lighting and other upgrades. I have also worked with our purchasing department to find vendors that offer discounts for bulk purchases.

Operations Manager.question: How would you fit in the team?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are the glue that holds your team together. They are responsible for ensuring that all the different departments and teams work together smoothly and efficiently. As such, you should be looking for a candidate who will be able to fit in with your team and understand the different personalities and work styles of each member.
expectations: Ability to work with different personalities
Ability to work well under pressure,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been good at working with people from different backgrounds and have always been able to find common ground with people who may have different opinions than me. I believe that it is important to listen to everyone's ideas and opinions before making a decision.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you made an improvement that benefited the company?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are responsible for ensuring that the company is running smoothly and efficiently. As such, you should be looking for an individual who has a track record of identifying and implementing improvements to the business.
expectations: Specific examples of improvements that were made
Details about how the improvement was made
Evidence of a positive impact on the company,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I once identified a process that was taking too long to complete and found a way to cut the time in half. I did this by working with the team to identify bottlenecks and then implementing a new process that allowed us to complete the work in half the time.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about your previous assignment.
Operations Manager.overview: The hiring team wants to understand what your candidate has done in the past and how it has prepared them for the role. The operations manager is responsible for overseeing the smooth flow of work within the organization and ensuring that each department is working at peak efficiency. As such, your candidate should have a strong understanding of how to manage a team and ensure that they are working efficiently.
expectations: Level of experience managing a team
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I previously worked as a project manager and oversaw the work of a team of five members. I was responsible for making sure that each member was working efficiently and that we were all working toward the same goal.

Operations Manager.question: How would you resolve a conflict between two very talented managers?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that your team members are able to work together effectively. In some instances, this may mean resolving conflicts between managers who have very different personalities. You should be looking for an individual who can handle these situations with tact and grace.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first make sure that both managers were aware of the conflict and then work with them to come up with a solution that would allow them to work together more effectively.

Operations Manager.question: How will you overcome organizational obstacles?
Operations Manager.overview: As operations manager, your candidate will be responsible for ensuring that the different teams in your organization work together like a well-oiled machine. However, there may be times when the team encounters obstacles that prevent them from functioning as effectively as they should. Your candidate should have a strategy for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring that the team is able to work together to achieve their goals.
expectations: Ability to work with different personalities
Knowledge of how to overcome organizational obstacles,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand what the obstacle is and why it is preventing us from achieving our goals. Then, I would work with the team to find a solution that works for everyone.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to give constructive feedback to your peers?
Operations Manager.overview: As operations manager, your candidate will need to be able to give constructive feedback to his or her peers. This question will allow you to understand how they approach giving feedback and how they handle the situation when they are on the receiving end of feedback.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I was able to give constructive feedback to my peers by first identifying the problem and then offering a solution. I made sure that my peers understood that I was not criticizing them but rather trying to help them improve their work.

Operations Manager.question: What was the most difficult/challenging manager you ever had and why?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for managing a team of individuals who will be responsible for helping your company achieve its goals. As such, you should be looking for an individual who has experience working with different personalities and can effectively manage a team.
expectations: Ability to work with different personalities
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: My most difficult manager was my last boss. He was very demanding and had a tendency to micromanage. I found that the best way to work with him was to make sure that I was always one step ahead of him and to always have a plan in place.

Operations Manager.question: How will you leverage your past experience in developing new revenue sources.
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for helping your organization identify new revenue streams and ensuring that they are implemented in a way that does not disrupt the organization's current operations. Your candidate should have a clear strategy for identifying new revenue sources and be able to explain how they will be implemented.
expectations: Ability to work with different departments
Ability to identify and implement new revenue sources,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first identify the areas of our business that are not currently generating revenue and then develop a plan for how we can start generating revenue from these areas. I would then present my plan to the executive team and get their buy-in before moving forward.

Operations Manager.question: How much time do you spend on the production floor?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers need to be able to work closely with the teams that they are supporting. As such, you should be looking for a candidate who is comfortable spending time on the production floor and interacting with the staff.
expectations: Level of time spent on the production floor
Ability to communicate effectively with production staff,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I spend at least a few hours a week on the production floor. I find that it is important to get out of my office and talk with my team members face-to-face.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a process you improved at your current position.
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are responsible for ensuring that the business runs smoothly. As such, they need to be able to identify and improve processes that may be holding up the company's ability to achieve its goals. Your candidate should have a clear example of a process that they improved in their current role.
expectations: Specific example of a process that was improved
Level of experience in improving processes
Clear understanding of how the process was improved,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I streamlined our hiring process by creating a checklist that all hiring managers needed to follow when interviewing candidates. This checklist ensured that all the necessary information was gathered and that we were able to make decisions quickly.

Operations Manager.question: What made you decide to apply for this position?
Operations Manager.overview: This question is a great way to get a sense of how your candidate feels about the position and the company. You should be looking for an individual who is excited about the opportunity to join your team and is eager to learn more about your organization.
expectations: Desire to learn more about the company,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been interested in working for your company for some time now and am excited to join your team.

Operations Manager.question: What is the most important leadership role you've ever held?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will need to be able to lead a team of individuals who are responsible for different aspects of the business. As such, you should be looking for an individual who has experience leading a team and can articulate how they have done so effectively.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: My most important leadership role was when I was a project manager for a large retail chain. I was responsible for managing the work of the team and ensuring that we met our deadlines. I was also responsible for ensuring that the team had everything they needed to complete their work.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a decision made by your manager.
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will likely be the liaison between different departments and may need to defend a decision made by one department to another. As such, you should be looking for an individual who can communicate effectively and diplomatically.
expectations: Ability to work with different personalities,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I once disagreed with my manager's decision to hire a new member of staff. I felt that the position was unnecessary and that we could complete our work without the new hire. However, my manager felt that the new hire would help us complete our work more efficiently. In the end, I was proven right and we were able to complete our work without the new hire.

Operations Manager.question: How will you handle the situation if an employee wants to file a worker's compensation claim if you believe the injury didn't occer at work.
Operations Manager.overview: As operations manager, your candidate will be responsible for ensuring that your employees are safe and healthy while they are working. In some instances, employees may want to file worker's compensation claims if they believe that their injuries were sustained at work. However, the operations manager may not agree with their assessment of the situation and need to make a decision about how to proceed.
expectations: Understanding of the company's worker's compensation policy
Ability to make a fair decision based on the facts of the case,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first talk to the employee and find out what happened. Then, I would talk to my supervisor and our human resources department to understand our company's worker's compensation policy. If I still believe that the injury wasn't sustained at work, I would explain my rationale for denying the claim.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you had to make a presentation.
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are often tasked with presenting to different groups of stakeholders. The candidate should be able to clearly communicate the information that they have gathered and be able to answer questions from the audience.
expectations: Ability to gather and present information effectively,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have made presentations to different teams within my organization on a regular basis. I find that the best way to make a presentation is to first understand the audience's needs and then present the information in a way that is most relevant to them.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you supported your team.
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are responsible for ensuring that the team is supported in their work. As such, they may need to help resolve issues that arise within the team or help the team members with their work. Your candidate should be able to provide a specific example of a time when they helped resolve a problem within the team.
expectations: Ability to empathize with team members
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have had experience supporting my team in a variety of ways. For example, I have helped my team members with their work by providing them with additional information or resources that they needed to complete their tasks. I have also helped my team members by listening to them and helping them resolve their problems.

Operations Manager.question: What would you do if an employee is angry?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for managing and motivating the team. As such, they will need to be able to handle different situations with grace and tact. You should be looking for an individual who can empathize with the employee's feelings and respond in a way that helps the employee feel supported.
expectations: Ability to respond to the situation in a way that helps the employee feel supported,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand why the employee is upset. Then, I would offer my support and help them work through their feelings.

Operations Manager.question: Are you willing to be on call 24/7?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are responsible for ensuring that the business runs smoothly and efficiently. As such, they may be called upon to help out in a crisis situation or to help resolve a problem that has arisen. You should be looking for an individual who is willing to be on call at all times and is able to resolve problems quickly.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been on call for the last three years and have never had to respond to an emergency. However, I am always prepared to do so if needed.

Operations Manager.question: How many employees have you coached to succeed and name one that has failed.
Operations Manager.overview: As operations manager, your candidate will be responsible for helping your team members grow and develop. You should be looking for an individual who is able to coach team members to succeed and has a track record of helping others reach their goals.
expectations: Level of experience coaching team members
Ability to recognize and address performance issues
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have coached three employees to succeed in their roles. One of them was a junior member of the team who was struggling with his work. I worked with him to find out what was causing him to struggle and helped him to overcome his obstacles.

Operations Manager.question: How do you handle difficult people?
Operations Manager.overview: As operations manager, your candidate will be working with a wide variety of people, including clients, vendors, and internal staff. Your candidate should be able to work with people from all walks of life and understand how to handle difficult situations.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I always try to approach difficult people with a positive attitude and a willingness to understand their perspective. I believe that by approaching people in this way, I can better understand their needs and work with them to resolve any issues.

Operations Manager.question: How do you handle your employees?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for managing a team of individuals and ensuring that they are all working towards the same goals. As such, you should be looking for a candidate who is able to handle employees with different personalities and work styles.
expectations: Ability to handle employees with different personalities
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I try to get to know each of my employees on a personal level and understand what motivates them. I also try to be as transparent as possible about the goals of the business and how each employee's work contributes to those goals.

Operations Manager.question: How would you handle an angry customer?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that your company's clients are satisfied with the services that they receive. As such, your candidate should be able to handle difficult situations with grace and tact.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the customer's needs and concerns. Then, I would work with my team to find a solution that would satisfy the customer and allow us to move forward.

Operations Manager.question: How will you handle situations when you don't see eye to eye with a coworker?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers need to be able to work with all kinds of different personalities. As such, you should be looking for a candidate who is able to handle conflicts in a professional manner and can work with others to resolve disagreements.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Ability to remain professional in the face of conflict
Ability to resolve conflicts with others,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand why my coworker feels the way they do and then try to find a solution that works for both of us.

Operations Manager.question: How would you penetrate a new market with your product?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for helping your company grow. As such, they will need to be able to identify new markets that your company can enter and develop strategies for penetrating those markets.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first look at the market and determine what needs it has that we can fulfill. Then, I would work with our sales team to develop a strategy for penetrating the market.

Operations Manager.question: How many pieces can your area move with X amount of employees, working X amount of hours - per day.
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations team will be responsible for moving a lot of pieces to ensure that your business is running smoothly. As such, you should be looking for an operations manager who can demonstrate a strong understanding of the number of pieces that can be moved with a certain number of employees and hours worked.
expectations: Strong understanding of how many pieces can be moved with a certain number of employees and hours worked
Ability to break down the problem into smaller parts
Ability to use data to support their response,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: Based on our current processes, we can move approximately 20 pieces per employee per day.

Operations Manager.question: How will you communicate with people who have dealt or are dealing with many of the ills of society?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that your organization is able to attract and retain top talent. As such, they will need to be able to communicate with people from different backgrounds and cultures. You should be looking for an individual who is able to communicate effectively with people from different backgrounds and cultures.
expectations: Ability to empathize with different types of people
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the reason why the person is dealing with these issues and then try to find out how I can help them. I would also try to understand what they are looking for in a job and then offer them a position that would allow them to grow as a professional.

Operations Manager.question: What kind of schedule can you handle?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are often required to work long hours and weekends to ensure that the team is able to meet deadlines. As such, you should be looking for an individual who is comfortable working under pressure and who can handle a heavy workload.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been able to handle a heavy workload and have never had any issues with working long hours or weekends. I am confident that I can continue to do so in this role.

Operations Manager.question: If you could get a "do over" what would you change in your professional career?
Operations Manager.overview: This question is designed to assess whether the candidate has a clear understanding of their professional strengths and weaknesses and whether they have a plan for improving their weaker areas.
expectations: A plan for addressing these weaknesses
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would have spent more time learning how to work with people who are not as strong as I am. I have always been a strong performer and have not had to work with many people who are not as strong as I am. However, in my new role, I will be working with people who are not as strong as I am and will need to learn how to work with them.

Operations Manager.question: What did you do to improve the process, not what your team did?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that the team is working at peak efficiency and will need to identify areas where the team can improve. As such, you should be looking for an individual who can take a step back and look at the big picture.
expectations: Ability to identify areas of improvement
Ability to think critically and solve problems,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first look at our process and identify areas where we can improve. Then, I would work with the team to come up with solutions that would allow us to streamline our work and complete tasks more quickly.

Operations Manager.question: What have you done to go out of your way for a customer?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that your company's customers are satisfied with the services that they receive. As such, your candidate should have a strong sense of customer service and be willing to go out of their way to ensure that your customers are happy.
expectations: Ability to empathize with customer needs,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had a customer who was having trouble with a product that I had sold her. I went out of my way to make sure she was satisfied and even offered her a refund.

Operations Manager.question: Can you tell me about yourself?
Operations Manager.overview: This is a general question that gives the candidate a chance to tell you about their background and how they ended up in their current role. You should be looking for an individual who has a strong work ethic and is able to communicate effectively.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been passionate about helping others succeed. I started out as a teacher and then moved into a role where I was able to help people grow their careers. I have been working in operations for the past five years and have found that I really enjoy helping teams to work together more efficiently.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a difficult situation you faced and how did you handle it?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that your team is able to complete their work on time and with the highest level of quality. As such, they will face a variety of challenges that may include dealing with difficult clients, vendors, or employees. You should be looking for an individual who can handle these situations with poise and grace.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I had a situation where one of my team members was not performing up to standard. I sat down with him and explained that he needed to improve his performance or he would be let go. He took my feedback and worked hard to improve his performance.

Operations Manager.question: What makes you interested in security?
Operations Manager.overview: Your candidate's answer to this question will give you an idea of what drives them to do their job. You should be looking for a candidate who has a passion for the work they do and is excited to share their knowledge with others.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have always been interested in security and have been following the industry for years. I am thrilled to have the opportunity to work in this field and help organizations protect their most valuable assets.

Operations Manager.question: How do you motivate your team?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers need to be able to motivate their team to perform at their best. Your candidate should be able to explain how they would motivate their team to perform at peak levels.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first identify the strengths of each member of my team and then use these strengths to motivate them. For example, if one of my team members is a strong communicator, I would assign them to work on a project that requires a lot of interaction with other departments.

Operations Manager.question: How would you handle an employee who refuses to follow a directive?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers need to be able to work with different types of personalities and ensure that all staff members are working together to achieve the same goals. As such, you should be looking for an applicant who can work with different types of people and is able to resolve conflicts in a professional manner.
expectations: Ability to resolve conflicts in a professional manner
Ability to empathize with different types of people,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand why the employee is refusing to follow the directive. Then, I would explain why the directive is important and how it will help the organization achieve its goals.

Operations Manager.question: What is an example of a time when you had to handle a client escalation?
Operations Manager.overview: As operations manager, your candidate will be responsible for ensuring that clients are satisfied with the work that your organization produces. In some instances, clients may feel that they are not getting the level of service they expect and may escalate their concerns to your operations director. Your candidate should be able to handle these situations with tact and grace.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: The last time I had to handle a client escalation was when a client felt that we were not meeting their expectations in terms of turnaround time. I was able to schedule a meeting with them and explain our process for handling requests and why we were behind schedule. I was able to get them to understand our process and they were satisfied with our response.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time when you mentored someone (or a team) that was struggling?
Operations Manager.overview: As an operations manager, your candidate will be responsible for ensuring that each member of his or her team is performing at a high level. This may mean that your candidate will need to step in and help members of his or her team who are struggling to meet deadlines or who are having trouble with a particular task. You should be looking for an individual who can identify the root cause of the problem and help the employee overcome it.
expectations: Ability to identify the root cause of a problem
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I once had an employee who was struggling to meet deadlines. I sat down with him and asked him what was going on. He told me that he was having trouble understanding the requirements for the project and asked if I could help him. I worked with him to understand the project's requirements and then helped him develop a strategy for completing his work on time.

Operations Manager.question: Which Core Value do you resonate with?
Operations Manager.overview: The Core Values are the foundation of your company's culture. As such, you should be looking for an individual who can demonstrate that they are aligned with the values that your company holds dear.
expectations: Ability to articulate a strong connection with the Core Values
Ability to communicate how the Core Values have helped them in their career,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I resonate with the Core Value of "Be a team player." I have always been a team player and enjoy working with others to achieve common goals.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time you mentored someone and how did it go?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are often responsible for training new hires and helping them to become productive members of the team. As such, you should be looking for an individual who is able to communicate effectively and who can work well with others.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have mentored several new hires in my previous roles. I find that the best way to get them up to speed is to break down the work into smaller tasks and then have them complete the work while I observe.

Operations Manager.question: How is your past experience relevant to OYO operations profile?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are responsible for ensuring that the different departments within your organization work together to produce results. As such, your candidate's past experience should be relevant to the operations role. You should be looking for an individual who has experience working in a similar role or in a role that required them to manage a team of individuals.
expectations: Ability to explain how past experience is relevant
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: My previous experience as a project manager has given me the opportunity to work with different departments and understand how they function. I am confident that I can use this experience to help OYO's operations team work together more effectively.

Operations Manager.question: What is your experience in supervising people?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are responsible for overseeing the work of different teams and ensuring that they are able to complete their work on time. As such, you should be looking for an individual who has experience in supervising others and can manage them effectively.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been a supervisor for the last five years and have worked with a team of twenty people. I have always strived to create a positive work environment where people feel supported and are able to complete their work on time.

Operations Manager.question: How often do you clean the public restrooms on a typical 8 hour shift?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for ensuring that the different areas of your business are clean and well-maintained. This includes public restrooms, which may be used by a large number of people on a daily basis. You should be looking for an individual who is committed to ensuring that the restrooms are clean and well-maintained.
expectations: Ability to work with janitorial staff
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I clean the restrooms on a daily basis. I have found that this is the best way to ensure that they are well-maintained and clean.

Operations Manager.question: What is the most creative thing you've done?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers need to be creative in order to find new ways to improve their processes and make their teams more efficient. Your candidate should be able to tell you about a time when they were able to use creativity to solve a problem or come up with a new way of doing things.
expectations: Ability to think outside the box
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I once needed to come up with a way to improve the efficiency of our shipping process. I noticed that we were spending a lot of time trying to find the right box for each order. So, I came up with a system that would allow us to store all of our boxes in one place and label them with the appropriate order number. This saved us a lot of time and money.

Operations Manager.question: What was the last decision you made with little information available and what was the result?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers are often faced with situations where they need to make decisions with limited information. As such, you should be looking for an individual who can make decisions based on the information available and who can provide a rationale for their decision.
expectations: Ability to make decisions with limited information
Ability to provide a rationale for the decision,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I was working on a project that required me to create a new process for our team. I had limited information about the process that was currently in place, but I was able to use the information that I did have to create a new process that was more efficient and streamlined.

Operations Manager.question: How would you deal with a problematic colleague?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations director will need to work with a wide range of individuals, including your colleagues and other departments. As such, you should be looking for an individual who is able to work with others in a positive manner.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand why the colleague is behaving in a certain way. Then, I would try to find out if there is anything that I can do to help them improve their performance.

Operations Manager.question: How would you handle a difficult situation?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be the one who helps your team and business run smoothly. As such, there may be times when the team encounters a problem that requires a solution. Your candidate should have a strong approach to problem-solving and be able to handle difficult situations with grace.
expectations: Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first try to understand the problem from all angles and then come up with a solution that makes sense for everyone involved.

Operations Manager.question: Give us an example of where you took a decision without considering the impact on others.
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for making decisions that will impact the entire organization. As such, you should be looking for an individual who can make decisions that are in the best interest of the company without taking into account how their decisions might impact other teams.
expectations: Ability to make decisions that are in the best interest of the company
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I was working on a project that required me to work with a team in another country. I had to decide whether we should use a translation service or have our team members learn the language. I decided to have our team members learn the language so they could communicate directly with our partners.

Operations Manager.question: What's the hardest thing you've ever done?
Operations Manager.overview: The hiring team is looking for a candidate that can handle the pressures of the job and will be able to keep the business on track. As such, you should be looking for an answer that shows that your candidate has experience with high-pressure situations and can handle them in a positive manner.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Ability to think clearly and logically,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I have been in situations where I have had to work with a team member who was not performing up to expectations. This was a difficult situation because I needed to find a way to motivate the individual without damaging our working relationship.

Operations Manager.question: How do you think you can positively impact the day sort?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager should be able to identify ways to improve the efficiency of your business. In this question, you are looking for a candidate who can think critically about the day sort process and identify ways to make it more efficient.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would first look at the current process and identify any areas where we might be able to improve efficiency. Then, I would look at how we can streamline our processes and make them more efficient.

Operations Manager.question: If a customer is yelling at you what would be your reaction?
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations director will be the face of your company to many of your customers. As such, it is important that they are able to handle stressful situations with grace and poise.
expectations: Ability to remain calm under pressure
Ability to empathize with the customer
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I would listen to what the customer has to say and then explain why we are unable to meet their request. I would also make sure that they understand that I am there to help them and that we will do everything we can to resolve the issue.

Operations Manager.question: How will your degree help you in this position?
Operations Manager.overview: Operations managers need to be able to understand how different business departments work together to produce results. As such, your candidate will need to have a strong understanding of the different functions that are performed in your organization.
expectations: Strong understanding of the different business functions
Ability to communicate effectively with different departments,
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: My degree in business administration has given me a strong understanding of the different functions that are performed in an organization. I have also taken several courses on operations management, which has given me a deeper understanding of how different departments work together to produce results.

Operations Manager.question: Describe yourself and your capabilities to someone who cannot see you.
Operations Manager.overview: This is a question that allows you to gauge your candidate's ability to communicate effectively. It is important that your operations manager can clearly and concisely describe their strengths and weaknesses to a potential employer.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I am a hard-working individual who is always looking for ways to improve my skills and the processes I manage. I am also a team player who is willing to go above and beyond to help my colleagues succeed.

Operations Manager.question: Tell me about a time you had to innovate.
Operations Manager.overview: Your operations manager will be responsible for helping your business stay ahead of the curve. As such, you should be looking for an individual who can think outside the box to find new ways to improve efficiency and productivity.
Operations Manager.sampleAnswer: I once worked with a team that was tasked with developing a new product. We had a limited amount of time to develop the product and needed to find ways to reduce the time it took to complete each step in the process.
